docs.title: Overview and terminology
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Purpose: run Codex CLI or Claude Code, normally in one Kata VM per worker.
  • Flow: prepare host → select credentials → prepare images/proxies → launch from your project.
  • Next: Installation, or the quick start on a prepared host.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Term Meaning Execution host Linux/KVM environment running services, BuildKit and proxies; WSL/VM hosts must meet the same requirements Operator Trusted CLI user; node socket and BuildKit access grant root-equivalent host control Node Root management service that verifies and manages containerd, VMs, networking and resources Worker A task environment, normally with its own Kata VM; managed by name or ID Agent Codex CLI or Claude Code running inside the worker Worker image OCI image containing agents, tools and the entrypoint; built with BuildKit Auth Proxy Holds real credentials and mediates AI requests authorized with worker placeholders Egress proxy Mediates Git, npm, pip and other general traffic; holds no real credentials Job A background command inside an existing worker, not a separate VM

docs.title: Two kinds of profiles
docs.text:
Profile Purpose Selection Authentication Store API/OAuth credentials separately from host CLI logins Global auth_profile or --auth-profile Resources Select CPU, memory and PID limits --profile-size standard, small, compact, etc.
  • Selecting credentials does not change resource limits.
  • Selecting resources does not change authentication or the provider account.

docs.title: Directories
docs.text: Location Contents and use Product source checkout Development and custom builds; not required to install or initialize a release Working project Repository the agent edits; launch oaiso codex or oaiso claude here Guest /workspace Shared project; writable by default, with changes reflected on the host ~/.config/codex-dock/config.toml Host user settings: credential selection, proxies and launch defaults Project oaiso.toml Optional project settings; excludes credentials and extra host mounts Independent profile storage Owner-only 0700 directories and 0600 files; outside all worker shares

docs.title: Stop and resume
docs.text:
Action Meaning Foreground agent exit Remove the worker by default; retain it with --keep stop Stop the VM, retain the worker and revoke its placeholder start Rerun the same worker's program; no suspended memory state is resumed rm Reclaim owned networks and worktrees; preserve required results first
  • Shared host files remain after worker removal, except for managed worktrees that are reclaimed.
  • Worker start is separate from the agent's conversation-resume options.
  • Details: file sharing and operations (Japanese).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • User settings live in ~/.config/codex-dock/config.toml.
  • Use oaiso --config PATH COMMAND to select another file.
  • make install-config installs the example without overwriting an existing file.

docs.title: Project settings
docs.text:
• oaiso.toml is optional. Workers can start without it using user settings and built-in defaults.
  • Create it to customize a project or share settings with a team. The filename is lowercase.
  • Without a project file, project init and project check are unnecessary.
  • Run oaiso project init at the repository root to create oaiso.toml, and oaiso project check to validate it. Commit it to share settings.
  • init, run, codex, and build read the file from the current directory; run --project DIR reads DIR/oaiso.toml.
  • Parent directories are not searched.
oaiso project init
oaiso project check
git add oaiso.toml

Example output

$ oaiso project init
/home/user/my-project/oaiso.toml
$ oaiso project check
Project config: /home/user/my-project/oaiso.toml
build.template = plain
run.image = codex-dock:latest
  • Paths vary. project check validates settings without starting a VM or connecting to an AI provider.
  • An old codex-dock.toml blocks loading until renamed (Japanese); its restrictions are never silently discarded.

You can also change the agent started by a plain oaiso run from the CLI. oaiso default shows the effective value and where it came from.

oaiso default codex          # global config
oaiso default claude --local # this project only
oaiso default shell          # restore the authenticated shell
  • --local creates or updates oaiso.toml in this directory.
  • Commit the file to share it.
  • An explicit --agent, --exec, IMAGE COMMAND, or -- COMMAND overrides the default.
  • oaiso codex always starts Codex.
[run]
image = "codex-dock:latest"
approval_mode = "suggest"

[build]
template = "plain"

docs.title: Host-managed agent policies
docs.text:
Codex- and Claude-specific defaults can live outside repositories in owner-private ~/.config/codex-dock/agent-policies/config.toml:

[run]
agent_policy = "approve-for-me"

Use oaiso run --agent-policy NAME for one run or global --agent-policy-file PATH for another store. See host-managed agent policies for creation, auditing, and the complete allowlist. Repository oaiso.toml cannot set host-only fields.

  • For a custom image, commit a project Dockerfile and use matching run.image and build.tag values.
  • The project root is the build context.
  • A Dockerfile using FROM codex-dock:latest automatically builds the bundled base image on a fresh clone.
[run]
image = "my-project:dev"
model = "your-model"

[build]
dockerfile = "Dockerfile.codex-dock"
tag = "my-project:dev"
  • packages.dock is also loaded automatically.
  • Pin dependency versions in the project Dockerfile or package list when repeatability matters.
  • Project templates must be built-in or unchanged copies of built-in templates; commit a Dockerfile instead of depending on a locally edited template.

docs.title: Allowed project keys
docs.text: Category Keys or values Image and template run.image, run.template Agent and model run.agent (shell, codex, claude), run.model Approval run.approval_mode (suggest, auto-edit) Resource budget run.profile_size (built-in standard, small, compact) File restrictions run.read_only, run.read_only_rootfs, run.no_git_metadata, run.deny_read, run.deny_write Network restrictions run.no_internet, run.egress_allow_domains, run.policy_preset Lifecycle run.max_lifetime, run.idle_timeout, run.retention Startup run.start_hooks, run.readiness, run.readiness_timeout Watchers run.watch_polling Build build.dockerfile, build.template, build.tag Validation Contract Project read_only / no_internet Only true; cannot relax host restrictions run.image / build.tag Must match Credentials, proxy, runtime, token lifetime, extra host mounts Global configuration or explicit flags only Unknown keys Fail validation

docs.title: Startup syntax and restriction merging
docs.text:
Location start_hooks readiness Global config.toml Shell strings, e.g. ["npm ci"] Shell string, e.g. "test -d node_modules" Project oaiso.toml Array of argv arrays, e.g. [["npm", "ci"]] Argv array, e.g. ["test", "-d", "node_modules"]
  • Project hooks run inside the guest; review cloned settings and shared paths before init or run.
  • File denials append to host restrictions.
  • Without explicit CLI overrides, project lifetime/idle values can only select a shorter positive limit; a positive project retention value is applied.

  • Enforcement: lifecycle and reproducibility.

  • init and run build missing images.

  • For an existing project image, automatic rebuilds check the Dockerfile timestamp; run oaiso build after changing copied files or dependencies alone.

  • Products can use PrepareProject in the Go API to validate the same project file and build missing images.

  • The Go API does not load global settings; the product must apply host settings and authorization.

  • It copies egress_allow_domains into LaunchRequest.EgressAllowDomains.

  • Normal precedence: explicit CLI flags > project config > global config > built-in defaults.

  • Project read_only and no_internet only add restrictions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
default_image = "codex-dock:latest"
proxy_image = "codex-dock-proxy:latest"

[run]
runtime = "kata"
user = "current"
approval_mode = "suggest"
token_ttl = 3600

[proxy]
container_url = "http://codex-auth-proxy:18080"
admin_url = "http://127.0.0.1:18081"
forward_allow_domains = ["github.com", "registry.npmjs.org"]
forward_allow_ports = [80, 443]
  • Use the credential sources for API keys and OAuth files.
  • Explicit flags override config.
  • This example uses legacy host authentication. For profiles, put auth_profile before the first table and merge admin_secret_file into the existing [proxy] table; follow profile selection.
  • Command-specific settings override global defaults.
  • Only the documented environment overrides should be relied on; arbitrary CODEX_DOCK_* names are not supported.

docs.title: Global settings
docs.text: Key Default Purpose auth_profile Unselected Independent profile; --auth-profile auth_profile_dir ~/.config/codex-dock/profiles Profile storage root; --auth-profile-dir default_image codex-dock:latest Worker OCI image proxy_image codex-dock-proxy:latest Image for both proxy roles default_template Unset Template for run/build default_token_ttl 3600 Token lifetime in seconds auto_build true Rebuild changed on-disk templates default_shell_type Detect from host shell bash/zsh verbose, debug false CLI logging

docs.title: auto_build
docs.text:
• Compare the template Dockerfile mtime to the image creation timestamp.
  • Only on-disk templates are checked.
  • Purely embedded templates have no file to compare.
  • Missing images are built regardless of this setting.

docs.title: default_shell_type
docs.text:
• Without a setting, host $SHELL selects zsh when its basename is zsh, otherwise bash.
  • Debug --shell defaults to bash unless explicitly overridden.

docs.title: Run settings
docs.text:
Under [run]:

Key Default or inherited value Flag runtime kata --runtime kata_runtime io.containerd.kata.v2 --kata-runtime profile_size standard --profile-size image default_image --image template default_template --template agent shell --agent token_ttl default_token_ttl --token-ttl approval_mode suggest --approval-mode user current --user shell_type default_shell_type --shell-type auto_build auto_build Config only mounts Empty --mount watch_polling false --watch-polling model Unset --model read_only false --read-only read_only_rootfs false --read-only-rootfs agent_state_size auto (512MiB) --agent-state-size; state storage, unreleased (main) no_git_metadata false --no-git-metadata no_internet false --no-internet egress_allow_domains Empty --egress-allow-domain policy_preset Unset --policy-preset deny_read / deny_write Empty --deny-read / --deny-write max_lifetime / idle_timeout / retention "0s" Matching hyphenated flags; "30m", "2h"; requires reap protect_main false v0.0.4. --protect-main; protect the primary process from idle collection max_requests / max_concurrent 0 v0.0.4. --max-requests / --max-concurrent max_transfer_bytes / max_observed_tokens 0 v0.0.4. --max-transfer-bytes / --max-observed-tokens. Limits environment_lock Unset --environment-lock image_id Unset --image-id start_hooks Empty --start-hook readiness Unset --readiness readiness_timeout "0s" (effective 60s) --readiness-timeout ssh_proxy / jvm_proxy false --ssh-proxy / --jvm-proxy ca_bundle Unset --ca-bundle; additional worker PEM roots
  • These are trusted global settings; project keys are limited to the allowlist.
  • Durations use Go syntax, such as 24h; 1d is not supported.

Explicit --image wins over template image selection. runtime = "runc" is an explicit compatibility mode on the same containerd node, without VM isolation.

docs.title: run.mounts
docs.text:
[run]
mounts = ["/home/user/datasets:/data:ro", "./cache:/cache:rw"]
  • Relative host paths resolve from the command's working directory.
  • An explicit --mount replaces the config array.

  • --read-only controls the workspace; extra mounts have their own permissions.

  • The legacy network_name setting is not used by current network commands, which use dock-net-proxy.

  • Select a proxy network with proxy run --network.

docs.title: Build settings
docs.text:
• Under [build], template inherits default_template and tag sets the output image name.
  • Without an explicit tag, templates use their own tag; a plain build uses codex-dock:latest.
  • See build.

docs.title: Proxy settings
docs.text:
• Trusted global auth_profile selects an independent profile; auth_profile_dir overrides its storage root (default ~/.config/codex-dock/profiles).
  • Corresponding flags are --auth-profile / --auth-profile-dir.
  • An explicit selection disables host credential fallback.
  • These keys are not allowed in project configuration.

  • See creation and startup.

  • Admin-secret files must be owner-only 0600 regular files.

  • Supplying both a file and a value, including configured/environment values, fails.
  • Explicit run secret flags override configuration.
  • Keep these files and profile storage outside worker shares.
  • Drain workers and explicitly recreate the proxy when changing admin authority.

Under [proxy]:

Key Default Used by max_connections / max_connections_per_source 0 v0.0.4. proxy run --max-connections / --max-connections-per-source network_bytes_per_second 0 v0.0.4. --network-bytes-per-second. Scope and behavior container_url http://codex-auth-proxy:18080 run --proxy-container-url admin_url http://127.0.0.1:18081 run --proxy-admin-url, worker management admin_secret Unset Admin client; also supply the server secret with proxy run --admin-secret admin_secret_file Unset Owner-only 0600 file; proxy run --admin-secret-file, run --proxy-admin-secret-file, init, worker management and TUI forward_default_deny true --forward-default-deny; deny general egress when both domain and CIDR grants are empty forward_allow_domains, forward_deny_domains Empty --forward-allow-domain, --forward-deny-domain forward_allow_cidrs, forward_deny_cidrs Empty --forward-allow-cidr, --forward-deny-cidr forward_allow_ports, forward_deny_ports Empty --forward-allow-port, --forward-deny-port allowed_models Empty (unrestricted) proxy run --allow-model; exact upstream IDs; constrained tokens reject WebSocket upstream_proxy Unset proxy run --upstream-proxy; explicit HTTP(S) upstream proxy ca_bundle Unset proxy run --ca-bundle; additional proxy PEM roots

  • run.ca_bundle configures the worker; proxy.ca_bundle configures the proxy. BuildKit registry CA trust is configured separately by the administrator.

  • The data URL is used by workers; the admin URL is used by the host CLI.

  • General egress uses run --http-proxy-url.

  • The legacy firewall.proxy_container_url key is still read, but use [proxy] for new config.

  • On upgrade, configure host domain/CIDR grants before creating new workers, or explicitly opt into the previous behavior with forward_default_deny = false.

  • Existing proxies, workers and CONNECT tunnels are not changed automatically.

  • Missing explicitly selected configuration files, parse errors and invalid default-deny values fail CLI startup.

  • Rules apply only to general egress.

  • Denials win and all nonempty allowlists must match.
  • forward_default_deny defaults to true, denying empty destination allowlists.
  • Explicitly set false (CLI --forward-default-deny=false) to retain public-destination access without grants.
  • A port alone is not a destination grant.
  • Bare example.com includes subdomains; =example.com matches that name exactly, for both allow and deny rules.
  • Private address blocking cannot be overridden by an allowlist.
  • Policy denials return HTTP 403 for HTTP requests and CONNECT.
  • Domain/port checks run before DNS; resolved addresses are checked before TCP connection.
  • Direct worker traffic remains isolated at the network layer.
  • See the verification record for automated checks and successful real Kata acceptance results.
  • Recreate the proxy to apply changes.
  • See policy rules (Japanese).

docs.title: Environment overrides
docs.text:
Variable Purpose CODEX_DOCK_RUNTIME Override run.runtime CODEX_DOCK_KATA_RUNTIME Override run.kata_runtime CODEX_DOCK_PROXY_ADMIN_SECRET Admin client secret CODEX_DOCK_KATA_NODE_SOCKET Absolute node socket path CODEX_DOCK_STATE_DIR Private absolute path for cleanup/retry records XDG_STATE_HOME State root when no dedicated state directory is set BUILDKIT_HOST Builder address; default unix:///run/codex-dock-buildkit/buildkitd.sock HTTP/HTTPS/NO/ALL proxy variables, upper/lowercase BuildKit build args CODEX_PROXY_CERT CA file passed as BuildKit proxy_ca secret OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Host proxy credentials CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN Host auth proxy subscription access token from claude setup-token CODEX_DOCK_CODEX_VERSION / CODEX_DOCK_CLAUDE_VERSION Exact agent CLI version override for builds

Runtime overrides take precedence over config, below explicit flags. DOCKER_HOST and Docker contexts are not used.

  • Claude Code accepts host CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for subscription authentication.
  • Build overrides include CODEX_DOCK_CLAUDE_VERSION.
  • See Claude Code for source precedence and upgrade steps.

docs.title: Host service configuration
docs.text:
• Paths under /etc/codex-dock/ below describe manual installation; automatic setup uses managed configuration under /opt/codex-dock/releases/.

  • Check actual arguments with systemctl cat codex-dock-node codex-dock-containerd codex-dock-buildkit.

  • Host services are configured separately from user settings: node serve --help, /etc/codex-dock/containerd.toml, kata.toml, kata-assets.json and buildkit.toml.

  • [kata].node_socket configures the verification client.
  • If using a custom path, set CODEX_DOCK_KATA_NODE_SOCKET to the same value for the engine client.
  • See host setup (Japanese).

docs.title: Credential File Locations
docs.text:
Path Contents ~/.config/codex-dock/apikey Saved OpenAI API key ~/.codex/auth.json Codex login ~/.config/codex-dock/anthropic-apikey Saved Anthropic API key ~/.claude/.credentials.json Claude Code login
  • Do not include their contents in logs or images.

  • See auth proxy.

  • Host [proxy].allowed_models optionally allows exact upstream model IDs.

  • Empty preserves legacy behavior; enabled policies deny unsupported AI routes and WebSockets.
  • Explicit proxy run --allow-model flags take precedence.
  • Recreate the proxy and check supported routes.

docs.title: Operator resource profiles
docs.text:
• Additional FD and block I/O profile fields: v0.0.4. Existing built-in profiles retain their defaults.

  • run.profile_size selects a built-in or node-registered name.

  • The root node operator registers additional budgets through node serve --resource-profiles /etc/codex-dock/resource-profiles.json, independently of user TOML.

  • See bounds, guest assets and immutable reservations.

  • Generate registration JSON with oaiso profile define compact-256 --pids-limit 256; query effective values with oaiso profile --node --json.

  • PID limits apply to both host and guest; generating JSON alone does not register it on the node.

  • Generate registration JSON with oaiso profile define compact-256 --pids-limit 256 and inspect active PID ceilings with oaiso profile --node --json.

  • Limits apply on both host and guest.

  • proxy.credential_routes: v0.0.4. Absolute broker configuration file path; trusted host configuration only.

docs.title: Case-scoped credentials and run identity
docs.text:
English | 日本語

  • A host product serving multiple users or cases can run a separate auth proxy for each case.
  • Real credentials stay in the product store and host proxy; worker VMs receive only short-lived tokens.
  • The existing CLI proxy remains available.
Component Status 0600 FileStore, independent profiles and auth-proxy integration Implemented Dedicated login Kata, login flow and API connection checks Development version; live accounts need separate verification Optional encryption and key backends Implemented in v0.0.3: passphrase/existing Secret Service, migration and lock Real credentials in work VMs Never provided; short-lived tokens only

docs.title: Store contract
docs.text:
Interface: pkg/cxd/credentialstore.Store.

Operation or result Durable-store contract Load(ctx, caseID) Return current credentials, Version and ConnectionVersion SaveRefresh(ctx, caseID, expectedVersion, provider, next) Atomically compare the expected version and persist the OAuth refresh Successful save Return a new Version only after durable commit Login replacement, disconnect or competing refresh Return credentialstore.ErrConflict or ErrNotFound Logs Never log credential arguments

docs.title: Keep the two versions separate
docs.text:
Version Normal OAuth refresh Connection replacement Version Change after each update Change ConnectionVersion Preserve Change
  • The product owns DB encryption, user authorization and case-to-run mapping.

docs.title: Expose one case per socket
docs.text: Item Requirement API credentialstore.Serve(ctx, socketPath, caseID, store) Scope One case over a host Unix socket Case separation Separate socket per case Parent directory Owned by the process user, mode 0700 Socket Mode 0600

docs.title: Startup and execution
docs.text:
1. Allocate a unique proxy name, host admin port, and admin secret of at least 32 characters per case.

  2. Call cxd.EnsureCaseProxy(ctx, cxd.CaseProxyOptions{NodeSocket: nodeSocket, Name: "cxd-user-a", CaseID: "user-a", StoreSocket: socketPath, AdminPort: 18181, AdminSecret: secret}).

    • Build a matching codex-dock-proxy:latest image first.
    • Only the case proxy receives the credential socket mount; the VM does not.

  3. Pass the returned AdminURL and ContainerURL, plus the secret, to cxd.Open in Options.

    • Set LaunchRequest.Identity to identity.Identity{CaseID: "user-a", RunID: "run-1", ConnectionVersion: "v1", Provider: "openai"}.
    • Include case, run, attempt, and connection generation in RequestID; keep it unchanged on retries of that attempt.

  4. On cancellation, call client.RevokeRun(ctx, id) to stop new requests and active streams, then Stop and Remove the worker.

    • On disconnection, call client.RevokeCase(ctx), remove all workers, stop new launches for that case, and call cxd.RemoveCaseProxy(ctx, nodeSocket, proxy.Name, caseID).
    • Removal rejects a proxy referenced by a retained worker.

docs.title: Case separation and restart
docs.text:
• Use separate proxies, admin secrets, credential sockets, and admin ports for case A and case B.
  • EnsureCaseProxy verifies an existing container's case digest, image, socket, and admin port.
  • After restart, the proxy reloads credentials from the store.
  • A changed credential or connection version revokes old issuance; a failed OAuth save revokes the case.

docs.title: Provider, model and egress authorization
docs.text:
• Identity.Provider is openai or anthropic and restricts the proxy to that provider's API routes.
  • CaseProxyOptions.AllowedModels optionally restricts authenticated AI requests to exact upstream model IDs, checking their JSON body before upstream I/O or credential injection.
  • Empty preserves unrestricted forwarding.
  • See additional controls for supported routes and limitations.
  • Per-worker general egress allowlists are described in network policy; changes require a new worker.

docs.title: Host credential separation
docs.text:
• Case proxies are opt-in.
  • The existing CLI flow using host HOME credentials is unchanged.
  • A case proxy does not read HOME credentials or local OAuth state.
  • Keep its admin port on loopback and never pass the admin secret to a worker or project configuration.

docs.title: Recovery after a save failure
docs.text:
• OAuth save failures revoke new requests and active stream leases.
  • Storage recovery alone may not restore a refresh token already rotated upstream.
  • The product must reconcile credentials/connection generation, including re-login if needed, and must not silently reauthorize old runs.
  • Restarting the proxy alone does not guarantee credential recovery.

docs.title: Claude subscription credentials
docs.text:
• For official Claude Code subscriptions, AnthropicOAuth accepts an access-only setup-token record without RefreshToken.
  • Expiry then requires host-side credential replacement and reconnection.
  • A login record with a refresh token and known expiry is refreshed and saved with CAS before use.
  • See Claude Code.

docs.title: Initial implementation: 0600 files
docs.text:
• credentialstore.NewFileStore(directory) implements the same Store contract as a encrypted store, using plaintext files.
  • Its directory must be owned by the process user with mode 0700; each <profile>.json and lock file uses 0600.
  • It rejects unsafe permissions, symlinks, hardlinks and invalid names, without host CLI or authentication-environment fallback.

docs.title: Creation and refresh persistence
docs.text:
• Create(ctx, name, credentials) generates new credential and connection versions and never overwrites an existing profile.
  • Load and SaveRefresh use a cross-process lock.
  • Refresh compares the expected version before persisting through a temporary file, fsync and atomic rename.
  • Refresh cannot change another provider or the connection generation.
  • Ambiguous persistence failures, including a directory-fsync failure after rename, follow the existing proxy contract that revokes affected runs.

docs.title: Storage and encryption scope
docs.text:
• This backend does not encrypt secrets.
  • In WSL, use a private Linux-side directory; shared folders and backups need separate protection.
  • FileStore can also serve a case-scoped Unix socket mounted only into its auth proxy as described above.

docs.title: CLI integration
docs.text:
• The CLI's independent profiles use FileStore through auth profile set/import/show/list and explicit --auth-profile.
  • Selection disables host credential fallback.
  • Each profile has a separate directory; only the selected directory is mounted read-write into its auth proxy.
  • OAuth refresh persists there and proxy restarts reload it.
  • Retained workers record the profile and connection generation, rejecting restart under another login.

  • A encrypted store replaces the Store implementation while preserving its conformance tests; neither the vault nor automatic migration is implemented.

  • The CLI rejects overlaps between profile storage and workspace, clone or extra mounts.

  • Embedding API callers must also keep Store data and admin authority outside worker shares.
  • Creation/import is create-only; re-login requires explicitly stopping/removing old workers and recreating the proxy.

docs.title: Independent credential management: WSL, VMs and headless systems
docs.text:
• Storage, encryption, unlocking and migration: local credential store specification.

  • This section specifies future product-vault requirements.

  • Optional encryption, key backends and dedicated login are implemented in v0.0.3. Live accounts and WSL deployment acceptance remain separate checks.
  • The initial FileStore, existing product API-key files and local OAuth rotation state are permission-restricted plaintext.
  • External Store encryption belongs to the embedding product.

docs.title: Separate control environments from work VMs
docs.text:
• The trusted control environment owns the Controller, Vault and auth proxy.
  • Its design targets include physical Linux, WSL 2 and Linux VMs.
  • The rule against real credentials in work VMs concerns workers running arbitrary code; it does not prohibit running the trusted control environment inside a VM.
flowchart LR
  user[User / browser] --> control
  subgraph control["Trusted control environment: Linux / WSL 2 / VM"]
    keys[Key backend] --> vault[Product encrypted vault]
    vault --> store[CredentialStore]
    store --> proxy[Auth Proxy]
  end
  worker[Untrusted work Kata] -->|Placeholder only| proxy
  proxy --> provider[Provider]
  • Use product-specific profiles and key namespaces without automatically importing host CLI logins, Windows user credentials or inherited authentication variables.
  • Workers must not receive the vault, unlock keys, credential sockets or control-environment HOME.
  • Windows administrators, the Windows user owning the WSL distribution, hypervisor administrators and control-environment root remain trusted.
  • Windows processes under that user can access WSL Linux files.
  • At-rest encryption does not protect an unlocked process from a malicious same-UID process or memory access by its host.

docs.title: Key storage and unlocking
docs.text:
• Separate the encrypted file format from the key backend.
  • Use a random data key with AEAD and authenticate the profile, provider and schema as associated metadata.
  • Protect that key with the chosen backend; do not implement automatic unlocking through a plaintext key beside the ciphertext.
Control environment Planned unlock path Requirement Linux desktop Available Secret Service or explicit passphrase Check the backend, user session and lock state WSL 2 Explicit passphrase as a standard path; optional available Secret Service No mandatory Windows credential sharing, systemd, GUI or D-Bus Linux VM, SSH or headless Explicit passphrase; unattended unlock only through an explicitly configured protected channel No mandatory TPM, vTPM or desktop keyring Windows key protection integration Potential optional backend Validate user-scoped DPAPI, narrow helper authorization and migration before providing it; not required initially
  • Secret Service uses a user D-Bus session and can require unlocking or prompting.
  • A running systemd does not establish keyring availability; see WSL systemd documentation.

  • DPAPI usually depends on the user and machine, so cloned or reinstalled environments must not assume the same protected key remains usable.

  • Read passphrases through a hidden TTY or explicit dedicated input FD, never argv, environment variables or ordinary logs.

  • Use age scrypt to protect new identity bundles and bound file-supplied KDF work. Argon2id remains only in the read-only legacy decoder.
  • Measure memory/time budgets on small VMs and enforce upper bounds on file-supplied KDF parameters.
  • Derive keys only on unlock or passphrase changes, outside ordinary inference and OAuth refresh paths.

  • Explicitly convert old ciphertext using oaiso auth profile migrate-age NAME; see the format/migration contract.

  • Choose the backend explicitly during initialization.

  • Refuse unlocking if the selected backend is unavailable/locked; never switch backends, import host credentials or save plaintext. An already-unlocked proxy retains its in-memory key; stop it with auth profile lock separately from locking the OS keyring.
  • Noninteractive callers must receive an error rather than wait indefinitely for input.
  • No direct backend-conversion command is currently provided; reauthenticate into a new profile using the other backend. Future direct migration must unlock with the previous backend and durably rewrap before switching.
  • A lost key must not silently create a new empty vault.

docs.title: Files, recovery and login
docs.text:
• Prefer product-private storage on the WSL Linux filesystem.
  • Do not infer safe protection from chmod 0600 on DrvFS paths such as /mnt/c or shared folders.
  • Check the actual filesystem, ownership, permissions, socket behavior and atomic rename/fsync guarantees; reject unverified storage by default.
  • See WSL permissions.

  • Never put plaintext keys beside ciphertext in shared or synced folders.

  • WSL exports, VM clones, backups and disk snapshots may include credential state.

  • Manage ciphertext separately from recovery keys and require explicit recovery on a new environment.
  • Running control-VM memory snapshots and hibernation images can include decrypted secrets; vault encryption does not protect those copies.

  • Backups intended to exclude in-memory secrets require credential-using processes, including the proxy, to have exited.

  • Do not restore old refresh tokens or worker leases and resume automatically.

  • Explicit restores/clones require reauthentication and a new connection generation.
  • A snapshot restoring the vault, keys and generation ledger together cannot reliably be detected without independent trusted generation state.

  • AEAD and local CAS alone do not provide that guarantee.

  • Locking the key backend does not clear credentials already cached by the proxy.

  • Design explicit product lock/logout to stop issuance, revoke leases/streams and terminate credential-using processes while discarding their state.

  • Host swap, core dumps and outer snapshots need separate protection.

  • Support a user browser on another device through official device/headless flows or explicitly protected callback routing.

  • Do not assume the outer browser's localhost reaches WSL/VM localhost, or expose callback/admin ports to the LAN.
  • Login-only Kata runs must use a pinned CLI and temporary memory state, without workspace, hooks, plugins or ordinary console retention.
  • After permitted credential transfer and durable storage, discard temporary state on success, cancellation and failure.

  • Hold authentication integrations whose extraction/storage violates provider conditions.

  • Credential portability and Kata execution support are separate.

  • Validate nested virtualization, /dev/kvm and startup gates on actual WSL/VM deployments before claiming Kata support.
  • An operational credential backend does not establish runtime support, and failed isolation checks must not trigger automatic fallback to a weaker runtime.

docs.title: Implementation acceptance
docs.text:
• Initialize, unlock, save and unlock again after restart without D-Bus, Secret Service, systemd or TPM.
  • Handle keyring lock/session loss, wrong passphrase, key loss and canceled backend migration without plaintext or host-auth fallback.
  • Distinguish WSL Linux storage from DrvFS/shared filesystems; reject inadequate permissions, socket or durability guarantees.
  • Exercise WSL shutdown/restart, VM suspend/resume, separate-browser login, concurrent refresh, disk exhaustion and persistence failure.
  • Reject implicit reuse of old connections after explicit backup recovery/cloning, and document the limits of detecting outer snapshot rollback.
  • Reuse Store conformance and credential-leak tests, checking worker environment, files, logs and checkpoints.
  • These WSL/VM-specific acceptance cases have not been executed.

docs.title: Removed firewall feature
docs.text:
The old oaiso firewall and --allow-host / --block-host / --no-firewall / --sudo flags have been removed.

  • The root node service now enforces isolation with dedicated Linux bridges, namespaces and nftables tables.
  • Host setup requires administrator privileges.

  • Normal CLI use goes through the operator group.

  • Use network isolation for direct access restrictions and proxy policies (Japanese) for general egress allow/deny rules.

  • run --no-internet disconnects general egress while keeping AI API routes.
  • See migration (Japanese).

docs.title: Future work
docs.text: • Priorities, feature additions and security measures: improvement candidates. Implemented controls and proposed additions remain distinct.

docs.title: Simple setup, authentication and operation
docs.text:
• Implement the following six items, validating, documenting and committing each feature.
  • Retain existing profiles and the Auth Proxy. New login profiles default to keyring plus age, with explicit passphrase/plaintext alternatives.
Item State and completion criteria oaiso login Implemented in v0.0.3; live accounts unverified: agent/method selection, API connection check, independent profile storage Automatic first configuration Implemented in v0.0.3: admin authority and profile selection while preserving existing policy/settings Subscription login Kata Real Kata with fake credentials verified; live login unverified: pinned CLI, memory-only login, temporary VM cleanup, no secret retention in console logs or work VMs Consolidated status Implemented in v0.0.3: oaiso status distinguishes saved, connected, inference, runtime and update states Lightweight local encrypted storage Implemented in v0.0.3: keyring-default new login profiles, explicit migration, passphrase changes and locking; see verification Unified update guidance Implemented in v0.0.3: oaiso upgrade plans/applies distribution updates and explains image update order

  • Login is available in v0.0.3+.

  • In addition to Codex CLI and Claude Code, the following coding agents are candidates for future integration.

  • They are not currently supported.
  • Adoption, implementation order and release dates are undecided.

docs.title: Additional coding agents
docs.text:
Agent Integration work to investigate and implement Gemini CLI Launch adapter, authentication, Gemini proxy routing and headless execution GitHub Copilot CLI Copilot authentication and routing, GitHub integration, interactive and non-interactive execution OpenCode Launch adapter, provider configuration, proxy routing and non-interactive execution Aider API/proxy configuration, Git changes and commits, non-interactive execution Cursor CLI Launch adapter, authentication, endpoint configuration and headless execution Cline CLI Launch adapter, provider/auth configuration, headless execution and tools Kilo Code CLI Launch adapter, provider/auth configuration and proxy routing Goose Launch adapter, provider/auth configuration and tool/MCP integration
  • Investigate local CLI execution inside Kata separately from editor extensions and hosted offerings.
  • API and subscription authentication must be assessed per agent/provider; support for both is not assumed.

docs.title: Shared acceptance conditions
docs.text:
• Retain the authentication proxy.
  • Never pass real API keys, access tokens, refresh tokens or ID tokens to work VMs.
  • Workers receive only short-lived, per-run, proxy-scoped placeholders.
  • Use independent product authentication profiles, without automatically importing host CLI login files or inherited credentials.
  • Hold integrations whose storage or proxy use cannot satisfy official authentication terms.
  • Login-only Kata sessions must not persist secrets; discard temporary state on completion, cancellation and failure.
  • Do not replace the proxy with a persistent VM holding real credentials.
  • Prioritize independent credential management.
  • Real ID-token passthrough has been removed; do not weaken credential isolation or model authorization to add an agent.
  • Pin CLI versions, distributions and images; provide explicit launch settings independent of user/project configuration.
  • Extend static upstream checks for each agent.
  • Verify startup, tools, streaming, cancellation, stop/restart, revocation and credential leakage into logs, files and snapshots in real Kata.
  • Record verified behavior and unsupported constraints in the testing guide.
  • Review CLI/SDK licenses, retained baseline data, distribution terms and authentication/subscription conditions before integration.

docs.title: Independent authentication inside WSL and VMs
docs.text:
• The initial 0600 FileStore, independent profile creation/explicit import/selection and auth-proxy API/OAuth integration with durable refresh are implemented.
  • See usage.

  • Dedicated login Kata and API connection checks are implemented in v0.0.3. Encryption/explicit migration are also implemented. Live accounts, WSL/VM deployment acceptance and an actual desktop Secret Service still require verification.

  • Design the product's encrypted vault for trusted control environments running in WSL 2, Linux VMs and SSH/headless systems.

  • Retain the auth proxy and work-VM credential boundary without requiring an OS keyring, systemd or TPM.

  • Acceptance must include explicit passphrase unlocking, filesystem guarantees, lock/revocation, a browser on another device, backup, cloning and rollback.

  • See the detailed requirements.

  • Encryption/key backends are implemented in v0.0.3. Kata execution inside WSL/VMs and differences between desktop keyring services require separate deployment testing.

docs.title: Existing SDK dependency findings
docs.text:
• v0.0.4: dependency updates and applicability review completed; symbol findings reduced from 15 to 2. The earlier age migration reduced 19 to 15.
  • Both remaining findings concern unused daemon features. No finding exclusions; inapplicability rationale and dependency/API boundary regressions added.
  • Automated checks and follow-up real Kata network/revocation acceptance pass. No full eight-suite rerun, live-account or WSL acceptance.
  • Findings and affected modules.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Current state Start here No execution host yet Complete Installation first Host is ready Steps 1–4 start the first worker; steps 5–6 are optional Updating an existing installation Operations (Japanese)
  • This page covers v0.0.3 or later. A complete installation-to-first-run guide is also available.

docs.title: 1. Check the host
docs.text:
• Account: a normal user in the operator group.
  • Use the same account for credentials and normal CLI operations.
  • Normal run / proxy run operations do not need sudo.
oaiso runtime-check

Successful output (default Kata configuration)

[ok] egress-policy: Host rules are valid; private addresses stay blocked
[ok] runtime: io.containerd.kata.v2
[ok] host: linux/amd64
[ok] kvm: KVM device exists; the root node owns VM access
[ok] cgroups: cgroup v2 has cpu, memory and pids
[ok] node: pinned runtime, assets, resource profile and management socket verified
[ok] builder: BuildKit is reachable
[ok] forwarding: IPv4 forwarding enabled
  • All checks [ok] and exit code 0: continue.
  • An [error]: follow its Fix: line, then rerun. See diagnostic examples (Japanese).
  • Scope: host readiness. Provider authentication and live AI responses are checked later.
Task Requirements Run workers Linux x86_64, KVM, cgroup v2, dedicated containerd, Kata runtime-rs, Dragonball Build images BuildKit and buildctl Build the CLI from source Go 1.26.0 or later and Make
  • This page assumes the CLI and host are installed; otherwise return to Installation.
  • Release installations can run init from any directory; launch agents from your own project.

docs.title: 2. Prepare credentials
docs.text:
For new installations, use login to separate product and host credentials.

  1. Check the keyring. For SSH, WSL or headless use, open session and continue inside that shell.
  2. Choose exactly one login command below.
oaiso auth keyring check
# If the keyring is unavailable:
oaiso auth keyring session
Authentication Command Codex, API key oaiso login --agent codex --method api-key --profile work Codex, subscription oaiso login --agent codex --method subscription --profile work Claude Code, API key oaiso login --agent claude --method api-key --profile work Claude Code, subscription oaiso login --agent claude --method subscription --profile work
  • Login encrypts storage with keyring plus age, selects the profile and prepares the admin secret.
  • API keys use hidden input and a models-list connection check. Subscription login runs the official CLI inside temporary Kata.
  • Run init in the same keyring session. See passphrases and unlocking.
  • Do not additionally run manual auth profile set/import or admin-secret creation.

docs.title: Use an existing authentication method
docs.text:
Mode Setup Credential source Manual independent profile Authentication steps 1–3 Selected product Store only; no host fallback Legacy host integration Configure a source below Host credentials using source precedence

For legacy host integration

Agent Sources Codex OPENAI_API_KEY, saved API key, ~/.codex/auth.json Claude Code ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, saved API key
  • Login files: place under the invoking user's HOME.
  • File access: the proxy uses that user's UID/GID; 0600 files need no permission changes.
  • Workers receive placeholders, never real API keys or OAuth access/refresh tokens.
  • Claude details: API-key and subscription setup.
  • Saved Anthropic API keys are a compatibility input. auth set saves OpenAI keys only; use an independent profile for new Anthropic key storage.

docs.title: Allow general traffic before first startup, if needed
docs.text: Task Default and preparation AI inference only Fixed AI routes need no general-egress grant Git, npm or pip General egress is denied by default; allow required destinations Combine profile and network settings Merge keys into the same global [proxy] table; retain the admin-secret setting

docs.title: 3. Prepare images and start the proxies
docs.text:
Run as your normal user. Release installations work from any directory.

Configured provider Run exactly one OpenAI oaiso init --agent codex Anthropic oaiso init --agent claude
  • Do not run the other provider's preparation without its credentials.
  • Ready. means host, image and proxy preparation succeeded; verify live inference in the next step.

Final lines after successful Codex preparation

Ready. From your project run: oaiso codex
For host edit watchers add --watch-polling to `oaiso run` (Chokidar/Watchpack).
  • For Claude, the first line is Ready. From your project run: oaiso claude.
  • Host diagnostics, image checks and any required build logs appear before these lines.
init action Behavior or limit Diagnose host and find credentials Does not print credential contents or rewrite settings Prepare worker image Builds missing images and checks compatibility Start proxies Release installations package the installed static CLI into the proxy image Choose agent Explicit --agent, then configured default; a shell default prepares Codex Existing proxy with different authentication Running workers prevent a forced switch Outside this check Live provider authentication, connectivity and inference
  • Release installations create the proxy image from the installed static CLI. Source-built dynamic CLIs require their source checkout to build the proxy.
  • Once ready: return to the project directory.
  • Make Codex the default: oaiso default codex; add --local for this project only.

docs.title: Prepare each component separately
docs.text:
oaiso build --template plain --tag codex-dock:latest
oaiso proxy run
Component Purpose or endpoint codex-auth-proxy Authenticated AI requests codex-http-proxy General HTTP/CONNECT; no real credentials Admin API Host loopback 127.0.0.1:18081 Worker-facing API Not published to the host
  • proxy run creates the required network.
  • Details: auth proxy.
  • For an existing team's custom Dockerfile, review project settings and run init in that project. Release installations prepare a missing proxy image from the installed static CLI.

docs.title: 4. Start a worker
docs.text:
• Run from the project directory.
  • The project is shared at /workspace.
  • Choose the invocation matching your prepared provider below.
oaiso codex
# Or:
oaiso claude

# With Codex credentials; a configured default can start an agent instead.
oaiso run
oaiso run -- ls -la
Invocation Result oaiso codex Start Codex oaiso claude Start Claude Code oaiso run Configured agent; built-in default is an authenticated shell oaiso run -- COMMAND Run a command once Failed isolation check Startup stops; no automatic fallback to runc
  • Send a first prompt to check a live response. For 401/502 failures, use Troubleshooting (Japanese).
  • Foreground exit removes the worker by default; use the background example to try stop/restart.

docs.title: Share an environment with a team
docs.text:
• Optional: no oaiso.toml is needed for individual use with the default settings.

  • Run oaiso project init at the repository root.

  • Commit oaiso.toml.
  • Point [build] to a project Dockerfile for extra tools.
  • After cloning, prepare the host and credentials.
  • Run oaiso project check, then oaiso init.

Project settings

docs.title: 5. Run in the background
docs.text:
• This example uses Codex; substitute --agent claude for Claude.
  • It disables approval prompts; review the task and shared paths before running.
oaiso run --agent codex --name add-tests \
  --task "Add unit tests" --approval-mode full-auto -d

oaiso ps -a
oaiso logs add-tests --follow

Background startup output (final line)

Container started: a1b2c3d4e5f6
  • IDs vary. Find add-tests in ps -a; see the worker list example.
  • running means the worker is executing; check logs, artifacts and exit status for task success.

  • Short tasks may already be exited when listed. Check their logs too.

  • full-auto disables agent approval prompts.

  • Mount permissions still determine which shared files are writable.
  • Ctrl+C in logs --follow ends log following; the worker continues.
  • To isolate branches, first review worktree requirements (Japanese), then add --worktree and branch flags.

docs.title: 6. Stop, restart and remove
docs.text:
oaiso stop add-tests
oaiso start add-tests
oaiso stop add-tests
# Save results before removing the worker.
oaiso rm add-tests

Example stop, restart and removal output

$ oaiso stop add-tests
Stopping add-tests...
$ oaiso start add-tests
add-tests
$ oaiso stop add-tests
Stopping add-tests...
$ oaiso rm add-tests
Removing add-tests...
  • Stopping... and Removing... announce an attempt. Check exit code 0 and then ps -a to confirm completion.
  • After stopping: ⏹ exited. After restarting: ✅ running. After removal: no row.
  • With no workers, ps -a displays only column headers.
Operation or condition Result Stop Revoke the token; retain the container and snapshot Restart Recheck isolation and restore auth for the same worker ID/workspace Remove Clean up managed worktrees and networks; save results first Foreground exit Remove the worker unless --keep is set Shared proxies Keep running after workers exit
  • Restart reruns the main program; it does not resume suspended memory or execution state.
  • rm --force also removes running workers; use stop then rm for normal cleanup.

docs.title: Go API for embedding oaiso
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • github.com/pacificbelt30/codex-dock/pkg/cxd lets a trusted product on the same host manage workers through the existing oaiso node serve Unix socket.
  • It does not expose a new network service.

  • Access to the root managed socket permits arbitrary images, commands, and host mounts, so grant it only to trusted host processes.

  • Python, TypeScript and the machine-readable contract: Local API and SDKs (v0.0.4).

docs.title: Before connecting
docs.text:
1. Install the execution host (Japanese) with the node, containerd, Kata, and BuildKit.

    • Give the product access to the node socket at /run/codex-dock-node.sock, or set Options.NodeSocket to another path.

  2. Start the auth proxy and build or import the worker image.

    • Open does not start a proxy or create an image.

  3. Deploy the product's Go package with a compatible node.

    • Open validates the node and its Go client protocol; an incompatible version returns ErrVersionMismatch.
    • Update the embedded package from the same source revision when updating the CLI and node.

  4. The host admin API defaults to http://127.0.0.1:18081; general egress defaults to http://codex-http-proxy:18082.

  5. Standard proxy run/EnsureCaseProxy uses TLS 1.3 and mTLS from the guest relay to the auth proxy. Agents connect to guest-only http://127.0.0.1:18083. See coverage and custom-proxy limits.
  6. Options.ProxyContainerURL initially contains http://codex-auth-proxy:18080 as connection configuration; the actual transport is selected after querying proxy capabilities.
  7. Set Options.ProxyAdminURL, ProxyContainerURL, and HTTPProxyURL if your deployment differs.
  8. Keep Options.ProxyAdminSecret in the host product process.

docs.title: Choose an operation
docs.text: Method Contract Launch(ctx, request) Creates and starts a worker under a stable RequestID; ProjectDir must be absolute. Use Create → Start to separate creation from initial start Get / List Inspect worker state Exec / Wait Execute a command in a worker / wait for its main process Start / Stop / Remove Restart a stopped worker / stop it and revoke its auth token / remove its resources Request / RemoveRequest Query durable launch state by request ID / retry cleanup after a lost response Quarantine(ctx, worker) Stop ALL execution/network access and persist restart denial at the node; retain workspace/worktree/logs. Resume with a new worker under new policy Profiles(ctx) Query the running node's CPU, guest RAM, host memory reservation, and PID limits. These are reservation limits, not measured RSS Capabilities() / ProxyCapabilities(ctx) Query node build, protocol, and features / connected auth proxy features

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
• General egress defaults to deny even with zero-value Options.EgressPolicy.
  • Empty host domain and CIDR grants disable general egress, and a worker cannot widen that empty grant.
  • With grants present, the host maximum is enforced by a managed proxy even if the worker omits its own list.
  • Bare example.com includes subdomains; =example.com is exact.
  • Explicitly set Options.EgressPolicy.AllowPublicDestinations: true to permit public destinations without grants.
  • DefaultDeny: true takes precedence over that opt-in.
  • Fixed AI routes use independent authentication and model authorization.
package main

import (
    "context"
    "errors"
    "os"
    "time"

    "github.com/pacificbelt30/codex-dock/pkg/cxd"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    client, err := cxd.Open(ctx, cxd.Options{
        ProxyAdminSecret: os.Getenv("CODEX_DOCK_PROXY_ADMIN_SECRET"),
    })
    if err != nil { panic(err) }
    defer client.Close()

    worker, err := client.Launch(ctx, cxd.LaunchRequest{
        RequestID:     "product/project-7/job-123/attempt-1",
        ProjectDir:    "/srv/work/project-7",
        Image:         "codex-dock:latest",
        Profile:       "small",
        NoGitMetadata: true,
    })
    if errors.Is(err, cxd.ErrInProgress) {
        // Retry later with the same RequestID.
        return
    }
    if err != nil { panic(err) }
    defer client.Remove(context.Background(), worker.ID, true)

    command, err := client.CodexHTTPCommand(ctx, worker.ID)
    if err != nil { panic(err) }
    command.Argv = append(command.Argv, "exec", "Fix the tests")
    code, err := client.Exec(ctx, worker.ID, cxd.ExecRequest{
        Argv: command.Argv,
        Env: command.Env,
        Stdout: os.Stdout,
        Stderr: os.Stderr,
    })
    if err != nil { panic(err) }
    if code != 0 { panic("codex exited unsuccessfully") }
    if err := client.Stop(ctx, worker.ID, 10*time.Second); err != nil { panic(err) }
}
Request or operation Execution behavior No Agent in Launch Idle worker for repeated Exec calls Agent: "codex" / "claude" Run the CLI as the main process Exec Return the guest exit code separately from transport errors Wait Wait for the main process, not an individual Exec
  • This example sends a live AI request. Replace /srv/work/project-7 with a real project and prepare an OpenAI-authenticated proxy first.
  • CodexHTTPCommand supplies explicit HTTP/SSE settings. Never log command.Env, which contains the worker placeholder.

  • CLI auth_profile and admin_secret_file are not loaded automatically. Read admin authority on the host and supply Options, or configure case proxies and a Store.

  • LaunchRequest also supports model, approval mode, extra mounts, read-only rootfs, and disabling shared Git metadata.

  • Its default image is codex-dock:latest and default resource profile is standard.
  • Query client.Profiles(ctx) before selecting the smaller small or lightweight compact (guest 512 MiB / host 768 MiB) profile.
Image preparation Contract client.PrepareProject(ctx, dir, requestID, log) Validate oaiso.toml, build missing/stale images through BuildKit, return LaunchRequest for product review client.Build / client.BuildTemplate Available separately Launch prerequisites Built image and running auth proxy
  • PrepareProject does not load global settings or real credentials.
  • It copies project egress_allow_domains into LaunchRequest.EgressAllowDomains.
  • The Go API starts or reuses a dedicated egress proxy identified by the same policy ID as the CLI.
  • Options.EgressPolicy sets host limits that a worker allowlist cannot expand.
  • Build the matching proxy image before launch.
  • The API does not interactively start the auth proxy.
  • Keep real API keys and OAuth tokens out of LaunchRequest and the VM; keep the admin secret in host Options only.
  • The product applies its own host restrictions and authorizes users, cases, and runs.
  • For case credentials and execution identity, see case-scoped credentials.

docs.title: Retries and recovery
docs.text:
• Make each RequestID unique across the node.
  • Include the user or case, project, run, attempt, and connection version when those distinctions matter to your product.
  • Reusing an ID with different immutable options returns ErrConflict.

  • The node stores hashes of the ID and settings in a durable ledger, not the original ID, task text, or proxy admin secret.

  • With UseWorktree: true and no branch name, the API derives a branch name from the request ID.

  • A safe retry can reuse that branch after cleanup of a failed launch.

  • Concurrent launches with the same ID allow only one launcher to proceed; the other gets ErrInProgress.

  • If the response is lost, retry with the same ID to find the existing worker.
  • After a launcher disappears, the node reconciles its ledger with containerd and reservations before allowing a retry.
  • While the outcome is uncertain, it returns ErrInProgress and creates no second VM.
  • A completed worker removed later cannot be recreated with the same ID; the API returns ErrRequestGone.

  • Use a new ID for a new attempt.

  • While the five-minute launch lease is valid, an existing worker alone does not mean startup has completed.

  • If the launcher disappears before recording completion, retries may return ErrInProgress until the lease expires.
  • Once completion is stored in the ledger, retries return that result.
Launch result Recovery Error with a Worker.ID Inspect with Get; clean up with Remove ErrOutcomeUnknown Confirmation was lost; retry with the same ID ErrCleanupPending Retry cleanup
  • Request(ctx, requestID) reports the durable pending, complete, failed, or cleanup-pending state without exposing the live lease.
  • RemoveRequest(ctx, requestID, true) retries cleanup of the associated worker and deletion journal.
  • It also succeeds if only the prior cleanup response was lost.

  • Keep Options.StateDir stable across product restarts.

  • Canceling the Exec context stops the guest command.

  • Canceling Wait stops only the wait.
  • After a canceled Launch, the API still attempts cleanup.
  • Call Stop to stop a VM and revoke its token; call Remove to release its resources.

docs.title: Errors and compatibility
docs.text:
• Use errors.Is for ErrNotFound, ErrConflict, ErrInProgress, ErrCleanupPending, ErrRequestGone, ErrCapacity, ErrVersionMismatch, and ErrOutcomeUnknown.
  • Context cancellation and deadline errors are preserved.

  • Use errors.Unwrap to inspect the cause.

  • The public Go signatures do not expose internal node DTOs.

  • Deploy the CLI, library, node, and proxy image from matching builds.
  • The Go node protocol is v2; Open returns ErrVersionMismatch for incompatible node versions.
  • Capabilities() reports the validated node and ProxyCapabilities(ctx) reports the connected auth proxy.
  • The node's HTTP/JSON protocol over the Unix socket is internal and has no external compatibility guarantee.

Additional policy, execution and recovery APIs

  • Create(ctx, request) creates a stopped Kata worker; Start(ctx, worker) boots and verifies it before token activation and hook/agent execution.
  • Launch retains its combined create/start behavior.
  • ResourceUsage(ctx, worker) separates observed host cgroup current/peak memory and OOM kills from the profile budgets.

  • See operating conditions.

  • Use LaunchWithTimings(ctx, req) for sequential startup measurements.

  • ExecWithTimings(ctx, workerID, request) returns the exit code, ExecTimings and error for Exec (v0.0.4).
  • It returns Worker, LaunchTimings and error with the same contract as Launch.
  • See measurement scope and reproduction.

docs.title: Per-execution model authorization
docs.text:
• Set LaunchRequest.ModelPolicy to &identity.ModelPolicy{AllowedModels: []string{"model-id"}} to constrain the actual upstream request model per token.
  • The effective set intersects the proxy-wide allowlist.
  • A nil policy preserves inherited behavior; an explicitly empty policy denies every model.

  • Model selects an agent model and is not authorization.

  • Check ProxyCapabilities.TokenModelPolicy for support.

  • Unsupported proxies reject the request.
  • Policies are immutable creation inputs and survive stop/restart.
  • Restricted tokens permit validated HTTP/SSE AI routes only; WebSocket and redirects are denied.
  • General egress has a separate policy: use NoInternet or appropriate destination restrictions when bypass prevention is required.

A worker model policy must fit within 4 KiB including its serialized JSON and label name.

docs.title: Connection metadata and Codex HTTP/SSE
docs.text:
• Connections(ctx, workerID) returns the guest URL, authentication header/scheme, token environment variable name, transports and model-policy status.
  • It contains no token values or host credentials.

  • A created worker still requires Start before token activation.

  • CodexHTTPCommand(ctx, workerID) returns explicit HTTP/SSE Argv and Env containing only a short-lived placeholder.

  • Append exec or app-server and its arguments, then pass both to ExecRequest.
  • Connection settings use CLI -c overrides even when a caller ignores generated user configuration.
  • Do not log Env.

  • Verification targets the worker image's pinned Codex 0.163.0.

  • Normal launches with model restrictions disable WebSocket and request compression; unrestricted defaults are preserved.

  • The explicit helper also disables compression so the proxy can validate JSON.
  • See the official configuration reference and CLI configuration overrides.

docs.title: Claude Code connections
docs.text:
• ClaudeCommand(ctx, workerID) returns an explicit command/environment for the saved API-key or subscription mode, independent of user/project settings.
  • Append native Claude flags and pass both Argv and Env to Exec.
  • Do not log Env.
  • Connections reports ANTHROPIC_API_KEY with X-Api-Key for API mode, or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN with Bearer for subscriptions.
  • See Claude Code.

docs.title: Credential Store conformance
docs.text:
• Call pkg/cxd/credentialstore/storetest.Run(t, factory) from host-adapter tests.
  • The factory returns isolated test storage and a storetest.Harness controlling login replacement, disconnect, reopen and write-failure injection.
  • Reopen must construct a fresh adapter over the same durable database.

  • Never run the suite against production data or real credentials.

  • The suite checks refresh for both providers, stable connection generations, changing credential versions, exactly one winner among 12 concurrent CAS operations across instances, stale-write/reconnect rejection, durability after reopen, pre-commit failure/cancellation atomicity and snapshot ownership.

  • The caller supplies its database adapter and backend-specific failure controls.
  • Assertions never print credential values.

docs.title: Bounded temporary storage
docs.text:
Declare a guest path and filesystem ceiling in LaunchRequest.TemporaryStorage:

TemporaryStorage: []cxd.TemporaryStorage{{
    Target: "/run/build-cache", MaxBytes: 64 << 20,
    Medium: cxd.StorageMemory, Lifetime: cxd.StorageLifetimeVM,
    Executable: true,
}},
  • Only memory tmpfs with vm lifetime is supported.
  • Capacity is a filesystem ceiling, not preallocated memory.
  • Actual usage competes with applications within the existing guest memory budget.
  • The total of all declared ceilings must fit that budget; leave room for application memory.

  • Disk media, persistence and host storage reservations are unsupported and fail explicitly.

  • Targets must be clean absolute paths.

  • Sizes range from 4 KiB to 2 GiB in 4 KiB increments, with at most 16 filesystems.
  • Overlapping filesystems, hidden bind mounts, overlap with read-only binds or filesystem restrictions, and bootstrap/kernel paths are rejected.
  • Mounts use the worker UID/GID, initial mode 0700 and nosuid,nodev; noexec is the default.

  • Executable controls direct execution, not interpreters reading scripts.

  • Create does not use the filesystem.

  • During Start, the bootstrap verifies its type, capacity, owner and mount flags before hooks or user code run.
  • Data survives node restart and is discarded when the VM stops.
  • A later Start gets empty filesystems and reruns hooks.

  • Storage settings are immutable creation inputs.

  • This requires Kata and an updated pinned bootstrap.

  • Drain workers before installing the matching worker-guard and repin assets with runtime-lock --launcher ... --logger ....
  • Capabilities() advertises bounded-tmpfs-v1 only when that bootstrap supports capacity verification.
  • Unsupported nodes reject requests before creation.
  • Workers without declarations retain their existing behavior.

docs.title: Runnable embedding example
docs.text:
• examples/embedding/main.go uses only public APIs: capability/profile checks → Create → Start → cancel a streaming Exec → run another command in the same worker → Stop → RemoveRequest.
  • Cleanup uses a separate one-minute context.
  • Add -model for per-token authorization and -temporary-mib for temporary storage.
  • Only -prompt invokes Codex over explicit HTTP/SSE; the default test command makes no AI request.
go build -o /var/tmp/oaiso-embedding ./examples/embedding
/var/tmp/oaiso-embedding -project /srv/work/demo -request-id demo/attempt-1 -profile compact
# Requires an updated bootstrap and an allowed model; uses the real upstream.
/var/tmp/oaiso-embedding -project /srv/work/demo -request-id demo/attempt-2 \
  -profile compact -temporary-mib 64 -model MODEL_ID -prompt 'Run the project tests.'
  • The example reads CODEX_DOCK_KATA_NODE_SOCKET, CXD_EXAMPLE_PROXY_ADMIN_URL, CXD_EXAMPLE_PROXY_CONTAINER_URL, CODEX_DOCK_PROXY_ADMIN_SECRET and CXD_EXAMPLE_STATE_DIR from its host environment, falling back to Open defaults.
  • Case proxies also require CXD_EXAMPLE_CASE_ID, CXD_EXAMPLE_RUN_ID and CXD_EXAMPLE_CONNECTION_VERSION together.
  • CXD_EXAMPLE_* settings belong only to this example executable.

  • It does not display admin secrets or helper Env values.

  • The example removes its request at exit.

  • Use a new RequestID for another completed attempt.
  • After an uncertain response or cleanup failure, use the reported ID with Request / RemoveRequest.
  • Caller authorization, business state, database adapters, review/approval and Git workflows stay in the host application.

  • Reuse the conformance suite above for Credential Store adapters.

  • make kata-api-e2e VERSION=<matching-node-version> builds and runs this executable with synthetic upstreams in real Kata.

  • Select it alone with scripts/verify-go-api.py --binary ./oaiso --version <version> --run '^TestKataAPIIntegration/embedding-example$'.
  • A run with no executed subtests or only skips fails.

  • See the acceptance setup.

  • See quarantine for completion, retries and retained worktree cleanup.

  • Policy.Quarantined means the prohibition was persisted; QuarantinePending means its stop is unconfirmed.

  • Never treat an error from Quarantine as success.

  • v0.0.4: LaunchRequest.UsagePolicy specifies request/concurrency/body-byte/observed-token caps; query with Usage(ctx, workerID). Set CaseProxyOptions.UsageStateDir to a 0700 directory outside workspaces. Usage limits.

  • v0.0.4: LaunchRequest.Lifecycle.ProtectMain protects the primary process from idle reaping. Heartbeat(ctx, workerID, ttl) renews/releases a 0–5 minute activity lease without extending maximum lifetime. Contract and examples.

docs.title: Retaining diagnostic results
docs.text: • v0.0.4: SaveLaunchObservation and ReadObservations save/read launch timings. See format and limits. Handle storage failure separately from the launch result.

docs.title: Disk checkpoints
docs.text: • v0.0.4: Checkpoint, Checkpoints, InspectCheckpoint, RestoreCheckpoint, RemoveCheckpoint. See saved state, capacity and restore conditions.

docs.title: Worker TLS
docs.text:
• Available: v0.0.4. EnsureCaseProxy enables TLS; query ProxyCapabilities().WorkerMTLS.

  • Expiry, restart and legacy worker recreation.

  • TLS worker connection URLs refer to that guest’s loopback relay. Do not reuse them on the host/another VM or use URLs as execution IDs; use worker/run IDs.

docs.title: Resource controls
docs.text: • v0.0.4: connection, bandwidth, FD and block I/O limits. ResourcePolicies(ctx) exposes complete profiles; ResourceUsage.Policy reports the running contract. Proxy TCP limits are separate from AI request budgets.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Current state Next step New Ubuntu 26.04 host Follow steps 1–4 below Execution host already prepared Choose credentials and start a worker Updating an installed node Update procedure (Japanese) Other Linux distributions Manual installation (Japanese)

docs.title: Installed version
docs.text:
• These instructions install the signed prebuilt distribution (v0.0.6).
  • For the complete flow, follow installation through first startup.
  • The releases/latest commands below install the published release.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
Item Requirement OS and CPU Ubuntu 26.04, Linux x86_64 Host features systemd, KVM (/dev/kvm), cgroup v2 with cpu memory pids Account A normal user with sudo access Prerequisites Bash, curl, CA certificates and GitHub CLI for signature verification; no Go, Make or Git required Host Python uv-managed Python 3.12; missing uv/Python is prepared in user-owned directories Memory guidance At least 8 GiB for the default two-worker configuration; allow extra capacity for builds Network Access to GitHub Releases, uv/Python, pinned runtime archives, OS packages and container images WSL or a VM host All requirements above, plus nested virtualization
  • Operator group membership grants root-equivalent host management access. Choose trusted users only.

docs.title: 2. Prepare tools
docs.text:
Run as a normal user to install curl, CA certificates and GitHub CLI for signature verification.

bash <<'SH'
set -euo pipefail
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y curl ca-certificates
sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
oaiso_gh_key=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f -- "$oaiso_gh_key"' EXIT
curl -fsSL https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg -o "$oaiso_gh_key"
sudo install -m 0644 "$oaiso_gh_key" /etc/apt/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg
printf 'deb [arch=%s signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg] https://cli.github.com/packages stable main\n' "$(dpkg --print-architecture)" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-cli.list >/dev/null
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y gh
gh attestation verify --help >/dev/null
SH
  • Uses the official GitHub CLI APT repository. Skip this block if compatible tools are already installed.

  • Success: the final command exits with code 0. gh auth login is not required.

  • The installer uses Astral’s official installer to prepare uv in ~/.local/bin if needed.

  • Host Python is uv-managed 3.12; the OS Python is retained.
  • Check KVM with test -c /dev/kvm and controllers with cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.controllers.

docs.title: 3. Review the plan and install
docs.text:
Run from any directory; no source checkout is required.

curl -fsSL https://github.com/pacificbelt30/sandbox-oasis/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/pacificbelt30/sandbox-oasis/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --apply

Example plan output (excerpt)

Plan: verified Ubuntu 26.04 amd64 node; Kata 4.2.0 / Dragonball / containerd 2.4.2 / BuildKit 0.34.0 / runc 1.4.3
Bundle: /tmp/oaiso-release-<id>/bundle (version v0.0.6); operator: user; cache: /var/cache/codex-dock-setup; offline: no
  • Versions, paths and account names are examples and vary by installation and release.
  • Plan only ends with Plan only. Re-run the installer with --apply to install this release.
  • Successful application ends with Node installed. Log in again, then run oaiso init. Log in again before checking below.
  • Planning can download uv, Python and release assets. Host services are installed only with --apply.
Command or option Behavior No options Download and verify the matching release binaries, then display the plan --version v0.0.6 Download a specific release --apply Apply through sudo after the plan succeeds, forwarding the selected Python’s absolute path No operator option Register the invoking normal user --operator USER Register another existing normal user; required when invoking the script as root Installed component Main location or name CLI /usr/local/bin/oaiso Kata, containerd, BuildKit and runc Managed assets under /opt/codex-dock/releases/ Services codex-dock-node, codex-dock-containerd, codex-dock-buildkit Operator group codex-dock Bash, Zsh and Fish completion Under /usr/local/share/
  • Existing Docker and default containerd packages are retained.
  • Network setup, verification and recovery: setup details (Japanese).

docs.title: Download and review a pinned release
docs.text:
Example for v0.0.6. Inspect the saved script, then use the same file for planning and installation.

curl -fsSL -o install.sh https://github.com/pacificbelt30/sandbox-oasis/releases/download/v0.0.6/install.sh
less install.sh
bash install.sh --version v0.0.6
bash install.sh --version v0.0.6 --apply

docs.title: 4. Log in again and verify
docs.text:
1. Log out, then log in again as the registered normal user.
  2. Run:
command -v oaiso
oaiso --version
id -nG
oaiso runtime-check

Example CLI and group output

$ command -v oaiso
/usr/local/bin/oaiso
$ oaiso --version
oaiso version <version>
$ id -nG
user sudo codex-dock
  • $ marks an input line; copy executable commands from the bash block above.
  • Versions, account names and other groups vary. Check for membership in codex-dock.
  • runtime-check: see all successful checks and their meaning.
Check Expected result CLI Command path and version are displayed Group id -nG includes codex-dock Runtime runtime-check succeeds

docs.title: Next: credentials and first worker
docs.text:
1. Unlock the keyring and log in. For existing settings, see Authentication.
  2. Run oaiso init; use oaiso init --agent claude for Claude Code.

  3. From your project, run oaiso codex or oaiso claude.

  4. Normal init and run operations do not require sudo.

  5. Real API keys and OAuth tokens stay in the Auth Proxy; work VMs receive short-lived placeholders.
  6. General egress defaults to denial. Allow destinations (Japanese) when Git or package downloads are needed.

docs.title: What --bundle means
docs.text:
• A directory containing the prebuilt oaiso CLI, worker guard, I/O logger and bundle.json (version and SHA-256 checksums).
  • The release installer downloads and extracts it into a temporary directory; normally you do not specify the option. make node-bundle creates dist/node-bundle/ only when building from source.
  • Use --bundle PATH to use an extracted release bundle or bring one from another host. The destination host needs uv/Python, but not Go/Make.

  • It excludes Kata archives, container images, projects and credentials. Offline installation also needs prepared archives and Python.

  • Use a saved install.sh and a verified extracted bundle. See download and bundle examples (Japanese), including offline prerequisites.

docs.title: Other installation paths
docs.text: Method Scope and reference Build from source Developer build procedure (Japanese); requires Go, Make, Git and uv Manual host installation Kata host setup (Japanese) Prebuilt CLI/helper directory Bundle contents (Japanese); --bundle PATH skips Go/Make on this host Offline installation Offline setup (Japanese) Build and install CLI, helpers and completion make build / sudo make install; excludes Kata and host services Updates and rollback Update and recovery (Japanese)

docs.title: Official tool installation instructions
docs.text:
• Prebuilt installations do not require Go, Make or Git. Prepare development tools only for source builds.
  • Use the installer above to deploy Oaiso with its pinned runtime versions and settings.
Tool Installation or purpose Official instructions or downloads Bash Host shell; use Ubuntu's supplied shell GNU Bash installation curl Download the installer and release assets Official download guide GitHub CLI Verify signatures and provenance Official Linux installation uv Prepared automatically when missing uv installation Python Managed 3.12, prepared through uv for setup and updates Install Python with uv Kata Containers Worker VM isolation; deployed by the installer Installation guides containerd VM/container management; deployed by the installer Getting started BuildKit Worker/proxy image builds; deployed by the installer Quick start runc Proxy containers; deployed by the installer Releases
  • Go is needed in environments that build Oaiso or a product embedding its Go API. See the official Go Linux procedure and our command examples.

docs.title: Distribution verification
docs.text:
• The installer verifies signatures, source identity, the selected tag and SHA-256 before placement.
  • Verify the script before execution, inspect the SBOM and prevent rollback.

docs.title: Local API and Python / TypeScript SDKs
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4. Packages are not published to public registries yet.
  • Manage workers on the same Linux execution host through private pipes: SDK → oaiso api stdio → public Go API → existing node Unix socket.
  • No TCP listener or management-socket forwarding is added. Existing socket permissions remain required and grant host authority, including arbitrary mounts. Use trusted callers only.

docs.title: Requirements and scope
docs.text:
Item Requirement Execution host Prepared node, auth proxy and a built/imported worker image Versions Matching CLI, node and proxy builds; local protocol v1, node protocol v2 Python 3.12+; no runtime dependencies. Install uv TypeScript Node.js 22+; no runtime dependencies. Install Node.js. Compiler/types are development dependencies Configuration Explicit Open options; no automatic loading of CLI configuration or credential profiles Credentials Read the existing owner-only 0600 proxy admin-secret file into Options.ProxyAdminSecret.
