Real provider credentials stay in the auth proxy Workspace Existing absolute ProjectDir; normal /workspace sharing and host-file effects apply Included Create, launch, start, exec, get, list, wait, stop, remove, request reconciliation, quarantine, resources and capabilities; files, jobs and disk checkpoints Use Go for PTY, streaming I/O, image builds, artifact bundles, previews, live policy changes, checkpoint retention, credential Store and case-proxy creation
  • For writable workspaces, set LaunchRequest.User to the owning numeric UID/GID. Omitting it uses the image user; the SDK does not change host ownership.
  • General egress defaults to deny, as in Go. Host grants use Options.EgressPolicy.
  • No credential-returning API is exposed. Options travel through stdin, never shell arguments. SDKs discard bridge stderr and return fixed error categories.
  • Guest stdout/stderr are explicitly returned by exec; callers remain responsible for what their guest commands print.

docs.title: Install Python from source
docs.text:
Run as the operator from a checkout containing this feature. Create a new virtual environment; choose another directory if it already exists.

uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-sdk
uv pip install --python .venv-sdk/bin/python ./sdk/python
.venv-sdk/bin/python -c 'from oaiso import Client; print("SDK import OK")'

SDK import OK verifies the import, not node connectivity.

docs.title: Create, execute and clean up
docs.text:
Save as example.py. Place oaiso on PATH, prepare the proxy, replace /srv/work/project with a real directory and adjust the admin-secret path. Request IDs are examples: preserve the ID and options for retries; choose a new ID for a new task.

from pathlib import Path
import os
from oaiso import Client

secret = (Path.home() / ".config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret").read_text().strip()
request = {
    "RequestID": "my-app/project-1/task-1/attempt-1",
    "ProjectDir": "/srv/work/project",
    "Image": "codex-dock:latest",
    "Profile": "compact",
    "User": f"{os.getuid()}:{os.getgid()}",
    "NoInternet": True,
}
with Client({"ProxyAdminSecret": secret}) as client:
    worker = client.create(request)
    try:
        client.start(worker["ID"])
        result = client.exec(worker["ID"], ["printf", "hello"])
        print(result["exit_code"], result["stdout"].decode())
    finally:
        client.remove_request(request["RequestID"], force=True)

.venv-sdk/bin/python example.py

Example output:

0 hello
  • Client(...) validates connectivity and versions only.
  • create reserves resources without running guest code; start starts the guest.
  • Closing the client closes handles; stop/remove workers explicitly.

docs.title: Install TypeScript from source
docs.text:
Run from the repository root:

npm --prefix sdk/typescript ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
npm --prefix sdk/typescript run build

Then run from your application directory, replacing the source path:

npm install /absolute/path/to/sandbox-oasis/sdk/typescript

Save this as example.mjs. TypeScript uses the same API with the included declarations. Apply the same workspace, secret-path and request-ID requirements as in Python.

import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { homedir } from 'node:os';
import { Client } from '@oaiso/local';

const secret = (await readFile(`${homedir()}/.config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret`, 'utf8')).trim();
const request = {
  RequestID: 'my-app/project-1/task-2/attempt-1',
  ProjectDir: '/srv/work/project',
  Image: 'codex-dock:latest',
  Profile: 'compact',
  User: `${process.getuid()}:${process.getgid()}`,
  NoInternet: true,
};
const client = await Client.open({ ProxyAdminSecret: secret });
try {
  const worker = await client.create(request);
  try {
    await client.start(worker.ID);
    const result = await client.exec(worker.ID, ['printf', 'hello']);
    console.log(result.exit_code, result.stdout.toString());
  } finally {
    await client.removeRequest(request.RequestID, true);
  }
} finally {
  await client.close();
}

node example.mjs
  • Expected output: 0 hello. Do not log options or put secrets in argv.
  • TypeScript rejects fractions, non-finite values and unsafe integers before sending and rejects unsafe received numbers rather than returning rounded values. Use Go or Python for larger 64-bit integers.

docs.title: Cancellation and deadlines
docs.text:
Operation Cancellation means wait Cancel the wait only; the worker continues exec Propagate cancellation to the guest command; reconcile races with completion/disconnection create / launch Use Go cancellation/cleanup; query the request and remove remaining resources stop / remove A missing response leaves completion unconfirmed; query worker/request state Cancel result accepted: true The active call received cancellation; this does not confirm stop/cleanup Disconnect / close Cancel active calls and close handles; created workers may remain
  • Python: pending = client.submit("wait", {"worker_id": worker_id}), pending.cancel().result(), pending.result().
  • TypeScript: const pending = client.submit('wait', {worker_id: workerID}), await pending.cancel(), await pending.result.
  • TypeScript also accepts {signal: controller.signal} in the final options argument.
  • Server deadline: 180 seconds by default, at most 1,200 seconds. Configure Python timeout_ms / TypeScript timeoutMs; zero selects the default.
  • Python result(timeout=seconds) requests cancellation on timeout. Mutations may already have completed and require reconciliation.
  • Stop grace is separate: default 10 seconds; zero means immediate forced stop.

docs.title: Retry and errors
docs.text:
Identifier / state Meaning and next action Call id Connection-local response correlation, increasing from 1; assigned by SDK LaunchRequest.RequestID Durable, node-wide creation identity, 1–256 UTF-8 bytes; assigned by application pending / in_progress Running/recovering; query the same ID, do not duplicate with another ID complete Durable creation result; query get for current running state failed Prior creation failed; retry identical request/options cleanup-pending / cleanup_pending Retry cleanup by worker/request ID conflict Immutable options differ for an existing request request_gone Completed worker was removed; the same ID cannot recreate it outcome_unknown / transport_lost Reconcile via request / get before deciding to retry version_mismatch Install matching CLI/node/proxy builds, then reconnect permission_denied Check existing socket/file permissions; the SDK does not elevate privileges internal Unclassified Go failure; underlying text is withheld. Inspect state/audit on the trusted host
  • No automatic retries. Creation retries require identical request ID, immutable options and connection options. Mixing create and launch with the same ID conflicts.
  • Replaying exec may execute twice; never retry it automatically after a lost response.
  • Python APIError: code, codes, requires_reconciliation, partial_result. TypeScript: code, codes, requiresReconciliation, partialResult.
  • Partial Worker.ID can be used for cleanup. Error strings omit raw arguments, credentials and underlying errors.
  • Reconciliation flags describe the affected call; a false flag never proves unrelated workers stopped.
  • Worker Status is an observed opaque string. An unknown status never means stopped.

docs.title: Machine-readable contract
docs.text:
Item Contract Transport Private NDJSON stdin/stdout pipes, local protocol v1; one JSON object per line Request version, id, method, params; optional timeout_ms Response version, id, result and/or error; errors may include partial results Types Existing Go JSON field names are preserved inside DTOs; consult the schema for RequestID versus request_id Units Bytes use base64; Go DTO durations use nanoseconds, call deadlines milliseconds, stop grace seconds Bounds 1 MiB request, 4 MiB response, 256 KiB each stdout/stderr, 16 concurrent calls; cancel bypasses active-call slots Overflow Cancel and return output_limit plus partial output. Use Go streaming APIs for large output/PTY Validation Reject unknown/duplicate fields and malformed frames. A malformed outer frame closes the connection; reconcile active mutations Source JSON Schema, generated from Go DTOs and checked for CI drift 
oaiso api schema > local-api-v1.schema.json
  • Schema export needs no node/auth access. It uses JSON Schema draft 2020-12.
  • x-oaiso records per-method retry/cancel rules, request states and result types.
  • The schema defines types and the wire contract; Go and the node enforce reservations, network/model authorization and path constraints at runtime. Breaking changes require a new local protocol version and contract; discover additive methods through capabilities.
  • This is a deliberately limited adapter; check capabilities before using an operation. SDKs do not call the internal node HTTP API directly.

docs.title: Developer checks
docs.text:
Run from the repository root with Go, uv and Node.js installed:

go run ./api/generate
npm --prefix sdk/typescript ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
go test -race ./pkg/cxd/localapi
go test -c -o /tmp/oaiso-local-api.test ./pkg/cxd/localapi
uv run --no-project --no-config --managed-python --python 3.12 python scripts/verify-local-sdks.py --fixture /tmp/oaiso-local-api.test
  • Both SDKs use the same Go adapter for version/retry/conflict/lost-response/cancel/output-bound/redaction/cleanup tests.
  • See verification records for real Kata prerequisites, scope and results. Synthetic success is separate from real-account authentication/inference.

docs.title: Files, jobs and checkpoints
docs.text:
• Available: v0.0.4; additive methods within local API v1.
Operation Python TypeScript Read / write / list read_file / write_file / list_files readFile / writeFile / listFiles Background execution start_job startJob Job lookup / list job / list_jobs job / listJobs Logs with offset job_logs(worker_id, job_id, offset=0) jobLogs(workerID, jobID, 0) Wait / kill wait_job / kill_job waitJob / killJob Save / list disk checkpoints checkpoint / checkpoints checkpoint / checkpoints Inspect / remove inspect_checkpoint / remove_checkpoint inspectCheckpoint / removeCheckpoint Restore to a new VM restore_checkpoint(id, request) restoreCheckpoint(id, request)

Inside an existing Python client context with a running worker:

worker_id = worker["ID"]
client.write_file(worker_id, "input.json", b'{"task":"example"}')
print(client.list_files(worker_id))
job = client.start_job(worker_id, ["python3", "-c", "print('done')"])
finished = client.wait_job(worker_id, job["id"])
logs = client.job_logs(worker_id, job["id"], offset=0)
print(finished["exit_code"], logs["output"])

The TypeScript equivalent using an existing client/worker:

await client.writeFile(worker.ID, "input.json", Buffer.from('{"task":"example"}'));
console.log(await client.listFiles(worker.ID));
const job = await client.startJob(worker.ID, ["python3", "-c", "print('done')"]);
const finished = await client.waitJob(worker.ID, job.id);
const logs = await client.jobLogs(worker.ID, job.id, 0);
console.log(finished.exit_code, logs.output);
Contract Behavior Files Relative to /workspace, no symlink traversal, at most 512 KiB per transfer. Go/CLI retain their separate 64 MiB limit Larger files Use Go/CLI; chunked SDK upload is not provided Starting jobs Never automatically retried. Reconcile uncertain outcomes using job IDs/listing Logs Use next for the next offset; truncated indicates a retention gap Canceling job wait Cancels waiting only, not the job Checkpoint creation Requires a stopped Kata worker. Inspect the catalog after losing a create response Restore New RequestID required; reject conflicting image/digest or runc

See disk checkpoint scope. RAM and connections are excluded.

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • The root node service manages Linux bridges, namespaces, veth links and dedicated nftables tables.
  • It does not depend on Docker network APIs or a CNI daemon.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
Network or proxy Purpose dock-net-proxy Primary proxy network, host gateway and outbound NAT dock-net-w-<name> Private worker L2 network, without a host IPv4 address, default route or NAT codex-auth-proxy Fixed AI reverse routes and token API on connected worker networks codex-http-proxy General HTTP/CONNECT forwarding, attached only when allowed
  • Each worker has one private network.
  • Kata workers receive proxy URLs pinned to the verified front IPs on that network, without relying on the guest hosts file.
  • The worker uses loopback DNS; external resolution and dialing happen in the proxies.

  • Proxy namespaces do not forward IP packets between interfaces.

  • Dedicated nftables rules block worker-to-host and worker-to-other-interface traffic.

  • Host IPv4 forwarding and existing firewall rules must allow the proxy egress path.
  • The product does not flush other services' tables.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Listener Exposure Auth data 18080 Worker networks only Auth admin 18081 Primary egress IP, relayed to host 127.0.0.1 General forward 18082 Selected worker networks only
  • Workers cannot reach the admin listener or management sockets.
  • Only the auth proxy receives real credentials.

docs.title: Outbound policy
docs.text:
• General egress defaults to denial; without domain/CIDR grants, workers are not connected to the general proxy.
  • First-time setup: allow destinations before launch.
  • General egress supports domain, IP/CIDR and port allow/deny rules.
  • Denials win.
  • All nonempty allowlists must match.
  • Private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses remain blocked.
  • DNS answers and redirects are checked, and the dialer uses a verified address.
oaiso proxy run \
  --forward-allow-domain github.com \
  --forward-allow-domain registry.npmjs.org \
  --forward-deny-domain blocked.github.com
  • These rules control general egress, not fixed AI authentication routes.
  • run --no-internet disconnects the general egress proxy and keeps AI routes available.
  • See policy rules (Japanese).
  • Bare domains include subdomains; =hostname matches only that name.
  • Changing configuration does not update existing proxies or CONNECT tunnels; recreate proxies and workers after saving results.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Stop keeps networks for restart.
  • Remove detaches the selected proxies and reclaims owned resources.
  • Network IDs, addresses, namespace identity and firewall state are recorded privately and verified before reuse.
  • Subnets are selected from 10.253.0.0/16; existing addresses and routes are checked for conflicts.
oaiso network create
oaiso network status
oaiso network rm

See host setup and troubleshooting (Japanese).

docs.title: Performance and benchmarks
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Measure Kata asset verification, public Go API Exec and proxy authentication separately.
  • The measurement and regression record (Japanese) contains the before/after values, conditions and verified scope.

docs.title: Combine duplicate Exec verification
docs.text:
• Available: v0.0.4.
  • Runtime and host attestation share one full asset verification per Exec.
  • Every operation rereads all assets and checks SHA-256, ownership, paths, permissions and configuration. There is no timestamp cache.
  • Worker configuration, host processes/cgroups and guest identity, privileges and resource limits are checked before the command starts.
  • Nodes without verify-runtime-v1 use the previous verification sequence. Failure on a supporting node never triggers a legacy retry.
  • Assets are validated after admission-lock waiting, before supervisor handling in the same operation. Ownership, PID and resource-limit checks remain in place.
  • Standalone supervisor handling during stop/delete retains independent asset validation.
  • Startup also removes only duplication within one operation; asset checks before and after VM start remain separate.
  • Resource reservations, startup bootstrap checks and credential activation order are preserved.

docs.title: Asset verification and proxy authentication
docs.text:
• Asset verification checks file ownership, paths, executable permissions and SHA-256 with at most min(4, GOMAXPROCS) concurrent readers per validation.
  • Every validation reads every asset and checks configuration bindings.
  • This uses spare CPU capacity while retaining the security checks.
  • Parallel asset verification alone does not reduce the total hashing work. Combining duplicate Exec checks reduces repeated work within that operation.

  • Measure throughput under CPU saturation and performance on storage-bound hosts separately.

  • The auth proxy looks up issuance records directly by token value.

  • Issuance, restore and revocation update the index under the same lock, avoiding a scan of every worker.

  • Expiry, provider/model restrictions and active-stream cancellation follow the auth proxy contract.

  • These optimizations are enabled by the implementation and require no activation flag.

  • Follow the CLI, node and proxy update procedure (Japanese).
  • Products using the Go API must also use the same source version as the node.

docs.title: Measurements on 2026-10-25
docs.text:
• Scope: v0.0.4. Full asset verification within one Exec was consolidated from three reads to one.
  • SHA-256 accounted for 94.0% of baseline node CPU profile time.
Condition Value Host Linux amd64, Core i5-8500, 4 vCPUs, KVM Build Go 1.27.3, client/node GOMAXPROCS=4, matching measurement BuildVersion Runtime Kata 4.2.0 / Dragonball, containerd 2.4.2, BuildKit 0.34.0 Resources compact: 512 MiB guest, 768 MiB host reservation, 1 CPU, 512 PIDs; two-worker admission limit Order Before → after → after → before on the same node, assets and worker image Samples per version 6 sequential launches, 6 two-worker launch batches, 14 sequential Execs, 10 two-worker Exec batches Workload Warm page cache, prepared image, no general egress/Git metadata/agent, synthetic credentials Excluded Client Open, proxy creation, image builds/imports, cleanup and AI inference
  • The baseline is a saved source tree based on d9c0419e, including the preceding P1 work. This does not compare published releases.
  • Both versions enabled identical CPU profiling; no builds or other tests ran during measurement.
Operation Before, median After, median Time reduction Sequential launch 7.740 s 7.103 s 8.2% Two-worker launch, both complete 13.721 s 12.744 s 7.1% Public Go API Exec, /bin/true 2.475 s 1.161 s 53.1% Two-worker Exec, both complete 3.329 s 1.888 s 43.3%
  • Sequential Exec range: 2.362–3.229 s before, 1.094–1.361 s after.
  • Concurrent Exec range: 3.197–3.456 s before, 1.830–2.407 s after.
  • Sequential launch range: 7.638–8.080 s before, 6.904–7.238 s after.
  • Median Exec phases after the change: full assets/host verification 0.706 s, guest checks 0.203 s. Sequential VM-start API time was 3.670 → 3.667 s.
  • The VM-start API includes node-side waits. Further startup improvements and greater worker density remain future work.

docs.title: CPU, memory and I/O costs
docs.text:
Observation Before After Node CPU per Exec 3.062 CPU-s 1.064 CPU-s, 65.3% less Node logical reads per Exec 1.197 GiB 0.400 GiB, 66.6% less Node plus two VMs, CPU per Exec 3.256 CPU-s 1.336 CPU-s, 59.0% less Two VMs only, CPU per Exec 0.194 CPU-s 0.272 CPU-s Node CPU queue wait, 14 Execs total 0.883 s 0.808 s Node RSS at the end of Exec groups 36.79 MiB 38.84 MiB Combined observed memory of two VMs 313.31 MiB 312.80 MiB VM OOM kills 0 0
  • CPU/read counters are group totals divided by Exec count. RSS/memory are averages of two group-end observations.
  • CPU queue wait is OS scheduler waiting, summed from schedstat for threads present at both group boundaries.
  • VM CPU and node RSS increased; the measured CPU total decreased. VM reservations are unchanged.
  • Individual VM observed memory was 155.09–157.45 MiB, maximum observed peak 157.83 MiB. This does not capture startup peaks for every VM.
  • Node physical disk reads during Exec were zero in both versions. Fewer logical reads do not establish cold-storage speedup.
  • Launch-group node CPU/I/O counters include cleanup between samples and were not compared as launch-only costs.
  • The CPU sum excludes host processes outside the node and these VM cgroups.
  • AI latency, cold startup, other CPUs/profiles and more than two workers are unmeasured.
  • See real-Kata regression coverage (Japanese).

docs.title: Choose a measurement
docs.text:
Benchmark Includes Excludes BenchmarkWorkerRequest Authentication header parsing, record lookup, expiry/route checks, request context creation and release Network and upstream API communication BenchmarkLoadPinnedManifest Reading real assets; checksum, ownership, path and configuration checks VM startup and guest execution BenchmarkKataExec Per-exec asset, host and guest checks; running /bin/true and checking completion VM creation, client Open, warmup and AI inference BenchmarkKataLaunch A fresh Launch and its sequential phases; first Exec is reported separately Client Open, proxy creation, image builds/imports, removal and AI inference
  • The proxy benchmark measures accepted and unissued tokens with 1, 32, 256 and 4,096 issuance records.
  • Allocation figures reported by the Exec benchmark cover the client process.

docs.title: Locate startup costs
docs.text:
• The Go API client.LaunchWithTimings(ctx, req) returns Worker, LaunchTimings and error.
  • It uses the same request identity, verification, authentication and cleanup as Launch.
  • Measurement does not affect the request fingerprint.
  • Ordinary Launch does not allocate a timing record.
worker, timing, err := client.LaunchWithTimings(ctx, req)
// Preserve worker.ID for recovery on failure, following the existing API contract.
for _, phase := range timing.Phases {
    fmt.Printf("%s: %s\n", phase.Name, phase.Duration)
}
  • Phases partition elapsed wall time without overlap; their sum equals timing.Duration.
  • JSON durations are in nanoseconds.
  • They distinguish preflight, network setup, capacity reservation, container creation, created-worker verification, VM start, host/guest verification, token activation, bootstrap release, readiness and request confirmation.
  • vm_start covers the entire node start API, not pure VMM boot time.
  • host_guest_verification includes asset revalidation, host checks and the guest probe.
  • An idempotent retry reports only the phases actually executed, such as existing-worker lookup.

  • Failures return partial measurements including cleanup and request-abort confirmation.

  • Reports contain fixed phase names and durations only, without paths, arguments, request values, tokens or error text.

  • The caller decides whether to store or transmit them.
  • Phase names are diagnostics and may change between versions.
  • Use the existing API outcome for readiness and authentication decisions.

docs.title: Locate Exec costs
docs.text:
• Available: v0.0.4.
  • ExecWithTimings(ctx, workerID, request) returns the exit code, ExecTimings and error with normal Exec semantics for streams, exit status, cancellation and failures.
  • Records contain fixed phase names and durations only: no arguments, paths, output, credentials or error text. Concurrent calls use separate records.
code, timing, err := client.ExecWithTimings(ctx, worker.ID, cxd.ExecRequest{
    Argv: []string{"/bin/true"},
})
fmt.Printf("exit=%d ok=%t\n", code, err == nil)
for _, phase := range timing.Phases {
    fmt.Printf("%s: %s\n", phase.Name, phase.Duration)
}
Phase Includes request_validation Arguments, working directory and environment validation exec_lookup Worker lookup and running/managed/quarantine checks exec_runtime Runtime registration, resource profile and cgroup version exec_configuration Configuration, mounts, networking and resource limits exec_host Full asset/host attestation and node identity checks exec_guest Guest probe and restriction checks exec_create, exec_attach Command creation and stream attachment exec_io, exec_result Command I/O, waiting and exit-status inspection
  • exec_verification covers the short verification entry step.
  • Phases do not overlap and sum to timing.Duration; failures return partial timings.
  • exec_io includes command execution, potentially including AI response waits.
  • CPU time, memory and I/O counters require separate node-side profiles and cgroup observations.

docs.title: Run the benchmarks
docs.text:
• Run from the repository root with the development Go environment (Japanese).
  • The following CODEX_DOCK_BENCH_* variables are inputs to benchmarks only.

docs.title: Proxy authentication
docs.text:
No Kata node or real upstream API connection is required.

go test ./internal/authproxy -run '^$' \
  -bench '^BenchmarkWorkerRequest$' -benchmem -count=5 -benchtime=500ms

docs.title: Pinned asset verification
docs.text:
• On Linux, specify an existing sealed manifest.
  • The benchmark reads files without modifying them.
  • A root-owned manifest requires the node operator's read permissions.
  • Run from trusted source.
CODEX_DOCK_BENCH_MANIFEST=/etc/codex-dock/kata-assets.json \
  go test ./internal/kataguard -run '^$' \
    -bench '^BenchmarkLoadPinnedManifest$' -benchmem -benchtime=3x -count=5

docs.title: Exec in a real Kata VM
docs.text:
• On a prepared test host, start an idle managed Kata worker through the normal workflow and obtain its full ID.
  • The benchmark runs /bin/true in that VM.
  • The caller starts the worker and stops/removes it after measurement.
  • Replace FULL_WORKER_ID with its actual ID and set the dev value in -ldflags to the running node's BuildVersion.
CODEX_DOCK_KATA_NODE_SOCKET=/run/codex-dock-node.sock \
CODEX_DOCK_BENCH_WORKER=FULL_WORKER_ID \
  go test -ldflags '-X github.com/pacificbelt30/codex-dock/internal/buildinfo.Version=dev' \
    ./pkg/cxd -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkKataExec$' -benchmem -benchtime=3x -count=5
  • Omitting the manifest path or worker ID skips the corresponding benchmark.
  • A skip is not a successful measurement.

docs.title: Fresh startup in real Kata
docs.text:
• Use an isolated test node with no other users or concurrent launches.
  • Preload the worker and proxy images.
  • The benchmark creates a CredentialStore containing only an invalid API key, a dedicated case proxy, and a fresh worker for every sample, then removes them.
  • It uses no real account or upstream AI.
  • Workers have no general egress, Git metadata sharing or running agent; they remain idle.
CODEX_DOCK_KATA_NODE_SOCKET=/run/codex-dock-node.sock \
CODEX_DOCK_BENCH_LAUNCH=1 CODEX_DOCK_BENCH_PROFILE=compact \
CODEX_DOCK_KATA_TEST_IMAGE=codex-dock:latest \
CODEX_DOCK_KATA_PROXY_IMAGE=codex-dock-proxy:latest \
GOMAXPROCS=4 \
  go test -ldflags '-X github.com/pacificbelt30/codex-dock/internal/buildinfo.Version=dev' \
    ./pkg/cxd -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkKataLaunch$' -benchtime=3x -count=5 -timeout=20m -v
  • Match dev to the node's BuildVersion.
  • Omitting CODEX_DOCK_BENCH_LAUNCH=1 skips this benchmark.
  • launch_ms/op and phase-specific *_ms/op report launch times.
  • first_exec_ms/op separately measures the first /bin/true execution and completion after launch.
  • Each launch_timing JSON record contains individual measurements.
  • The Go benchmark also performs one calibration launch before its measured iterations.
  • Use CODEX_DOCK_BENCH_PROFILE to select a profile other than the default compact.
  • Results with preloaded images and a warm page cache do not establish first image-unpack or real task readiness latency.

docs.title: Measure startup, Exec and two-worker concurrency
docs.text:
• Available: v0.0.4.
  • Use a dedicated node with capacity for at least two more workers; avoid shared services.
  • Prepare the pinned worker/proxy images as above. No real credentials or AI inference are used.
  • The test measures three sequential launches, three two-worker launch batches, seven sequential Execs and five two-worker Exec batches.
  • It removes its own workers and case proxy afterward.
OAISO_KATA_PERFORMANCE=1 GOMAXPROCS=4 \
CODEX_DOCK_KATA_NODE_SOCKET=/run/codex-dock-node.sock \
CODEX_DOCK_KATA_TEST_IMAGE=codex-dock:latest \
CODEX_DOCK_KATA_PROXY_IMAGE=codex-dock-proxy:latest \
  go test -ldflags '-X github.com/pacificbelt30/codex-dock/internal/buildinfo.Version=dev' \
    ./pkg/cxd -run '^TestKataPerformance$' -count=1 -timeout=20m -v
  • Match dev to the node BuildVersion. Client GOMAXPROCS does not change the node setting.
  • perf_sample contains phase timings; perf_resources reports budgets, observed memory and OOM kills.
  • Wall-time samples exclude image builds/imports, proxy creation and cleanup.
  • Prepared-image, warm-page-cache results are separate from installation, cold startup and AI inference.
  • Node operators must collect CPU, disk I/O and scheduler waiting separately; this test alone does not collect them.

docs.title: Choose the next optimization
docs.text:
• Fresh-start measurements (Japanese) identify VM start as the main wait.
  • Prebooting unused VMs is the next candidate.
  • Warm pools, memory snapshots and VM forks are not implemented.

  • Existing Create creates a stopped worker; Start still boots its VM.

  • A warm pool needs to keep bootstrap closed and authentication inactive during preparation, then recheck assets, host/guest restrictions and policy at assignment.

  • It must preserve the current immutable workspace, mounts, UID, network, image, model authorization and execution identity.
  • Do not reassign workers to different requests or return used VMs to the pool.
  • Count waiting VMs against reservations.
  • Verify expiry, cancellation, ownership recovery after node restart and exclusive assignment before enabling it.
  • Compare assignment through first Exec against ordinary startup under identical conditions, including verification, replenishment and reserved-memory costs.
  • VM start's current share is not an achieved speedup.

docs.title: Comparison conditions
docs.text:
• Use the same Go version, CPU conditions, assets and worker profile, with no competing builds or tests.
  • Build the node and client with the same measurement BuildVersion.
  • Alternate the order of old/new revisions within pairs and compare medians across samples.

  • Distinguish warm page-cache measurements from runs that include initial disk reads.

  • Run regression checks (Japanese) after measurement.

  • Runtime changes require make kata-e2e.
  • Authentication changes also need active-connection cancellation checks for revocation, expiry, replacement, restore and proxy stop.
  • Remove test VMs, containers and networks before deleting test services or ownership records.

docs.title: Standalone proxy
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • This developer guide runs a local client without oaiso run.
  • It does not create Kata isolation or worker networks.
  • For normal use, follow the quick start.

docs.title: 1. Start a local proxy
docs.text:
• Prepare host credentials.
  • Create the admin-secret file first.
  • Requirements: Bash, Python 3, curl and a host Codex CLI. Select an independent profile globally first, if using one.
  • Run these examples in one bash session.
  • Both listeners bind to loopback.
export PROXY_ADMIN_SECRET_FILE="$HOME/.config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret"

oaiso proxy serve --role auth \
  --listen 127.0.0.1:18080 --admin-listen 127.0.0.1:18081 \
  --admin-secret-file "$PROXY_ADMIN_SECRET_FILE" &
PROXY_PID=$!

export PROXY_DATA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18080
export PROXY_ADMIN_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18081
curl --retry 5 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1 -fsS "$PROXY_DATA_URL/health" >/dev/null
  • Use serve for this local example: proxy run does not publish the data port to the host.
  • Do not expose plain HTTP admin APIs or bearer tokens to other machines.

docs.title: 2. Issue a token
docs.text:
export SESSION_NAME=my-session
TOKEN=$(python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.request import Request, ProxyHandler, build_opener
secret = Path(os.environ['PROXY_ADMIN_SECRET_FILE']).read_text().strip()
request = Request(os.environ['PROXY_ADMIN_URL'] + '/admin/issue',
    data=json.dumps({'container': os.environ['SESSION_NAME'], 'ttl': 3600}).encode(),
    headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Proxy-Admin-Secret': secret})
with build_opener(ProxyHandler({})).open(request, timeout=10) as response:
    print(json.load(response)['token'])
PY
)
export TOKEN

Do not print tokens to logs. /health checks the proxy process, not this token or upstream AI connectivity.

  • Admin authority is read from the file, not passed in argv. The token printed by Python is captured into a shell variable.

docs.title: 3. Use a separate client directory
docs.text:
• Create a separate Codex home so the original login file is not overwritten.
  • Parse the token response as JSON rather than inserting it into executable code.
export CODEX_HOME=$(mktemp -d)
chmod 700 "$CODEX_HOME"

python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

base = os.environ['PROXY_DATA_URL']
request = Request(base + '/token', headers={'X-Codex-Token': os.environ['TOKEN']})
with urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
    data = json.load(response)
home = Path(os.environ['CODEX_HOME'])
config = 'openai_base_url = ' + json.dumps(base + '/v1') + '\n'
if 'oauth_access_token' in data:
    auth = {
        'auth_mode': 'chatgpt',
        'OPENAI_API_KEY': None,
        'tokens': {
            'access_token': data['oauth_access_token'],
            'refresh_token': '',
            'id_token': data.get('oauth_id_token', ''),  # Fresh dummy JWT, not the real ID token.
            'account_id': data.get('oauth_account_id', ''),
        },
        'last_refresh': data.get('oauth_last_refresh', ''),
    }
    path = home / 'auth.json'
    with path.open('x', opener=lambda p, flags: os.open(p, flags, 0o600)) as out:
        json.dump(auth, out)
    config += 'chatgpt_base_url = ' + json.dumps(base + '/chatgpt/') + '\n'
(home / 'config.toml').write_text(config)
PY

if [ -f "$CODEX_HOME/auth.json" ]; then
  unset OPENAI_API_KEY
  export CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN_URL_OVERRIDE="$PROXY_DATA_URL/oauth/token?cdx=$TOKEN"
else
  export OPENAI_API_KEY="$TOKEN"
  unset CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN_URL_OVERRIDE
fi
codex
  • OAuth uses the new auth.json; API-key mode uses the placeholder environment value.
  • The API destination is explicit in config.toml.
  • See verified client versions (Japanese).
  • This host process is not isolated from the original home or other host secrets.

docs.title: 4. Revoke and stop
docs.text:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlencode
from urllib.request import Request, ProxyHandler, build_opener
url = os.environ['PROXY_ADMIN_URL'] + '/admin/revoke?' + urlencode({'container': os.environ['SESSION_NAME']})
secret = Path(os.environ['PROXY_ADMIN_SECRET_FILE']).read_text().strip()
request = Request(url, data=b'', headers={'X-Proxy-Admin-Secret': secret})
with build_opener(ProxyHandler({})).open(request, timeout=10) as response:
    response.read()
PY
kill "$PROXY_PID"
  • Revocation and expiry also end active HTTP/WS streams.
  • Remove the temporary CODEX_HOME after checking its path.
  • See the API reference.

docs.title: Additional sandbox controls
docs.text:
• These controls are opt-in.
  • General egress defaults to denial (Japanese); fixed AI routes use separate authorization.
  • Deploy matching node, proxy and worker images before enabling new controls.
  • File restrictions, image digests, idle activity and jobs reject unsupported nodes instead of silently skipping enforcement.
Priority Feature Entry points P0 A1 Effective policy, explanation, preflight policy show/check/explain, Go API P0 A2 Structured denial events policy events, TUI E, Go API P0 A3 Explicit presets --policy-preset, project config P0 A4 Diagnostics and capabilities doctor, capabilities, ProxyCapabilities P1 A5 File read/write restrictions --deny-read, --deny-write P1 A6 Exec/files/jobs/PTY/session CLI and Go API P1 A7 Lifetime, idle, retention Explicit settings plus reap --watch / Reap P1 A8 Environment locks, hooks, readiness environment lock, launch settings P1 A9 Independent clones and recovery --clone-dir, artifact, files API P1 A10 Fixed origin/path/header credential broker --credential-routes, Go callbacks P1 A11 SSH/JVM, upstream proxy, custom CA Compatibility flags and proxy settings Outside these additional controls Features Mandatory defaults File masks, clones and automatic deletion Additional network features TLS MITM and live policy changes Additional execution backends VM snapshots/forks, new OS backends and remote multi-user services

docs.title: Inspect and configure network policy
docs.text:
oaiso policy check --json
oaiso policy show --worker WORKER --json
oaiso policy explain api.example.com:443 --resolve --json
oaiso policy events --worker WORKER --follow --json
oaiso policy presets
oaiso run --policy-preset api --egress-allow-domain api.example.com -d
oaiso run --policy-preset dependencies -d
oaiso run --policy-preset offline -d
oaiso proxy configure
  • Worker inspection reads its actual selected proxy configuration and policy ID.
  • Without --worker, commands inspect host settings for new workers.
  • Explanation never opens a connection.
  • Without --resolve, an allowed decision covers only the hostname and port.

  • With it, every DNS answer is checked; connection establishment repeats those checks.

  • offline and test disable general egress while preserving fixed AI routes.

  • Configured fixed credential-broker routes also remain available independently of general egress rules.
  • dependencies selects common npm, Python and Go registries; api requires explicit domains.

  • Presets cannot widen the host allowlist or override denials/private-address blocking.

  • In the existing TUI, P opens proxy settings and E opens denial history.

  • Standalone proxy configure works without a running node.
  • It edits the six allow/deny lists, empty-list default denial, upstream proxy URL and CA path, validates destinations and saves without exposing secrets or overwriting unrelated settings.
  • Concurrent edits are detected.
  • Unsupported multiline arrays are rejected safely and can be edited in a text editor.
  • Saving does not update running proxies.

  • Drain workers and explicitly recreate the selected proxies to apply changes.

  • Denial events contain time, reason code, observed source address, destination authority and policy ID.

  • They exclude paths, queries, headers and credentials.
  • Egress proxy history is shared by its workers; source addresses are not authenticated run identities.
  • Use separate proxies for cases requiring separate history.
  • The in-process ring retains 512 records; CLI/API read the last 1000 retained console lines.
  • Each proxy process writes at most 100000 events, emits event_log_limit, then stops writing events to bound diagnostic disk use.
  • This is diagnostic history rather than a persistent audit log across proxy recreation.

docs.title: Stop communication and quarantine
docs.text:
To stop communication from an existing worker, run these commands on the host:

oaiso policy quarantine --worker WORKER
oaiso policy show --worker WORKER --json
  • policy revoke is an alias. This stops ALL execution in the selected worker, including general HTTP/CONNECT, fixed AI communication, background jobs and agents.
  • Other workers and shared proxies remain running.
  • The quarantine operation retains the workspace, managed worktree, container and logs.
  • Existing retention policies through reap and explicit deletion still apply; export artifacts that need longer preservation.

  • Saving settings or using ordinary stop does not quarantine a worker.

  • An updated node durably records the restart prohibition in its private OCI record before stopping without a grace period.

  • The node rejects start, VM start, exec and background-job execution, and completes interrupted stops during node recovery.
  • Accepted stops continue after a client disconnect with a node-owned 90-second deadline.
  • A different client's StateDir or replaying the same RequestID cannot clear it.
  • This requires a supporting node; reclaim retained workers before downgrading to an older node.

  • Check worker-quarantine-v1; unsupported nodes reject the operation.

  • Success requires the node's stop acknowledgment, stopped/quarantined status, AI placeholder revocation and Kata reservation release.

  • Lost responses, failed stops or credential-management failures return errors; retry the same worker.

  • A persisted request whose stop is unconfirmed reports quarantine_pending, and destination explanation cannot claim completed denial.

  • Resume with a new worker and RequestID under the new policy.

  • Unquarantine is not provided. v0.0.4 supports explicit live egress changes while worker execution continues.
  • VM termination stops further communication from the guest.
  • It cannot undo operations already accepted by a remote service and does not wait for every upstream socket in the shared egress proxy to close.
  • Preserve artifacts before reclaiming the retained worker with ordinary rm / RemoveRequest; removing a managed worktree also deletes that worktree.

docs.title: Files, execution and recovery
docs.text:
oaiso run --deny-read /workspace/.env --deny-write /workspace/config -d
oaiso exec --workdir /workspace --env MODE=test WORKER -- npm test
oaiso exec -it WORKER -- bash
oaiso files get WORKER src/main.go --local main.go.copy
oaiso files put WORKER input.json --local input.json
oaiso files list WORKER src
oaiso jobs start WORKER -- sh -c 'npm test'
oaiso jobs list WORKER
oaiso jobs logs WORKER JOB_ID --offset 0
oaiso jobs kill WORKER JOB_ID
oaiso artifact diff WORKER --output changes.patch
oaiso artifact commit WORKER --message 'Save staged changes'
oaiso run --clone-dir /absolute/new-copy -d
  • File restrictions use OCI masked/readonly paths below /workspace/.
  • Targets must already exist as regular files/directories inside the workspace; symlinks and resolutions outside it are rejected.
  • These are not inherited rules for future files, nor inode labels for aliases/hardlinks.
  • Avoid exposing the same sensitive content through additional mounts.
  • File APIs execute with guest Python 3, reject symlinks in every component, accept regular files up to 64 MiB, and atomically replace uploads in the same directory.
  • Directory listings allow at most 10000 entries.

  • VM validation and guest permissions remain enforced.

  • PTY streams combine stdout/stderr.

  • Streaming executions/sessions end on cancellation or disconnection.
  • Background jobs continue after client disconnection, with state and shim-owned logs recovered after node restart.
  • They retain at most 16 MiB of combined output while draining subsequent output.
  • Each logs call returns up to 1 MiB with the next offset and truncation status.

  • Finished jobs remain until worker removal; the node retains at most 4096 execution sessions.

  • Independent clones copy committed content without hardlinking Git objects.

  • Destinations must be new absolute paths.
  • Clones remain for recovery after launch failure or worker removal; retries never silently adopt an existing directory.
  • Diff exports tracked staged/unstaged changes relative to HEAD.
  • Retrieve untracked files explicitly, and stage desired changes/configure guest Git identity before committing.

docs.title: Lifecycle and reproducibility
docs.text:
oaiso run --max-lifetime 2h --idle-timeout 30m --retention 24h -d
oaiso reap --dry-run
oaiso reap --watch
oaiso environment lock IMAGE --source Dockerfile --source package-lock.json
oaiso run --image IMAGE --environment-lock codex-dock.lock.json -d
oaiso run --start-hook 'npm ci' --readiness 'test -f node_modules/.package-lock.json' --readiness-timeout 2m -d
  • Lifecycle limits require reap --watch or periodic Go API Reap calls.
  • No host service is installed automatically; limits stop being applied while the supervisor is down.
  • Idle means time since management execution activity, not guest CPU/filesystem activity.
  • Updated nodes protect registered jobs and exec/PTY sessions. Use --protect-main or bounded activity renewals below for other known work; guest CPU/filesystem activity is not inferred.
  • Explicit maximum lifetime can still stop busy workers.
  • Stop revokes tokens; removal uses existing ownership checks and deletion journals.

  • Zero retention never deletes a worker.

  • Environment locks pin the node OCI image digest and SHA-256 hashes of explicitly selected source files.

  • New lock files are created exclusively.
  • Source or image changes reject launch.
  • Include dependency lockfiles to cover package versions.
  • Start hooks run sequentially inside the guest after auth setup and before agent startup; launch completes after the readiness probe succeeds.
  • Failures/deadlines roll back launch.
  • The default hook/probe deadline is 60 seconds, within the existing 180-second launch deadline.

  • Older images without the support label reject hooks.

  • Project [run] supports policy_preset, deny_read, deny_write, max_lifetime, idle_timeout, retention, argv arrays for start_hooks/readiness, and readiness_timeout.

  • Host secrets, extra mounts, runtime and proxy endpoints remain host settings.

docs.title: Credentials and compatibility
docs.text:
• oaiso proxy run --credential-routes /absolute/private-routes.json mounts a 0600 host JSON file read-only into the auth proxy alone.
  • The egress proxy remains credential-free.
  • Example values are synthetic:
[{"Name":"service","Upstream":"https://api.example.com","Paths":["/v1"],"Methods":["GET","POST"],"Header":"X-Service-Key","Prefix":"","Provider":"openai","Secret":"HOST_SECRET"}]
  • ExactPaths adds exact matching (v0.0.4). Existing Paths include descendants; both allowlists are combined. See examples.
  • Guests send live placeholder Bearer tokens to http://AUTH_PROXY/broker/service/v1/....
  • Fixed HTTPS origin, path boundaries, method and provider are checked before injecting credentials.
  • Encoded paths, WebSockets and following upstream redirects are disallowed.
  • Secrets are never returned by a credential retrieval API.
  • Only configure trusted upstream APIs: an upstream that echoes its received secret can expose it.
  • Changes require drain/recreation.
  • Embedders can also use StartCredentialBroker with CredentialRoute.Secret callbacks, explicitly arranging listeners and worker network placement.
oaiso run --ssh-proxy --jvm-proxy --ca-bundle /absolute/extra-ca.pem -d
oaiso proxy run --upstream-proxy http://proxy.example.com:3128 --ca-bundle /absolute/extra-ca.pem
  • SSH uses a GIT_SSH_COMMAND CONNECT helper through the egress policy.
  • Host SSH keys/agent sockets are not shared automatically.
  • JVM HTTP(S) proxy properties are opt-in.
  • Worker CA bundles extend system trust for curl, Python and Node.
  • When Java and keytool are installed, the worker copies the system JVM truststore into its HOME and imports the additional certificates.
  • Proxy CA bundles extend system roots for both HTTP and WebSocket TLS verification.
  • Proxy chaining sends CONNECT to locally verified destination IPs and preserves private-IP blocking.
  • Credential-bearing upstream proxy URLs are rejected.

docs.title: Go API and performance
docs.text:
• The Go API adds Policy, ExplainPolicy, PolicyEvents, execution working directories/environments/TTY, StartSession/Resize, file and job operations, diff recovery and Reap.
  • Existing methods remain available.

  • Probe node and proxy capabilities separately.

  • The network-policy benchmark identified per-request linear domain scans and repeated IP parsing.

  • Compiled domain indexes preserve existing domain/IP matching semantics, covered by equivalence tests.
  • For 1000 domains, three runs on the same host measured 65.9–181 µs, 48112 B and 1002 allocations per check before, versus 152–153 ns, 0 B and 0 allocations after.
  • These are policy checks, not end-to-end network latency.
  • Reproduce with:
go test ./internal/networkpolicy -run '^$' -bench . -benchmem -count=3
  • TUI logs append incrementally instead of rebuilding history on each write, with 2000 lines and approximately 4 MiB per segment.
  • Polling stops when the UI exits.

The verification record distinguishes fixture tests, native Kata acceptance, and external-service tests.

docs.title: Model authorization and staged startup
docs.text:
• Use repeated oaiso proxy run --allow-model model-id, host [proxy].allowed_models, or CaseProxyOptions.AllowedModels to restrict a whole auth proxy to exact submitted model IDs.
  • Empty preserves legacy behavior.
  • The immutable configuration requires draining workers and recreating the proxy to change.

  • ProxyCapabilities reports support and active enforcement separately.

  • When enabled, authenticated POST requests are checked before credential injection or upstream I/O.

  • Only JSON bodies up to 8 MiB are accepted; duplicate keys, case variants of model, invalid JSON, compressed bodies and encoded paths are rejected.
  • The only allowed query is exact beta=true on Claude Messages/count_tokens; every other query is denied.
  • The original checked bytes are forwarded and redirects are not followed.
  • Supported paths are /v1/responses, /v1/responses/compact, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/moderations, /chatgpt/codex/responses, /chatgpt/codex/responses/compact, /anthropic/v1/messages, and /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens.
  • All other AI paths, model-listing/batch/file APIs and WebSockets are denied.
  • Clients must support HTTP.
  • This controls the submitted ID, not upstream alias resolution.

  • Custom broker routes, general egress and separately supplied credentials have separate policies; disable or restrict egress and do not configure alternative AI broker routes when model enforcement is mandatory.

  • Create materializes a Kata worker without starting a VM, hooks or agent or issuing a live worker token.

  • It still creates networks, snapshots and a host reservation; defer Create too if resource allocation requires approval.
  • Remove abandoned workers explicitly.
  • Maximum lifetime counts from creation, including any approval wait.
  • Create and Launch cannot share a request ID; retries of the same operation keep the same ID.
  • Start verifies isolation, activates the token and waits for hooks/readiness.
  • After cancellation or failure, reconcile with Request/Get and use a fresh context for cleanup.
  • Launch retains its combined behavior.

docs.title: Supervised collection and memory observation
docs.text:
• The optional systemd user unit deploy/kata/codex-dock-reaper.service runs the installed /usr/local/bin/oaiso reap --watch and restarts on failure after five seconds.
  • Copy it to ~/.config/systemd/user/, reload the user manager and explicitly enable/start the unit.
  • Monitor its journal and status.
  • An administrator must configure user linger if it needs to survive logout.
  • Nothing is enabled automatically.

  • Multi-case products should periodically call Reap through clients holding their own admin credentials and monitor failures.

  • Updated nodes protect pending execs, active exec/PTY sessions and detached jobs against idle collection, checking atomically with stopping so newly started work is protected too.

  • Use --protect-main for the primary process or bounded activity renewals for work known to the caller; neither infers guest CPU/filesystem activity.

  • Explicit maximum lifetime still applies to busy workers.

  • ResourceUsage returns a verified running VM's host cgroup current memory, optional peak and OOM-kill count separately from guest/host capacity budgets.

  • These are not guest RSS.
  • The guest budget is the worker cgroup limit, separate from total VM RAM shown by /proc/meminfo.
  • The standard default and small guest 1 GiB / host 2 GiB profile remain unchanged.
  • An explicit compact profile provides guest 512 MiB / host 768 MiB, one CPU and 512 PIDs for lightweight tasks.
  • Select CLI --profile-size compact or Go Profile: "compact" after querying Profiles on an updated node.
  • This is not a guarantee that large dependency installs/builds fit; measure product-specific workloads, concurrency, peaks and OOM events.
  • CLI vm inspect --json exposes the same host observations.

docs.title: Operator resource profiles
docs.text:
• v0.0.4: connection, bandwidth, FD and block I/O limits. ResourcePolicies(ctx) exposes complete profiles; ResourceUsage.Policy reports the running contract. Proxy TCP limits are separate from AI request budgets.

  • PID limits are configured per profile.

  • For example, oaiso profile define compact-256 --base compact --pids-limit 256 prints a JSON array with compact's CPU/memory budgets and a 256-PID ceiling.
  • It does not edit files or node configuration.
  • If definitions already exist, add the generated element to their array.
  • oaiso profile --node --json queries built-in and registered profiles on the running node; oaiso profile compact-256 --node displays one selected budget.

  • Without --node, the command continues to display built-in defaults.

  • Built-in standard, small and compact budgets are unchanged.

  • Operators can register additional CPU, guest/host memory and PID combinations in a root-owned JSON file with no group/world write permission.
  • Load it with node serve --resource-profiles /etc/codex-dock/resource-profiles.json:
[{"name":"batch","cpu_cores":2,"guest_memory_bytes":536870912,"host_memory_bytes":805306368,"pid_limit":256}]
  • Names start with a lowercase letter and contain lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, up to 63 characters.
  • The file permits 32 definitions and 64 KiB; duplicate or built-in names are rejected.
  • Bounds are 1–64 CPUs, 512–2048 MiB guest memory, host memory at least 256 MiB above guest memory and at most 3072 MiB, and 64–4096 PIDs.
  • Memory must be MiB-aligned.

  • These settings stay within pinned Dragonball assets and retain mandatory host/guest startup verification.

  • Query client.Profiles(ctx) before selecting Profile: "batch".

  • CLI callers use --profile-size batch or global run.profile_size; completion queries the node.

  • The package-level cxd.Profiles() returns built-in defaults only.

  • Non-512 PID profiles require the updated guest hook and schema-v2 metadata bound to that image.

  • prepare_guest.py build generates these assets; runtime-lock checks the image SHA256 and pins matching metadata as guest-policy.
  • Legacy images/manifests retain 512 behavior.
  • Registering non-512 limits on unsupported assets fails node startup.
  • Check dynamic-pid-profiles-v1 and operator-resource-profiles-v1.

  • The node sets an OCI annotation and bootstrap verifies the actual guest limit before activating credentials, using the pinned Kata hook state.

  • Drain existing VMs before switching/resealing guest images.

  • Allocation records pin the full custom budget.
  • Adding names does not change asset stamps, but file changes require a node restart.
  • Drain every reservation using a definition before modifying or deleting it: retained reservations cannot be reinterpreted.
  • Restore the old definition before recovery if it was changed accidentally.

  • Deployment and service restart are not automatic.

  • When resealing, use runtime-lock --logger /absolute/current/codex-dock-io-logger to select the matching logger explicitly.

  • An older helper selected through PATH may lack bounded-job logging options; pin the matching node-bundle helper.

docs.title: Primary-process protection and activity leases
docs.text:
• Available: v0.0.4; requires matching CLI/node support.
  • Existing idle defaults remain unchanged. Explicitly protect workers that need it.
Setting Protected interval On expiry/completion run --protect-main Primary process running or paused Normal retention after exit; interactive waiting also counts as running activity WORKER --ttl 2m Two minutes from the node-confirmed time Missing renewals expire; last activity and idle policy govern collection activity WORKER --ttl 0s Releases the renewable lease Release time becomes the last activity --max-lifetime Independent of both protections May stop busy workers
  • Renew from the operator CLI or host Go API; no management socket/upstream credentials enter VMs.
  • TTL is an integer 0–300 seconds. Renew sooner than expiry and monitor failures.
  • The node persists protection/expiry across node restarts. VM restart clears the previous renewable lease.
  • The final node-side idle decision is atomic. Unknown state, persistence failure or an inconsistent acknowledgement is not success.
  • Run reap --watch or periodic Go API Reap calls to enforce lifecycle limits.

On a configured execution host, protect a one-hour primary command from idle collection:

oaiso run --name long-job --detach --keep --idle-timeout 5m --protect-main --max-lifetime 2h --exec 'sleep 3600'
oaiso reap --dry-run

Replace my-worker with an existing worker name to renew an activity lease:

oaiso activity my-worker --ttl 2m

Example output (illustrative timestamp):

{"worker":"my-worker","active_until":"2026-10-24T12:02:00Z"}

Release protection separately:

oaiso activity my-worker --ttl 0s
  • Go API: LaunchRequest.Lifecycle.ProtectMain = true, client.Heartbeat(ctx, workerID, 2*time.Minute).
  • Project/host configuration: [run] protect_main = true.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Boundary Implementation Worker isolation Separate guest kernel with Kata runtime-rs / Dragonball Admission Root node verifies assets, host processes and resource limits before releasing user code Failed checks Stop startup; no fallback to runc or QEMU

docs.title: Worker boundary
docs.text:
Control Default User Non-root; caller's UID/GID Capabilities All sets cleared Guest restrictions NoNewPrivs=1, Seccomp=2 Guest resources 1 CPU, 2 GiB memory, 512 PIDs Host VM envelope 1 CPU, 3 GiB memory, no swap, 512 PIDs Network No direct internet, host or peer access; selected proxies only Management No node/containerd/BuildKit sockets or allocation records in workers
  • Verified Kata workers: Codex's inner sandbox uses danger-full-access to avoid nested namespace/seccomp conflicts.
  • Agent approval settings remain separate.

  • Shared files remain accessible under the selected mount permissions.

  • v0.0.4: TCP admission, per-source bandwidth, guest per-process FD and host block I/O ceilings. Opt-in controls; socket IP accounting is not execution authentication, FD ceilings are per process, and cached/tmpfs I/O is outside block limits.

docs.title: Storage and worker-visible fields
docs.text: Information Handling Real API keys and OAuth access/refresh/ID tokens Retained by the auth proxy; never returned to workers Worker credentials Short-lived placeholders Codex ID field Fresh dummy JWT: account ID, plan and FedRAMP flag only Original JWT headers/signature, email, user IDs and arbitrary claims Never forwarded Dummy JWT Client metadata only; not used for upstream authentication Egress proxy Receives no real credentials

docs.title: Acquisition, refresh and existing workers
docs.text:
• Initial acquisition and refresh return only selected fields.
  • Refresh errors retain HTTP status and known CLI recovery codes.
  • Issuer bodies and transport error details are not forwarded.
  • Tests: pinned CLI verification (Japanese).
  • Existing files/logs are not automatically erased: update the proxy, then stop and recreate old workers.

docs.title: Files and mounts
docs.text:
Item Contract Legacy auth files Caller UID/GID, private HOME, read-only mounts; owner-only 0600 retained Independent profiles No host auth mounts/environment; only the selected 0700 directory mounted read-write for refresh Credentials and lock files 0600; CAS, fsync and atomic rename Worker restart Verify profile and connection generation Capabilities and source modes No added capabilities or source-permission changes Admin authority Optional separate 0600 file, read-only mount into auth only; value stays out of argv Worker shares CLI rejects profile-storage overlaps; embedding callers must also keep credentials/admin authority outside shares At-rest encryption New v0.0.3+ login profiles default to Secret Service plus age/HMAC-SHA256; explicit passphrase mode remains available. No ciphertext or keys in work VMs
  • Trusted control environments may run inside WSL or a Linux VM.
  • Untrusted work VMs must never receive real credentials.
  • Requirements and deployment checks: WSL, VMs and headless systems.

docs.title: Encryption limits
docs.text:
• Protect inactive credential files; host root/same-UID process access, live memory, swap and outer VM snapshots are outside this protection.
  • Never store a passphrase alongside ciphertext. Lost keys require reauthentication.
  • Unlock failure never switches to host credentials, plaintext or another backend. Coexisting migration records fail closed.
  • Keyring storage encryption/locking depend on OS configuration.
  • Usage, specification, verification gaps.

docs.title: Token and admin boundaries
docs.text: Condition Behavior HTTP / WebSocket AI requests Validate issued, unexpired token before contacting upstream Revocation, expiry or replacement Cancel active streams and tunnels Admin operations Separate listener, unreachable from worker networks

docs.title: Trusted host operators
docs.text:
Item Trust or verification Node socket / BuildKit access Root-equivalent; operators choose images, commands and host mounts Runtime assets, tools and configuration Pinned in a root-owned manifest Manifest Does not replace release provenance or checksum verification Asset validation Reread and hash every asset on every validation Parallel readers At most GOMAXPROCS and four readers per validation Timestamp cache Never used to skip verification cgroup.kill recovery Verify all occupants of a dedicated resource group first Other processes Do not adopt arbitrary PIDs or other products' VMs

Measurement guide

docs.title: Communication and authorization
docs.text:
Item Limit or default Worker-to-auth-proxy traffic v0.0.4 managed proxies use TLS 1.3 and execution-bound client certificates; usage/migration. General egress retains HTTP proxy transport Worker token binding Managed TLS routes verify token and current execution public key. A copied token alone is insufficient. A compromised guest retains its own allowed authority. Custom legacy HTTP proxies remain unchanged General egress Default deny unless the host explicitly disables it Empty destination grants Disconnect general egress Worker-specific allowlists Select policy-specific proxies; identical policies can share Rule updates v0.0.4: explicit proxy-wide live changes, with generation checks, termination confirmation and fail-closed persistence; no automatic config reload Model authorization Opt-in at the host auth proxy; a CLI model flag alone does not enforce authorization Shared files / Git metadata Remain writable where explicitly shared read-write
  • Model routes, WebSocket denial and separate paths: additional controls.

docs.title: Quarantine
docs.text:
Operation or condition Effect policy quarantine / Go API Quarantine Stop one worker and durably prohibit restart at the node Work terminated Jobs, general communication and AI communication Workspace Retained; create a new worker to resume under new rules Error Does not establish completed isolation; retry
