docs.title: Qualify candidate updates
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4. Use an isolated candidate checkout and test images.
  • Never changes current pins, baseline or releases automatically.
Stage Checks Meaning Static Existing monitored definitions/CLI declarations No unreviewed monitored drift; runtime remains untested plan Static comparison and capture/checkout pin match Produces a plan, qualification remains pending run: CLI Both real CLIs, fresh HOME, environment allowlist Synthetic API/OAuth, proxy/refresh/SSE/tool fixtures run: Kata Compiles acceptance from this checkout; disposable node setup/network/diagnostics/broker/usage/update/recovery Actual guest CLI versions, Codex SSE and Claude tool+SSE against synthetic upstreams
  • Required skipped/missing cases never pass.
  • Records SHA-256 for capture, binaries, image archive, bundle manifests, acceptance executable/log, plus commit/tracked-patch/script hashes.
  • These are operator diagnostics, not signed provenance.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Asset Requirement Isolated checkout Exact candidate versions in both docker/sandbox/Dockerfile ARGs; keep normal main unchanged Capture and CLI binaries Static capture procedure; same versions, staged privately without global CLI updates Developer tools Go, uv-managed Python 3.12, populated Go module cache; fixture runs use GOPROXY=off Real Kata assets Setup/update/recovery test assets: two bundles, image archive, test node and runtime cache; matching CLI/proxy protocol/build versions Worker Both candidate CLIs and current entrypoint Synthetic proxy Test-only internal/authproxy fixture executable image; no real credentials

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
From the candidate checkout root, after capturing .kata-verification/contracts/candidate.json:

uv run --no-project --no-config --managed-python --python 3.12 \
  --with-requirements requirements-contracts.txt python scripts/qualify-upstream.py plan \
  --candidate .kata-verification/contracts/candidate.json \
  --out .kata-verification/candidate-plan
Result Action pending, exit 0 Plan only; no CLI/runtime compatibility verdict hold, exit 1 Review static.md; align candidate checkout pins/capture/images if mismatched error, exit 2 Repair acquisition/parsing/prerequisites; retain current version
  • Output must be a new directory under this checkout's .kata-verification/.
  • To continue a reviewed static hold, explicitly supply --reviewed-static-sha256 with the reviewed static.json digest. Never acknowledge unread differences.
  • Baseline comparison may retrieve fixed public URLs. Fixtures do not perform live provider login/inference/OAuth refresh.

docs.title: Run the complete qualification
docs.text:
Replace asset paths/tags with your prepared fixtures. Docker is only the disposable outer host; product workers use Kata.

uv run --no-project --no-config --managed-python --python 3.12 \
  --with-requirements requirements-contracts.txt python scripts/qualify-upstream.py run \
  --candidate .kata-verification/contracts/candidate.json \
  --out .kata-verification/candidate-run \
  --codex .kata-verification/contracts-tools/node_modules/.bin/codex \
  --claude .kata-verification/contracts-tools/node_modules/.bin/claude \
  --bundle dist/node-bundle-a --next-bundle dist/node-bundle-b \
  --images .kata-verification/setup-e2e/images.tar \
  --cache .kata-verification/setup-e2e/cache \
  --proxy-image oaiso-candidate-proxy:verification \
  --network-proxy-image oaiso-candidate-fixture:verification \
  --worker-image oaiso-candidate-worker:verification \
  --node-image codex-dock-setup-node:verification
  • Pass: exit 0, qualification.json has status: pass, both runtime stages pass, and adopted: false.
  • Failure retains pins/baseline. Inspect stage logs and retry corrected assets with a new output directory.
  • Controller reclaims only its own node/volume, leaving shared host services/workers unchanged.
  • Adoption, baseline/pin changes and release remain separate explicit work.
  • Scheduled CI creates the static result and plan artifact only; no KVM/live login/inference. Live subscriptions, provider production behavior, billing and WSL require separate validation.
  • Keep generated captures/binaries/raw logs out of Git; record verified scope in testing.

docs.title: Dependency checks and remediation
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Checked 2026-10-24 on Linux amd64, all Go packages.
  • Dependency updates, applicability review and boundary checks are included in v0.0.4.
  • govulncheck v1.9.0, Go 1.27.3. No finding exclusions or database modifications.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Target Symbol findings Interpretation Pre-age commit 1168123 19 Historical baseline age plus HTTP/2 patches, published v0.0.3 15 Reproduced before this change Current dependency updates 2 Patched versions remove 13 findings Remaining two 2 Daemon plugin functionality; reviewed execution configuration lacks the required features
  • This is not a zero-finding or vulnerability-free result. Both remaining findings stay visible.
  • Static findings, applicability and successful exploitation are different questions. This is not a completed repository-wide security audit.
  • New database entries, other OS/runtime configurations or dependency changes may change the result.

docs.title: Updated dependencies
docs.text:
Go module Previous v0.0.4 Findings removed containerd SDK v2.1.5 v2.2.9 8 gRPC v1.78.0 v1.83.1 2 OpenTelemetry v1.40.0 v1.44.0 1 moby/sys/user v0.4.0 v0.4.1 1 SELinux library v1.12.0 v1.13.1 1
  • Related API/runtime-spec/instrumentation/compression modules follow Go's dependency resolution; go.mod/go.sum updated.
  • gRPC requires OpenTelemetry v1.44.0; the selected containerd SDK requires SELinux v1.13.1.
  • SDK v2.2.9 includes fixes for all eight reviewed findings without increasing the minimum Go version.
  • Minimum Go 1.26.0, development/CI Go 1.27.3 and pinned daemon 2.4.2 are unchanged. Running host services/distributions were not updated.
  • age v1.3.2 and the existing patched x/net v0.60.0 remain pinned.

docs.title: Removed finding IDs
docs.text:
Module IDs containerd SDK GO-2026-6791, GO-2026-6597, GO-2026-5758, GO-2026-5622, GO-2026-5475, GO-2026-5378, GO-2026-5338, GO-2026-5064 gRPC GO-2026-6348, GO-2026-6061 OpenTelemetry GO-2026-5506 moby/sys/user GO-2026-6686 SELinux GO-2025-4098

See each ID in the Go vulnerability database. Removal of a finding does not establish that the affected daemon feature was previously used.

docs.title: Remaining findings and applicability
docs.text:
ID and primary advisory Required condition Observed product boundary GO-2026-4887, AuthZ plugin advisory Daemon forwarding request bodies to an AuthZ plugin No daemon/AuthZ implementation linked; SDK HTTP client/types communicate with the dedicated node GO-2026-4883, plugin installation advisory Daemon privilege validation during plugin installation No daemon/plugin implementation linked; node does not provide plugin APIs
  • Both are unreviewed module-wide entries covering all versions of the legacy SDK module. Primary advisories explicitly exclude configurations not using the affected features.
  • Execution uses the containerd/Kata node. Legacy SDK v28.5.2 remains a compatibility dependency, not a daemon installation/runtime.
  • TestNativeEntrypointsDoNotLinkDockerDaemon checks CLI/guard/logger/public Go API dependencies stay within legacy SDK client, API types and stdcopy.
  • TestNodeRejectsDaemonPluginEndpointsBeforeRPC checks plugin/auth/unknown endpoints return 404 before RPC, for versioned/unversioned URLs and malformed bodies.
  • Inspection also identified and fixed unknown API paths falling through to container handling.
  • A new SDK with substantially changed client/API types is a separate migration, not a required remediation for these two daemon conditions. Adding daemon functionality invalidates this applicability assessment.

docs.title: Verification scope
docs.text:
Check Coverage Dependency analysis Before 15, after 2; 13 removed; no exclusions Go Build, full race tests, vet, lint, module checksum verification Minimum Go version CLI builds with Go 1.26.0 Added regressions No daemon implementation linked; unsupported APIs rejected before RPC Cross-build macOS arm64/amd64 and Linux arm64; not runtime acceptance on those systems Acceptance Follow-up network/revocation suite passes on real Kata. No full eight-suite rerun, live-account or WSL acceptance

See existing verification scope (Japanese). Automated tests here do not establish new real-runtime acceptance.

docs.title: Repeat the analysis
docs.text:
• Requires the development environment, Go 1.27.3. Run as an ordinary user from repository root.
  • Fetches public modules/database data; no AI authentication/inference.
  • Installs the tool outside Git-tracked files.
mkdir -p .kata-verification/dependency-tools
GOBIN="$PWD/.kata-verification/dependency-tools" go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@v1.9.0
.kata-verification/dependency-tools/govulncheck ./...
  • With the same database, the two listed findings remain. Text mode returns exit 3 for findings; do not report a clean zero-finding result.
  • Raw logs/JSON/build outputs: .kata-verification/dependency-hardening-20261025/. Large reports and real credentials are not committed.

docs.title: Add or update documentation
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • For contributors editing documentation.
  • To use Oaiso, start with Installation or the quick start.
  • Follow the shared rules in SKILL.md.

docs.title: Choose the content and format
docs.text:
Content Location or format Product overview, installation and basic use README; exclude release changes and new-version announcements Release-specific changes doc/release-notes.md and GitHub Releases Feature usage and limitations Feature documentation, including its first release Improvement plans Describe this product's requirements, limits and acceptance criteria; omit named third-party evaluations, rankings and source-size comparisons from public documentation Comparisons and settings Tables Ordered actions Numbered lists Conditions and supporting notes Short bullets, one point per item
  • Write Japanese documentation in simple, concise Japanese; avoid difficult phrasing.
  • Mark each feature's first release, for example Available since v0.0.3. Label features separately when their introduction versions differ.
  • Verify introduction versions against tags and history. Do not confuse the documentation update version with the feature's first release.
  • Label unpublished features Unreleased (main) and replace this label with their first release after publication.

docs.title: Check the explanation
docs.text:
Topic Check Reader and sequence Distinguish first use, upgrades and development; cover prerequisites through cleanup Implementation Compare help, configuration examples and code; distinguish released behavior from main Choices Identify defaults, required and optional settings; show one working path first Privileges and effects Distinguish host/VM, user/admin, shared files, external traffic and deletion scope Success and errors Explain exit status and the next check; give recovery steps and a recheck command Evidence Distinguish starting, storage, connection, inference and artifacts; fixtures, skips and unexecuted tests do not establish live success Duplication Keep details in one place and align navigation, links, translations and configuration examples Secrets Use fake credentials, exclude authentication files and secret logs, and do not add live inference just to check documentation
  • Use oaiso-docs for documentation, or choose another workflow from the skill index.

docs.title: Chapters
docs.text: Chapter Reader's question Contents Getting started How do I run it the first time? Installation, prerequisites, authentication and first worker Guides How do I complete a task? Agents, files, images, credentials, networking and isolation Reference What is the exact interface? CLI, configuration, Go API, Credential Store and auth API Administration How do I maintain the installation? Daily operations, host updates, VM management, migration, troubleshooting and performance Development How does it work and how is it tested? Architecture, networking, upstream compatibility, testing and future work

docs.title: Write a page
docs.text:
1. Start with the purpose, prerequisites and first action; link required tools to their official installation instructions.
  2. Use numbered steps and commands for procedures.
  3. Use tables for choices, settings, defaults and limitations.
  4. Keep supporting bullets short, with one point per item.

  5. Link exact flags and contracts to Reference; link detailed verification records to Development.

  6. Distinguish implemented, planned, verified and unverified behavior.

  7. Keep real credentials and tokens out of examples.
  8. Add new feature pages to both their guide category and navigation.
  9. Keep chapter classifications aligned across languages; label Japanese-only pages.
  10. Preserve existing page paths and heading links.

docs.title: Write command and output examples
docs.text:
Item Convention Copyable commands bash blocks; keep prompts such as $ and output separate Human-readable output A following text block, with success indicators and the next check JSON output json blocks; label formatting or excerpts Environment-specific values Identify example versions, IDs, PIDs, times and paths Silent success State that success produces no output and add a verification command Errors Show the failing check, recovery clue and recheck Authentication and startup Distinguish storage success, preparation, execution and task success Multiple commands Make the whole block runnable from top to bottom; state the user, directory and required substitutions first Conditional or alternative paths Give each path its own heading and code block; do not include commented-out alternatives in the same block Interactive input, shell changes or re-login Split blocks at the boundary and explain where to continue
  • Check local output with the real CLI, an isolated HOME and fake credentials.
  • Check host-dependent output against implementation and existing evidence; adding an example does not establish live host validation.
  • For long build logs, show only useful sections and label omitted content.

docs.title: Separate conditional command blocks
docs.text:
• Prerequisites: the host and selected agent's credentials are ready. Run as a normal user from the project directory.
  • Choose exactly one block. Run its commands together, from top to bottom.

For Codex

oaiso init --agent codex
oaiso codex --version

For Claude Code

oaiso init --agent claude
oaiso claude --version

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
• Requires uv. Use managed Python 3.12, as in host setup and CI.
  • Run from the repository root.
uv python install 3.12
uv run --no-project --no-config --managed-python --python 3.12 --with-requirements requirements-docs.txt mkdocs build --strict
  • Check navigation coverage, page links and heading links.
  • Compare commands with the implementation; distinguish syntax checks from live host validation.
  • Check that README has no release changes or announcements and that feature documentation records the correct introduction versions.
  • Check command order, variables and working directories; keep alternative paths and interactive boundaries in separate blocks.
  • Compare command/flag tables with normal subcommand --help; native codex/claude help is forwarded to the agent.
  • Compare allowed keys, types, scope and precedence in both languages, including different global/project hook formats.
  • Walk authentication and update procedures from prerequisites through settings, preparation and verification; link checks alone do not establish runtime correctness.

docs.title: Feature and security improvement candidates
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Baseline: v0.0.6. This page tracks proposals, additional verification and included improvements.
  • P0 establishes guarantees; P1 improves daily use/security; P2 requires measured benefit. Unimplemented proposals have undecided effort and release dates.
  • No named-product evaluation or ranking is published here.
  • Preserve convenient local operation, the authentication proxy, isolation, revocation and cleanup.

docs.title: UX tasks after v0.0.6
docs.text:
Target: unreleased (main).

Task User-facing change Acceptance 1-A Host agent-policy list, search, value sources, and explanations Standalone editor; distinguish built-in and host policies 1-B Clone, edit, inherit, and select a default Review diffs and affected descendants, confirm discard, reject concurrent edits, save with mode 0600 2-A Terminal transport regressions Esc without newline, special keys, UTF-8 paste, ANSI, live resize, restored terminal flags and stdin ownership 2-B Real TUI interactions and layout Small screens, Japanese paste through a PTY, review/save, responsive dashboard after shell exit 3 Stage-specific startup guidance Preserve underlying errors and suggest recovery commands using selected configuration Critical review Mistaken saves, conflicts, misleading recovery, and return failures Real Kata, no secret display, owned-resource cleanup; distinguish live AI inference and physical-terminal visual checks

Interaction design draws on K9s search, Esc and help, VS Code settings scopes, search and reset, and Docker troubleshooting guidance. Oaiso adapts these ideas into source visibility, review before saving, and concrete checks for each startup stage.

Per-worker database disk preserves ordinary HOME and shared workspace coherence Stop/restart, crashes, disk-full recovery and cleanup checked on real Kata. Automatic migration of existing workers and history transfer to another worker remain out of scope P0 Remaining dependency findings Dependency updates and applicability review completed (v0.0.4). Findings reduced from 15 to 2; both concern unused daemon features Automated regressions pass. No finding exclusions; rationale recorded. Follow-up real Kata coverage uses the network/revocation suite P0 Live-account authentication Independent login, auth-only VM and encrypted storage implemented; live accounts/long refresh unverified API/subscription, refresh conflicts, proxy restart, cancellation, active-stream revocation, no secrets in logs/files P0 Network/revocation acceptance Additional coverage completed (v0.0.4). docs.title: Increase security strength
docs.text:
Priority Measure Evidence and intent Verification and residual limits P1 Encrypt VM–proxy traffic and bind authorization to execution origin Implemented (v0.0.4). TLS 1.3 and execution-bound auth-proxy certificates. General egress is outside this feature Copied bearer alone must fail from another origin. A fully compromised VM can still perform its authorized operations P1 Signed distributions, provenance and dependency inventory Implemented (v0.0.4). Signed distributions, provenance, SBOM and version floor. Release verification checks the published signatures and provenance Verify trusted signatures before placement; reject mismatches, unknown keys and unauthorized rollback. Signing-key compromise needs separate controls P1 Retained audit records Implemented (v0.0.4). Durable operation audit: creation/auth changes/policy issue/revocation/deletion outcomes Store IDs/reasons/results, never values; bounded retention, gap detection and leak tests. Local storage alone cannot promise root-resistant integrity P1 Malformed-input, race and failure testing Implemented (v0.0.4). Fuzz/load/race/persistence-fault tests, reusing existing CAS/cleanup coverage Extend existing tests with missing fuzz/race/fault cases; fail closed on connection floods, long streams, crashes and disk-full P2 Protect credential-handling processes At-rest encryption excludes same UID, running memory and swap Evaluate dedicated UID, dump restrictions, unlock expiry and key lifetime; do not promise elimination of all Go memory copies or host-root access P2 Finer network authority Implemented (v0.0.4). Fixed-origin broker: exact paths, CLI methods, TUI, Go API and private file Preserve subtree scopes; reject before reading secrets. General CONNECT TLS inspection and query/body restrictions remain outside scope
  • Real upstream API keys and OAuth access/refresh/ID tokens remain in the authentication proxy.
  • Work-VM execution credentials are short-lived, execution-scoped and proxy-only, unusable for upstream authentication. Host issuing keys never enter work VMs.
  • Encryption does not replace authorization or cleanup. Record coverage/gaps in security.

docs.text: Proposal Contract change Establish first Live network policy v0.0.4: explicit proxy-wide live policy changes; whole-VM quarantine remains separate Generations, apply acknowledgement, existing-connection termination, partial failure/restart recovery Generic TLS decryption/L7 restrictions Guest CA trust and supported protocols Pinning, HTTP/2/gRPC/WS, signed requests, secret echo/logs and overhead Memory snapshots/VM fork Preserve/clone processes, RAM, connections, identity and deadlines Reissue tokens, prevent secret residue, CPU compatibility, avoid duplicate external effects Other OS/multiple hosts/tenants Trusted single-host operator assumption Authentication, authority, quota, placement, mutual authentication, audit and recovery Dedicated credential UID Profile/keyring/service ownership Existing-profile migration, headless/WSL unlock, lock/cleanup and root trust

docs.title: Order of work
docs.text:
1. Prioritize P0 acceptance and dependency work.
  2. Add small increments for usage limits, audit, signed distribution and embedding contracts according to need.
  3. Start performance work with measurements; prototype prestart/persistence to establish cost and benefit.

  4. Reject changes that weaken authentication, isolation, revocation or cleanup.

  5. Already implemented: default-deny egress, token-scoped model restrictions, PID profiles, broker, Create→Start, PTY/files/jobs, independent login and encrypted storage. Do not propose these again as missing features.

  6. Additional controls/Go API first shipped in v0.0.2; independent login, keyring/encryption and consolidated status/distribution updates in v0.0.3. Existing feature pages retain detailed conditions.

docs.title: Workflow and SDK additions
docs.text:
Target: v0.0.4. Implementation adds SDK file/job/checkpoint operations, reviewed artifact bundles, loopback previews, policy proposals and explicit live changes, and checkpoint retention/pins. Feature-specific automated tests and disposable Kata acceptance verify these paths.

  • Live updates are proxy-wide, generation-checked and close existing general HTTP/CONNECT connections before reporting completion.
  • File SDK transfers have a separate 512 KiB bound. Mutating calls are never automatically retried.
  • Retention preserves the existing 16 GiB hard capacity; its byte target is a cleanup target.

docs.title: Local encrypted credential store specification
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Specification for v0.0.3 or later.
  • Usage, Store contract.

docs.title: Defaults and dependencies
docs.text:
Item Contract Default New login profiles use Secret Service; existing profiles and low-level set/import remain unchanged; explicit --encrypt/--plaintext alternatives Location Private product profiles on the control host, outside workspace/clone/additional shares Encrypted data API keys, OAuth access/refresh/ID tokens, credential versions and connection generations Implementation Embed filippo.io/age v1.3.2 in the Go binary External dependencies Passphrase mode needs no network, external age CLI, additional daemon or database Proxy admin authority Separate 0600 file; outside this store and never shared with work VMs Go Minimum 1.26.0; development/CI toolchain 1.27.3. Binary-distribution users need no Go
  • Official age source, format specification, Go API.

docs.title: Format and cryptography
docs.text:
Element Contract File NAME/NAME.vault, a single atomically updated JSON manifest Manifest version Oaiso schema 2, separate from the standard age format version Public metadata Profile name, unlock backend, key ID, public age recipient and protected key file Credential ciphertext Standard binary age stream, base64 encoded in the manifest, encrypted to an X25519 recipient Secret bundle Product-specific age private identity plus an independent random 32-byte authentication key Store authentication HMAC-SHA256 binds the manifest and credential ciphertext Complete reads Consume the age stream through EOF, validating the final chunk and size limit before use
  • Public-key age encryption does not authenticate the sender. The separate authentication key prevents someone knowing only the recipient from replacing stored credentials undetected; protect it together with the private identity.
  • age implements credential/key-bundle encryption. No custom cipher, age recipient or age-format parser is implemented.
  • The whole .vault file is a JSON manifest, not direct input to the age CLI. Interoperability tests extract its age ciphertext and decrypt it with the official CLI.
  • Keeping one file avoids multi-file transactions during ordinary OAuth refresh.

docs.title: Key protection
docs.text:
Method Contract Passphrase Encrypt the secret bundle using an age scrypt recipient; hidden TTY or dedicated FD New scrypt cost logN=17, r=8, p=1, approximately 128 MiB workspace; explicit small-control-host budget Accepted maximum SetMaxWorkFactor(18) prevents unbounded file-supplied KDF work Input limits New passphrases 12–4096 bytes; explicit descriptor >= 3, maximum 4096 bytes Keyring New-login default; store/read-back the bundle through an existing service or an explicit private session Keyring requirements Host secret-tool and user D-Bus; 15-second operation timeout Everyday use Unlock on proxy startup; no repeated prompt while the same proxy is running Refresh cost Reuse the unlocked identity and encrypt to its public recipient; no scrypt per inference/refresh
  • age CLI defaults to logN=18; Oaiso explicitly uses 17 for its 128 MiB budget and accepts reads up to 18. Implementation.
  • No automatic unlocking through a plaintext key alongside ciphertext.
  • OS keyring encryption/locking depend on OS configuration. Unavailable backends never switch to passphrases, plaintext or host credentials.
  • No direct backend-conversion command; reauthenticate into a new profile using the other backend.

docs.title: Proxy and VM boundary
docs.text:
1. Unlock the identity/authentication-key bundle in host CLI memory.
  2. Transfer it to the existing Auth Proxy through a bounded, length-prefixed private stdin stream.
  3. Drop the long-running host command's unlocked references after proxy readiness.
  4. Give work VMs only short-lived, proxy-scoped placeholders.
Boundary Contract argv/environment/configuration/container metadata/ordinary logs No secret bundle or real credentials Stdin protocol Maximum 1024 bytes; reject partial input, disconnect and excessive lengths Proxy reuse Match profile, protected-key fingerprint, connection generation and protocol Older proxy protocol Drain workers and explicitly remove/recreate the authentication proxy Work VMs No ciphertext, identity, authentication key, credential socket or control-host HOME Login-only Kata Separate temporary memory-only collection using the pinned official CLI

docs.title: Persistence and locking
docs.text:
Operation Contract OAuth refresh Cross-process lock and atomic expected-version CAS; retain connection generation Durable save Ciphertext temporary file, fsync, atomic rename and directory fsync Failure/conflict Never acknowledge success; propagate to existing proxy revocation behavior Product lock Stop workers/proxies belonging to this private store; retain work/ciphertext OS keyring lock Does not erase an already-unlocked proxy; run auth profile lock separately Process close Clear owned key/authentication-key byte slices and drop the age identity reference
  • Public credentialstore.Store is unchanged.
  • Go cannot guarantee zeroing every temporary secret copy; bound lifetime, including process termination.

docs.title: Explicit migration
docs.text:
Source Operation Plaintext .json auth profile encrypt NAME; verify age persistence/read-back before deleting plaintext Encrypted schema 1 auth profile migrate-age NAME; unlock using its original backend and explicitly convert Ordinary schema-1 writes/new proxy startup Refuse; no automatic conversion or credential fallback Migration generation Rotate credential/connection versions; old workers cannot be reauthorized Recovery backup Retain NAME.vault.v1-backup with mode 0600; ciphertext only, never loaded automatically Conflicting backup Refuse overwrite; preserve recovery data Retry/interruption Validate using the selected backend and resume; an already-migrated profile does not rotate again Coexisting plaintext/ciphertext Fail closed until explicit migration compares content and completes Passphrase change Reprotect the same identity/authentication key; retain connection generation
  • Argon2id/XChaCha20-Poly1305 remain only in the read-only schema-1 decoder, never new writes.
  • Keyring migration retains the old keyring item for encrypted-backup recovery; operators can remove retired backups/items after verification.
  • Backups still decrypt with old passphrases/keys. Deleted blocks and earlier backups are not securely erased.

docs.title: Protection and verification
docs.text:
• Primary target: reading inactive credential files, disks and backups.
  • Outside this protection: control-host root/same-UID process access, live memory, swap and outer VM snapshots.
  • Local-only storage cannot fully detect a snapshot rolling back keys, ciphertext and generation state together.
  • WSL uses private Linux storage; reject unverified DrvFS/NFS/FUSE filesystems.
  • Results, measurements and remaining checks.

docs.title: Keyring sessions
docs.text:
• User guide: existing desktop service discovery and private headless sessions.
  • The CLI owns foreground D-Bus and GNOME Keyring processes; normal exit, SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP cancel and reap them.
  • Keys stay in the separate private keyring files and proxy memory; no passphrase file or global PAM modification.
  • Share validation rejects keyring storage and filesystem D-Bus socket paths.

docs.title: Network and revocation acceptance
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Additional checks: v0.0.4.
  • Reuses existing tests and local synthetic upstreams; no live accounts.
  • Automated tests, real Kata evidence and unverified conditions are recorded separately.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text:
Condition Automated checks Additional real Kata checks DNS Entire answer set, mixed A/AAAA, answer order, verified-IP dialing, changed answers on later connections, empty answers DNS scenarios use automated fixtures; real Kata destinations use fixed IPs IPv4/IPv6 Private, loopback, link-local, IPv4-mapped and metadata denial Guest HTTP/CONNECT denials and successful public IPv4/IPv6 CONNECT echo Redirect Cannot escape destination grants Allowed IP redirecting to metadata is denied CONNECT Same destination/port restrictions as HTTP; allowed TLS tunnel Active IPv4/IPv6 tunnels end on quarantine SSE Three AI routes × revoke, expiry, reissue, restore and proxy stop Token revocation while the VM runs; closure observed at upstream peers WebSocket Revoke, expiry, reissue, restore and proxy stop Concurrent SSE/WS peers close on revocation Failed stop Node errors, false ACK, persistence failure and unknown state never establish completed quarantine Real successful stop, peer closure and restart denial; failures use automated fault injection CLI reporting Unknown/running/paused/restarting show QUARANTINE PENDING; JSON includes quarantine_pending: true Real post-stop show and explain
  • General and AI traffic have separate authority. AI token revocation does not stop general CONNECT; use policy quarantine to stop all traffic.
  • IPv6 evidence covers proxy destination validation and tunneling, not guest IPv6 address assignment or a live external IPv6 path.
  • A test-only image exposes connection counts, never real API keys or request contents. It is not a production authentication proxy.

docs.title: Run automated checks
docs.text:
• Requires the development tools. Run as an ordinary user at repository root.
  • No live AI authentication or inference.
go test -race ./internal/networkpolicy ./internal/authproxy ./internal/engine ./internal/sandbox ./internal/workeregress ./cmd
  • This alone does not run real Kata acceptance.
  • Main checks: TestMixedDNSFamiliesFailClosedAndPublicAddressesArePinned, TestWorkerSSELeaseEndsOnRevocationAndExpiry, TestWorkerWebSocketLeaseEndsOnRevocationAndExpiry, TestPolicyCommandsNeverReportUnconfirmedStopAsBlocked.
  • Stop failures: TestQuarantinePersistsBeforeStopAndBlocksStartAfterReload, TestQuarantineRequiresUpdatedNodeAndConfirmedTargetStop.

docs.title: Run real Kata acceptance
docs.text:
1. Follow disposable-node preparation (Japanese) to build the setup-test-a/setup-test-b bundles, matching acceptance binary and standard proxy/worker images.
  2. Build the additional test-only proxy with the same setup-test-a version. Do not use it for production authentication.
mkdir -p .kata-verification/network-proxy
CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -c -ldflags "-X github.com/pacificbelt30/codex-dock/internal/buildinfo.Version=setup-test-a" \
  -o .kata-verification/network-proxy/fixture.test ./internal/authproxy
docker build -f deploy/kata/Dockerfile.proxy-fixture \
  --build-arg CODEX_DOCK_BUILD_VERSION=setup-test-a \
  -t oaiso-network-fixture:verification .kata-verification/network-proxy
docker save -o .kata-verification/setup-e2e/network-images.tar \
  codex-dock:kata-guard codex-dock-proxy:policy-verification oaiso-network-fixture:verification
  1. Select network/revocation acceptance. The controller cleans up its own node and volume.
CODEX_DOCK_DISPOSABLE_SETUP=1 uv run --no-project --no-config --managed-python --python 3.12 \
  python scripts/verify-setup.py \
  --bundle dist/node-bundle-a --next-bundle dist/node-bundle-b \
  --images .kata-verification/setup-e2e/network-images.tar \
  --acceptance .kata-verification/setup-e2e/acceptance.test \
  --network-proxy-image oaiso-network-fixture:verification \
  --acceptance-run '^TestKataNetworkRevocation$'
  • Success requires the named suite to pass and no remaining VMs, tasks, containers or dedicated networks after setup/update/recovery.
  • Check acceptance.txt, including upstream peer counts reaching zero for SSE/WS and general traffic.
  • Version mismatch, missing images or unavailable KVM are failures, never passing skips or runc substitutions.
  • Results and evidence: testing (Japanese).

docs.title: Automatically test authentication, network and failure boundaries
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Additional fuzz/load/stop-race coverage: v0.0.4; existing CAS and cleanup tests are reused.
  • Synthetic credentials and local fixtures only. No real accounts or external AI inference.
Boundary Inputs/faults Required behavior Authentication Unissued tokens, malformed headers No upstream work or credential injection Model policy Duplicate/case-variant JSON and trailing values Only permitted models; preserve accepted request bytes Broker URL/path Other origins, traversal, percent encodings, doubled slashes, forbidden methods Fixed origin/path/method scope Destinations IPv4/IPv6/metadata, mixed DNS, malformed authorities No dial to rejected destinations/addresses Management JSON Duplicates, Unicode field aliases, trailing/unknown data, size/depth excess Reject before authentication/Store mutation Token lifetime Negative/oversized/TLS-excess TTL Do not replace existing authority with invalid leases; omitted HTTP TTL uses configured default Persistence Injected ENOSPC, broken audit head, OAuth save failure No fresh budgets/credentials; do not silently reset budgets after recovery Load/long streams 96 concurrent SSE requests and revocation Close existing streams, admit no new upstream work Stop races Concurrent issuance/stop; issue/restore after stop No remaining authority; end expiry-monitor goroutines Store Existing multiprocess CAS/failure tests Reject conflicts and unpublished updates Cleanup/cancel Existing stop failure, deletion journal, lost response/retry tests Keep unknown state explicit and retain cleanup retries

ENOSPC is injected at the persistence boundary; shared disks are never filled. These tests do not claim every transport/policy/Store/failure combination is exhausted.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Prepare the Go toolchain, then run at repository root.

Regular race coverage:

make test

Five bounded fuzz targets:

make security-fuzz
  • Five seconds/two workers per target, plus seed preparation and compilation.
  • Fixed seeds also run with normal tests. Fuzz exploration and full race testing are separate.
  • CI runs both. Reduce and sanitize failures before adding regression inputs; never commit raw private logs/credentials/bulk exploration caches.

docs.title: Real Kata
docs.text:
Use the disposable node procedure.

Scope Selection TLS/network/revocation --acceptance-run '^TestKataWorkerMTLS$' Go API, case isolation, proxy audit --acceptance-run '^TestKataGoAPI$' Encryption/keyring TestKataEncryptedProfile, TestKataKeyringProfile

Signing CI contacts GitHub/Sigstore. Normal upstream CLI contract checks remain offline; real AI authentication/inference is separate. See evidence and limits.

docs.title: Prepare development tools
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Purpose Go, Make and Git Install a prebuilt release Not required; the installer also prepares missing uv/Python Build the CLI, node and helpers from source Required; follow this page Build a product embedding the Go API Go is required in the build environment, which can be separate from the execution host

docs.title: Required tools and official instructions
docs.text:
Tool Purpose or requirement Official instructions or downloads Go go.mod requires at least 1.26.0; builds the CLI, node and helpers Linux installation, downloads and SHA-256 GNU Make Build and test targets Official downloads and documentation Git Source checkout and version control Linux installation curl Download release assets Official download guide uv Isolated host Python and dependency management Installation Python 3.12 Setup, validation and documentation scripts Install Python with uv C compiler Go race tests; also builds the static PID hook during manual Kata preparation GCC installation
  • Python uses uv-managed distributions, rather than a source build of Python itself.
  • The commands below target Ubuntu 26.04 on Linux x86_64. Go uses the official archive; Git, Make and GCC use Ubuntu packages.

docs.title: 1. Prepare basic tools
docs.text:
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y curl ca-certificates git make build-essential

docs.title: 2. Install Go using the official Linux procedure
docs.text:
Skip to step 3 if a suitable Go installation is already available.

  1. Check the stable Linux amd64 archive and SHA-256 on the official download page, then download and verify it.

    curl -fL -o go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz https://go.dev/dl/go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz
echo '65efbc80fdc1fa2cd2631cad5b481777a68e8725f34e89f50fc6ac714e379b40  go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz' | sha256sum --check -
    • 1.27.3 is an example. For another version, change the filename, URL and SHA-256 together.
    • Expected: go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz: OK. Do not continue if verification fails.

  2. After successful verification, remove the existing /usr/local/go tree and extract the archive as instructed by Go.

    sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go
sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz
    • This replaces the toolchain under /usr/local/go. Do not extract over an existing Go tree.

  3. Add the following line to ~/.profile and also run it in the current shell.

    export PATH="/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"

  4. Verify the active installation.

    command -v go
go version

    /usr/local/go/bin/go
go version go1.27.3 linux/amd64
    • The version should match the installed archive. If another Go is selected, check PATH ordering.

docs.title: 3. Prepare uv and Python
docs.text:
Only install uv if it is missing, using its official versioned installer.

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.13.5/install.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
uv python install 3.12
uv --version
uv python find --no-project --no-config --managed-python --system 3.12
  • uv 0.13.5 matches CI. If uv is already installed, only prepare and check Python.
  • The last command should print the absolute path of a uv-managed Python 3.12 executable.
  • The OS Python is retained.

docs.title: Host-managed agent policies
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Available: v0.0.6 and later.

Oaiso can keep Codex and Claude Code defaults for approvals, reasoning, history, and related behavior on the host. Policies live in owner-private ~/.config/codex-dock/agent-policies/config.toml; repositories cannot change host-only fields.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
oaiso agent-policy list
oaiso agent-policy show approve-for-me
oaiso run --agent codex --agent-policy approve-for-me

Built-ins are interactive, approve-for-me, autonomous, review, private, and restricted. The approve-for-me profile selects Codex approvals_reviewer=auto_review and Claude auto. Automated review does not disable the Codex sandbox, Kata VM, or per-worker egress policy.

Select a host default:

oaiso agent-policy init
oaiso agent-policy default approve-for-me
oaiso agent-policy audit
oaiso agent-policy plan

Alternatively set run.agent_policy = "approve-for-me" in the normal global config. Precedence is native agent arguments, explicit Oaiso flags, portable repository settings, global config, host policy, then built-in defaults.

docs.title: Select and edit in the TUI
docs.text:
Available: unreleased (main). Run as your normal user; the editor also works while the node is stopped.

oaiso agent-policy configure
  1. Select a policy. * marks the host default and built-in marks read-only profiles.
  2. Use C to clone a built-in, Tab to move between panes, and / to search settings.
  3. Inspect each value, its source, description, and safety meaning. Enter edits a field; Stage keeps it in the draft. R or Inherit removes the local override.
  4. Use D to stage the host default and Ctrl-S to review changes, warnings, and affected descendants.

  5. In the review, Tab moves to Cancel / Save. Only a successful Save writes the owner-private 0600 file.

  6. Esc returns; leaving with unsaved changes asks whether to discard. Ctrl-R reload behaves the same way.

  7. Concurrent file edits reject saving and retain the draft; inspect the other edit before reloading.
  8. Changes apply to new workers. A global run.agent_policy override is displayed and takes precedence over the host default.
  9. The same editor opens with G from oaiso ui. Editing forms work best with at least 80 columns and 22 rows. Use Tab to reach the explanation pane and arrow keys to scroll it.

docs.title: Edit with the CLI
docs.text:
Clone a built-in and store only the differences:

oaiso agent-policy clone approve-for-me team
oaiso agent-policy set team description "Team default"
oaiso agent-policy set team codex.reasoning_effort high
oaiso agent-policy set team codex.web_search disabled
oaiso agent-policy set team claude.effort high
oaiso agent-policy default team

Use unset to inherit again, diff to compare effective values, and doctor to find redundant or hard-to-maintain inheritance. oaiso agent-policy fields [SEARCH] lists every accepted value and its safety meaning.

Profiles cannot contain arbitrary TOML fragments or agent arguments. Oaiso validates a fixed allowlist and passes structured JSON to the guest, where the entrypoint owns the generated configuration keys.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• full-auto and danger remain strong choices; agent-policy audit reports their risks.
  • Live web features cannot grant destinations denied by Oaiso egress policy.
  • A model is only a default; Auth Proxy model authorization remains authoritative.
  • Verified Kata workers retain the existing Codex danger-full-access inner default because Kata is the primary boundary.
  • Repository oaiso.toml cannot set host-only agent-policy fields.

Directly edited files must use schema version 1 and mode 0600. Run oaiso agent-policy validate and oaiso agent-policy doctor afterward. Unknown keys, invalid enum values, inheritance cycles, and files readable by another user are rejected.

docs.title: Preserve Codex SQLite state
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Available: unreleased (main), for newly created regular Kata workers after updating the matching CLI, node and worker-guard. Existing workers and data are not migrated automatically.

Codex SQLite databases use a private ext4 disk while HOME keeps its usual location. Shared workspace coherence settings remain in place. HOME configuration, authentication placeholders and conversation files retain their locations.

docs.title: Lifetime
docs.text: Operation or condition Stored state Stop/restart the same worker SQLite databases and ordinary HOME retained Restart the node process Retained; missing runtime metadata is regenerated from the same disk Remove the worker, including ordinary run exit cleanup Disk removed too; use --keep to retain the worker Create another worker Separate empty disk, including when reusing a name --read-only-rootfs No state disk; existing temporary HOME behavior, lost when the VM stops Authentication-only VM or runc No private state disk Rootfs checkpoint State disk contents excluded; see checkpoint scope

docs.title: Interactive use and restart
docs.text:
Prerequisites: login/init completed as the regular host user. Use a new worker name, codex-work. This example explicitly retains a worker for shell connections.

  1. Create and connect from the host:
oaiso run --agent shell --name codex-work --detach --keep --exec 'sleep infinity'
oaiso connect codex-work
  1. Start Codex inside the guest shell:
codex

  1. Quit Codex, then use exit in the guest shell to return to the host. Closing the connection leaves the worker running.

  2. Stop and reconnect to the same worker from the host:

oaiso stop codex-work
oaiso connect --start codex-work
  1. Resume inside the guest shell:
codex resume --last

If Codex asks you to trust the folder, review the target before confirming. To select non-interactive history created by codex exec, the pinned Codex version requires codex resume --last --include-non-interactive.

When finished, leave the guest shell and remove the worker from the host. This also removes its HOME and private database disk.

oaiso stop codex-work
oaiso rm codex-work

docs.title: Capacity and configuration
docs.text:
Setting Meaning Default or auto Reserve 512MiB for each new regular Kata worker --agent-state-size 1GiB Capacity at creation; integer sizes from 64MiB through 8GiB --agent-state-size off Disable when managing SQLite storage yourself [run].agent_state_size Host default; an explicit CLI flag wins Go/local API LaunchRequest.AgentStateSize Same values; an existing empty value preserves default behavior

Regular user's host configuration:

[run]
agent_state_size = "1GiB"

Capacity is fixed at creation. Existing disks are not automatically resized or reformatted. Numeric capacities such as 64MiB cannot be combined with temporary HOME or runc.

  • The default database directory is /var/lib/oaiso-agent-state/codex. An image's explicit CODEX_SQLITE_HOME is preserved.
  • Explicit Codex sqlite_home configuration takes precedence over the environment variable, following OpenAI Docs. Explicit FUSE-backed paths retain their mmap limitation.
  • Only the owning guest UID can access the mount. Host space is reserved at creation. This feature does not add storage encryption.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
Condition Next action Host space reservation fails Check host df -h and oaiso ps -a; remove only your unneeded workers or choose a smaller capacity for a new worker Guest database disk full Remove your unneeded files, handle SQLite's failure and retry; databases are never automatically deleted Missing/replaced disk or changed permissions Startup refuses and retains data for operator investigation; no automatic empty replacement Conflicting runtime metadata or cleanup failure Cleanup information is retained; inspect contents and ownership before retrying Additional mount overlaps the database path Choose a target that does not overlap /var/lib/oaiso-agent-state, or use --agent-state-size off when managing database storage yourself Old node/bootstrap Update and verify the matching components, then create a new worker

Conditions and unverified cases are recorded in testing (Japanese).

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Prerequisites: prepare the host, credentials and worker image.
  • Working directory: the project you want the agent to use.

docs.title: Supported agents
docs.text: Agent API key Subscription Details Codex CLI OpenAI API key ChatGPT OAuth Authentication, launch options Claude Code Anthropic API key Claude OAuth or setup-token Claude Code Other agents Not supported Not supported Future work

docs.title: Choose a launch method
docs.text:
Goal Codex Claude Code Forward native CLI arguments oaiso codex oaiso claude Set image, worktree or mount options oaiso run --agent codex oaiso run --agent claude Set the default for oaiso run oaiso default codex oaiso default claude
  • Arguments after oaiso codex or oaiso claude go to the agent CLI.
  • Set Oaiso launch flags through oaiso run --agent ....
  • For direct launch, choose the independent profile in trusted global configuration.
  • The built-in oaiso run default is an authenticated shell.
  • Project-only defaults: use oaiso default codex --local, for example.

docs.title: Authentication, network and approval boundaries
docs.text: Item Behavior Real credentials Stay in the host Auth Proxy; never passed to work VMs Worker AI traffic Short-lived placeholders authorize fixed AI routes General traffic Denied by default; allow required destinations (Japanese) CLI model selection Selects a model; authorization also requires proxy model limits Agent approvals Configured with the run options; separate from Kata isolation

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• File sharing and worktrees (Japanese).
  • List, inspect logs, stop and restart workers (Japanese).
  • Update the CLI and images (Japanese).
  • Run agents through the Go API.

docs.title: Recover an artifact bundle
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4.
  • Run on the host against a running worker whose workspace is a Git repository with HEAD and accessible Git metadata.
  • Select explicit regular workspace files. Export their contents, their Git diff against HEAD, and a manifest containing worker/image/runtime IDs, HEAD, sizes and SHA-256 hashes. Add --job JOB_ID to include selected job IDs, running state and exit codes.
Limit Value Selection 1–256 files, up to 32 job IDs; selection metadata up to 64 KiB; untracked files may be selected Combined file and patch data Up to 32 MiB Relative path Up to 94 UTF-8 bytes; no symlinks or directory recursion Exclusions Known credential paths including .git, .ssh, .aws, .codex, .claude, .env*, credential JSON and private-key extensions Host output bounds Enforce 1 MiB for a plan and the selected capacity plus 1 MiB for tar output, independently of the guest Not exported Environment variables, authentication files at known excluded paths, or execution logs
  • Exclusions do not detect secrets embedded in arbitrary selected files. Review the content yourself.
  • Git external diff and textconv are disabled. Shared-workspace host changes are included.

docs.title: Review the files
docs.text:
Example: recover src/main.go and result.json from dev-worker.

oaiso artifact plan dev-worker \
  --include src/main.go \
  --include result.json
  • Check files, patch_bytes, total_bytes, and the plan id.
  • Copy the reviewed ID at the following prompt.
read -r -p 'Artifact plan ID: ' artifact_plan_id

docs.title: Export the reviewed contents
docs.text:
oaiso artifact bundle dev-worker \
  --include src/main.go \
  --include result.json \
  --plan-id "$artifact_plan_id" \
  --output ./dev-worker-artifacts.tar
tar -tf ./dev-worker-artifacts.tar

manifest.json
changes.patch
files/result.json
files/src/main.go
  • Use the same --job JOB_ID selections when planning and exporting. Logs, arguments and environment values are excluded; an exit code is not final while running: true.
  • Creates a new 0600 file; never overwrites an existing output.
  • Refuses changed contents or a changed patch. Review another plan before retrying.
  • Removes incomplete output on failure. Does not extract or commit automatically.
  • Recover before deleting the worker/worktree.
Go operation Method Plan client.PlanArtifacts(ctx, workerID, cxd.ArtifactOptions{Paths: paths}) Export client.ExportArtifacts(ctx, workerID, options, writer); set ExpectedPlan

Use SDK file operations for individual Python/TypeScript transfers. Bundles use CLI/Go.

  • Go writers may contain partial output after an error. Receive into a temporary file and accept it only after success.

docs.title: Save operation audit records
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4.
  • Records contain hashed subject IDs, fixed reason/operation codes, intent and success/failure. No credentials, placeholders, keys, bodies, URLs or arbitrary error messages.
Component Recorded operations Directory Node VM create/start/stop/delete, checkpoint create/delete Node state directory, audit/ Managed auth proxy Issue, policy issue, restore, revoke, policy denial usage-state-dir/audit/ Independent profiles Create, OAuth refresh, encryption migration, key method changes Profile root, audit/ Embedded auth proxy Proxy operations above Config.AuditDirectory, otherwise UsageStateDir/audit/; no persistence when both are empty

proxy serve --audit-dir /absolute/path explicitly selects a directory. Case proxies persist under CaseProxyOptions.UsageStateDir/audit/; OAuth refreshes through custom Stores are also recorded at the proxy boundary. Never share audit storage with workers. Hashing predictable IDs does not guarantee anonymity. Arbitrary guest commands and upstream processing are outside this audit's scope. Reasons are fixed codes such as completed, failed, canceled, storage_full and network denial codes. An error outcome is a failure response, not a guarantee of no state change.

docs.title: Verify and export
docs.text:
Run as the directory owner (administrator for node state). Replace the path with the actual audit directory.

oaiso audit --directory /absolute/path/audit > audit.json
  • Exit 0: sequence, hash chain and independently saved head agree; no pending intents.
  • Pending operations: JSON is emitted, then the command fails. Reconcile actual resource state before retrying.
  • Missing, partial or mismatched records fail validation; no automatic repair.
Condition Behavior Permissions Owner-private 0700 directory, 0600 regular files; symbolic/hard links rejected Capacity 16 MiB per journal; no automatic deletion. Go Journal accepts 1 KiB–64 MiB Full disk/capacity or broken evidence Refuse new create/start, token issue/restore and credential changes Stop/revoke/delete Proceed even when evidence cannot be saved; report audit failure in service logs Result persistence fails The operation may have completed. Node returns 503; credential operations return an error. Inspect before retrying Token issue result fails Revoke the newly issued token and return an error Process interruption An intent without a result is pending; a mismatched head blocks new authority Integrity Sequence/hash/head detect gaps and edits. Local owner/root can rewrite or roll back the entire journal

Stop the owning service before archiving the entire directory. Verify and retain the archive, then start with a new owner-private directory. Archives form separate recording periods; external retention and continuity are operator responsibilities. Local storage alone cannot guarantee root-resistant integrity or detect replacement with a previously valid complete journal.

docs.title: Authentication and profiles
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Prerequisite: complete installation.

  • Configure authentication on the trusted host, including a WSL or VM host.

  • For new v0.0.3+ installations, follow install → keyring → login → first startup. Login selects the profile and prepares the admin secret automatically.

  • The steps below cover manual registration with set/import; do not combine them with the login flow.

docs.title: 1. Choose credential separation
docs.text:
Mode Credential storage Use it for Independent profile (recommended for separation) Product directory with mode 0700; files with mode 0600 Separate product authentication from host CLI logins Legacy host integration Host credential files and authentication environment variables Reuse existing host authentication Embedding product Store Storage provided by the embedding application Manage per-case credentials through the Go API
  • Selected independent profiles never fall back to host authentication.
  • The manual set/import examples below use 0600 plaintext. New v0.0.3+ login profiles default to keyring plus age.
  • Keep credentials and profile selection out of project oaiso.toml files.

docs.title: 2. Choose the agent and authentication method
docs.text:
Agent API key Subscription Codex CLI Register an OpenAI key Import Codex OAuth credentials Claude Code Register an Anthropic key Import Claude OAuth credentials; see Claude setup-token

For an independent profile, run exactly one command below. All alternatives use the name work.

Authentication Command OpenAI API key oaiso auth profile set work --provider openai Anthropic API key oaiso auth profile set work --provider anthropic Codex OAuth oaiso auth profile import work --format codex --credentials-stdin < /private/login/auth.json Claude OAuth oaiso auth profile import work --format claude --credentials-stdin < /private/login/.credentials.json

Successful registration output

Operation Output Register API key Profile created (plaintext, 0600). Import OAuth Profile imported (plaintext, 0600).
  • API-key entry shows API key:; typed characters are hidden.

  • This confirms storage, not key validity or subscription access.

  • Replace /private/login/... with the actual JSON path from a prior official CLI login.

  • OAuth import separates the copied credentials from the host CLI's storage; later logins are not automatically synchronized.
  • auth profile set: hidden TTY input; keep real keys out of command arguments.
  • auth profile import: explicit stdin input; source files are not automatically discovered or deleted.
  • Legacy host integration: prepare credentials.

docs.title: 3. Configure admin authority and profile selection
docs.text:
1. Create the admin secret in a separate 0600 file.
  2. Select the profile globally.
  3. Set auth_profile to the created name, work. Replace /home/user/... with your actual absolute path.
  4. Check the selected authentication mode:
oaiso auth show

Output for a selected OpenAI API-key profile

Profile: work
Storage: plaintext (0600)
OpenAI: api-key
Anthropic: disabled
Registered credentials Expected line OpenAI API key OpenAI: api-key Codex OAuth OpenAI: oauth Anthropic API key Anthropic: api-key Claude OAuth Anthropic: oauth Provider without credentials disabled; cannot launch that provider
  • Expected in profile mode: Profile: work, and api-key or oauth for the selected provider.
  • Creating a profile does not select it. Before selection, auth show reports legacy OpenAI information.
  • For login through a dedicated Kata VM, see login and API connection checks.

docs.title: 4. Continue to the first worker
docs.text:
1. If needed, allow general network destinations.
  2. Return to image and proxy preparation.

  3. Prepare Codex for an OpenAI profile, or Claude for an Anthropic profile.

  4. init checks for a credential source; the first live agent request separately checks provider authentication.

docs.title: Refresh and switching
docs.text:
Operation Behavior Normal OAuth refresh CAS save to the same Store; retain the connection generation Re-login or account switch Import into a new profile, then replace the workers and proxy Credentials passed to workers Short-lived placeholders only; no real API key or access/refresh/ID token Login Kata, automated login and API connection checks Implemented in v0.0.3; live-account verification remains separate Local encryption and key backends age and keyring in v0.0.3+; external Vault integration uses an embedding Store
  • Storage, permissions and limitations: Security.
  • Flags and file paths: Authentication command reference.

docs.title: Configure credential-broker routes
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Inject credentials only into a fixed HTTPS origin and allowed paths/methods.
  • Workers call the broker using issued placeholders. Real credentials remain in the authentication proxy.
Feature Availability Fixed HTTPS origin, subtree paths and methods v0.0.2+ Templates, CLI and TUI helpers v0.0.4 Exact paths and CLI method selection v0.0.4

docs.title: Choose the scope
docs.text:
Input Allowed scope --exact-path /v1/read Only /v1/read; reject children and /v1/read-more --path /v1/read /v1/read and /v1/read/...; reject /v1/read-more Both Either path list may authorize the path No paths Reject saving/startup --method GET GET only; omission defaults to GET and HEAD --method POST POST only; CONNECT/TRACE cannot be configured
  • Repeat methods or use --method GET,HEAD. Repeat --exact-path for multiple exact endpoints.
  • Exact matching covers the URL path, excluding query/body content.
  • Reject ambiguous paths: alternate path encodings, dot segments, repeated/trailing slashes and control characters.
  • Do not follow redirects; reject WebSocket. Incoming Host and method-override headers are not forwarded.
  • If an origin accepts destinations or operations through query/body data, review that API's own authorization.

docs.title: Create an exact read endpoint
docs.text:
Run in Bash as the regular operator. Replace the example origin/path. Secrets stay out of terminal output, history and command arguments.

read -r -s -p 'Broker secret: ' broker_secret
printf '\n'
printf '%s' "$broker_secret" | oaiso broker set service \
  --template bearer-readonly --origin https://api.example.com \
  --exact-path /v1/read --method GET --secret-stdin
unset broker_secret
oaiso broker check

Example output with one route:

[{"name":"service","upstream":"https://api.example.com","paths":null,"exact_paths":["/v1/read"],"methods":["GET"],"header":"Authorization","prefix":"Bearer ","secret_set":true}]
  • Exit 0 and secret_set: true indicate successful local configuration checks.
  • paths: null means no subtree permission; only the exact path applies.
  • No DNS, connectivity, provider authentication or inference is tested.

docs.title: Allow descendants instead
docs.text:
Update the saved service to permit GET/HEAD on its subtree, preserving its secret:

oaiso broker set service --origin https://api.example.com --path /v1/read
oaiso broker check

docs.title: Create a separate POST-only endpoint
docs.text:
Enter its secret through stdin. Permit /v1/write only, excluding descendants:

read -r -s -p 'Broker secret: ' broker_secret
printf '\n'
printf '%s' "$broker_secret" | oaiso broker set service-write \
  --origin https://api.example.com --exact-path /v1/write \
  --method POST --secret-stdin
unset broker_secret
oaiso broker check

docs.title: Edit in the TUI
docs.text:
oaiso broker templates
oaiso broker configure
Field Meaning Template bearer-readonly uses Authorization; api-key-readonly uses X-Api-Key. Both start with GET/HEAD Path prefixes Permit a path and its descendants Exact paths Permit that path only Methods Specify only required methods New secret Blank preserves the saved value; saved secrets are never displayed
  1. Enter name, HTTPS origin and paths.
  2. Apply a template; adjust Methods if needed.

  3. Validate, enter the secret, then Save.

  4. Dashboard B opens the same form. broker configure also works without a running node.

  5. Load route loads the named route. Reload after a concurrent-edit rejection.

docs.title: Apply to the proxy
docs.text:
Drain workers and explicitly remove old proxies before creating them again. Saving alone does not update running rules.

oaiso proxy run --credential-routes "$HOME/.config/codex-dock/broker/routes.json"

Host configuration alternative, adding to the existing [proxy] section:

[proxy]
credential_routes = "/home/alice/.config/codex-dock/broker/routes.json"
  • Workers call /broker/service/v1/read on the authentication proxy with an issued placeholder Bearer token.
  • Existing Paths retain subtree behavior. To narrow a route, move it to ExactPaths and remove overlapping Paths.
  • Use CredentialRoute.ExactPaths in Go, ExactPaths in the stored JSON and exact_paths in broker check output.
  • --file PATH edits/checks another file; provide the same absolute path to the proxy.

docs.title: Storage and protection
docs.text:
Item Scope Default file ~/.config/codex-dock/broker/routes.json Editor permissions/limits Directory 0700, file 0600; at most 1 MiB/128 routes Secrets Plaintext in this private file, separate from agent age profiles Worker mounts Node rejects overlap with broker files; keep them outside workspaces Authentication/revocation Require a live issued token; revoke existing broker streams when it expires or is revoked Model-restricted tokens Reject broker routes because arbitrary APIs have no verifiable model schema Origin Trust the fixed upstream; it may echo received secrets in its response
  • Host root and the same UID are trusted.
  • Review CONNECT limits and bypass prevention (Japanese). General egress and fixed AI routes retain separate authorization.

docs.title: Disk checkpoints
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4; matching CLI/node/proxy required.
  • Saves a stopped Kata root filesystem for a new VM on the same node. No RAM, instruction pointer, live connection or stream resume.

docs.title: Saved and excluded state
docs.text:
State Contract Ordinary rootfs files Installed tools and data under paths such as /opt; deleted files remain absent Basic metadata Permissions, numeric UID/GID, modification times and symlinks retained; hard links materialized as independent files Masked read-denied paths Underlying files and hard-link aliases excluded even when original data remains on disk Workspace/additional shared mounts Contents excluded; explicitly supply new host directories at restore; host data is never rolled back Private Codex database disk Contents excluded; unreleased (main) state storage. Restored workers get an empty new disk /home, /root Contents excluded, including credentials, history, caches and user-local dependencies; only top-level home directory skeletons/ownership retained /run, /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev, /proc, /sys Contents excluded, including tmpfs, bootstrap files and kernel state /var/log, hosts/hostname/resolv.conf Excluded; necessary runtime settings are generated for the new VM Environment, argv, credentials, network rules, usage limits, jobs Not copied; configure a new execution Extended attributes, ACLs, file capabilities, special files Not retained; this is a filesystem archive, not a block-disk clone
  • Hard links to excluded regular files are also excluded. Guest symlink paths in exclusions also exclude their resolved in-root targets.
  • Add --exclude for application secrets. Mandatory exclusions cannot be removed.
  • Arbitrary user-written secrets cannot be identified automatically. Supply additional exclusions before saving.
  • Proxy API/OAuth credentials, stores and ledgers are outside worker disk. Proxies, login-only VMs and quarantined workers cannot be captured.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
As the regular operator after login/init, replace source-job with your retained worker:

  1. Flush/save application data and stop databases as required. The application owns multi-file consistency.
  2. Stop the worker; capture never automatically stops a running/paused VM.
  3. Create a checkpoint.
oaiso stop source-job
oaiso checkpoint create source-job --exclude /opt/app/private.env

Example output (selected fields, illustrative IDs/size):

{"format":"oaiso-disk-v1","id":"64-character checkpoint ID","image":"docker.io/library/oaiso-checkpoint:...","digest":"sha256:...","bytes":734003200,"entries":24000,"excluded":["/home","/workspace","..."]}
  • Retain id. Source worker remains intact; start/stop/remove are blocked for that worker during capture. Other workers remain manageable.
  • A confirmed stop does not prove application consistency after SIGKILL or forced shutdown.
  • Failure before publication never exposes a completed checkpoint. Publication/reply failure can leave an unknown outcome: inspect list before retrying.

docs.title: Inspect and restore
docs.text:
oaiso checkpoint list

In Bash, enter a saved ID when prompted. Replace /home/alice/new-project with an existing directory you own:

read -r -p 'Checkpoint ID: ' checkpoint_id
oaiso checkpoint inspect "$checkpoint_id"
oaiso run --checkpoint "$checkpoint_id" --name restored-job \
  --project /home/alice/new-project --detach --keep --exec 'sleep 300'
  • Original workspace contents are not transferred. Specify additional mounts, profile, model/network/usage policies for the new execution.
  • Agents/dependencies retain their saved on-disk versions; compatibility with newer agent/application releases needs separate validation.
  • Restore issues a fresh VM ID, network and proxy placeholder; normal host/guest verification gates execution.
  • Cannot combine with --image, positional image, --template or --environment-lock. Kata only.
  • Existing workers are never overwritten. Usage budgets are not restored/refunded; this is a separate execution.

docs.title: Capacity, removal and compatibility
docs.text:
Property Contract Per archive Default 4 GiB; create --max-bytes can narrow to 1 MiB–4 GiB; at most 500,000 entries Node catalog 16 GiB sum of published logical archive sizes, at most 1,024 checkpoints; one create/remove operation at a time Physical disk Not a filesystem-wide quota; original images, unpacked snapshots and temporary containerd content also need space Storage Local OCI image in the dedicated containerd namespace; no automatic registry upload Cancellation/failure Unpublished content becomes GC-eligible after lease release; physical space may not be reclaimed immediately Node restart Completed checkpoints persist; in-progress capture is not resumed Compatibility oaiso-disk-v1, Linux amd64, canonical entrypoint matching the current node; current Kata/guard/isolation checks apply Scope New VM on the same node; cross-node transfer, RAM snapshots and stream resume are not provided 
read -r -p 'Checkpoint ID: ' checkpoint_id
oaiso checkpoint rm "$checkpoint_id"
  • Removal refuses any retained worker referencing the image, even if stopped. Recover its output and remove that worker first.
  • Inspect/list after failures; use oaiso status and runtime-check for launch issues. Excluding required libraries or application configuration can prevent the application from working.
  • Host root/node operators are trusted. This is not encrypted backup or tamper-resistant archival storage.

docs.title: Go API
docs.text:
Operation API Capture client.Checkpoint(ctx, workerID, cxd.CheckpointOptions{Exclude: []string{"/opt/app/private.env"}}) List/inspect client.Checkpoints(ctx) / client.InspectCheckpoint(ctx, checkpointID) Restore client.RestoreCheckpoint(ctx, checkpointID, newLaunchRequest); new RequestID/workspace/identity Remove client.RemoveCheckpoint(ctx, checkpointID) Capability disk-checkpoint-v1 in client.Capabilities().Features
  • Unsupported old nodes fail explicitly.
  • Capture response loss means unknown outcome; reconcile source ID/creation time through the catalog before retrying.

docs.title: Retention planning and pins
docs.text:
• Available: v0.0.4.
  • The existing hard catalog capacity remains 16 GiB. --keep-bytes is a cleanup target, not a lower admission quota for future captures.
  • Counts logical tar bytes, not total host/containerd content or expanded snapshot usage.

Get an ID from oaiso checkpoint list:

read -r -p 'Checkpoint ID to protect: ' checkpoint_id

oaiso checkpoint pin "$checkpoint_id"
oaiso checkpoint inspect "$checkpoint_id"
  • pinned: true protects against retention cleanup.
  • Remove protection with oaiso checkpoint pin "$checkpoint_id" --unpin.
  • Explicit checkpoint rm ID remains available; pins protect automatic selection only.

Plan removal of checkpoints older than seven days and/or above an 8 GiB target:

oaiso checkpoint prune --max-age 168h --keep-bytes 8589934592
Field Meaning delete IDs selected oldest first protected Pinned or referenced by retained workers using the same image digest remaining_bytes Projected logical capacity after deletion target_met Whether the byte target can be met without deleting protected items id Reviewed retention-plan ID

Enter the reviewed ID:

read -r -p 'Checkpoint retention plan ID: ' retention_plan_id

oaiso checkpoint prune --max-age 168h --keep-bytes 8589934592 \
  --apply --plan-id "$retention_plan_id"
oaiso checkpoint list
  • No deletion without --apply. Periodic use requires an explicitly configured external scheduler.
  • Recompute the plan before deletion. New captures, pins, references or age-boundary changes invalidate a stale plan.
  • Partial failure may follow some deletions. Inspect the catalog and review a fresh plan before retrying.
  • Inspection failure aborts cleanup instead of treating resources as unused. Shared content is not broadly pruned.
  • Go: RetainCheckpoints(ctx, cxd.CheckpointRetentionOptions{...}), PinCheckpoint(ctx, id, true); apply using Apply: true and ExpectedPlan.

docs.title: Encrypt stored credentials
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available in v0.0.3 or later.
  • New login profiles use the keyring by default. Existing profiles and low-level auth profile set/import keep their existing behavior.
  • Supports API keys and subscription credentials. The Auth Proxy remains; work VMs receive no real credentials.

docs.title: Choose a backend
docs.text:
Backend Use case Requirements Passphrase WSL, Linux VMs, SSH and headless hosts A long passphrase, at least 12 bytes Keyring (new-login default) Desktop, SSH, WSL and VMs Secret Service, user D-Bus, secret-tool; setup and headless use
  • age is embedded: no additional age executable, service, database, Vault or container; storage/unlocking are local.
  • Use an existing desktop service or an explicitly opened private session; failure never switches backends. Keyring storage protection depends on its OS configuration.
  • Existing keyring unlock dialogs may appear. Unanswered operations fail after 15 seconds.
  • secret-tool manual; Ubuntu packages it as libsecret-tools.

docs.title: Create an encrypted login
docs.text:
oaiso login --agent codex --method subscription --profile work --encrypt
  • Enter and confirm a hidden passphrase.
  • Choose --method api-key for an API key; --agent claude for Claude Code.
  • Subscription login runs in temporary Kata; collected credentials are encrypted directly.
  • Existing profiles are never overwritten; choose a different name.

Use --keyring instead of --encrypt for an existing OS keyring:

oaiso login --agent claude --method api-key --profile claude-work --keyring

docs.title: Start, inspect and lock
docs.text:
oaiso init --agent codex
oaiso status
oaiso auth profile show work
oaiso auth profile lock work
Action Behavior Proxy startup/restart Unlock on host; transfer the data key through container stdin Additional tasks with a running proxy Check wrapped-key fingerprint and connection generation; reuse without another prompt status, profile show/list Show storage metadata without decryption status --check-connection Explicitly unlock and check API keys through models APIs; no inference profile lock Stop affected workers and authentication proxies; retain work and ciphertext
  • show reporting locked means that command has not decrypted credentials. Inspect the separate status proxy check for a running proxy.
  • Lock interrupts work; save results first.
  • Stopping the proxy or rebooting also discards its process-local key.
  • OS keyring locking does not erase an already-unlocked proxy key; use profile lock separately. That command does not lock the OS keyring itself.
  • Old proxy images need rebuilding; drain workers before recreating proxies.

docs.title: Migrate plaintext
docs.text:
1. Save work and stop affected workers.
  2. Stop the authentication proxy.
  3. Explicitly migrate:
oaiso auth profile encrypt work
  • Save ciphertext, read it back and verify before removing work.json.
  • Migration rotates connection generation; create new workers instead of reauthorizing old ones.
  • If interrupted with both records present, normal reads fail closed. Repeat the same command/passphrase to compare credentials and complete migration.
  • Different content is never silently removed.
  • Deleted disk blocks and old backups are not securely erased.

docs.title: Migrate the older encrypted format
docs.text:
oaiso auth profile show work
oaiso auth profile lock work
oaiso auth profile migrate-age work
oaiso init --agent codex
  • Format: legacy-v1 identifies the old format; new records show Format: age.
  • Save work first. Stop/remove old proxies, then migrate using the original passphrase or keyring.
  • Verify age persistence/read-back and rotate connection generation; create new workers.
  • Retain work.vault.v1-backup as 0600 ciphertext, never automatically loaded.
  • Retry the same command after interruption; a different backup is never overwritten.
  • Retrying an already migrated record verifies it without rotating generations again.
  • Keyring migration also retains the old keyring item for backup recovery; operators can remove retired items after verification.
  • New proxy startup/refresh on the old format is refused, without plaintext/host credential fallback.
  • Host setup --rollback does not downgrade credential formats. Prefer reauthentication when recovering an older version; do not resume old workers.

docs.title: Change a passphrase
docs.text:
oaiso auth profile lock work
oaiso auth profile passwd work
  • Unlock with the old passphrase, then enter/confirm the new one.
  • Remove stopped profile proxies, then protect the same age private identity/authentication key using the new passphrase.
  • Refuse changes while profile workers/proxies are running; unavailable for keyring-backed profiles.
  • Run oaiso init with the new passphrase to restart the proxy.

docs.title: Noninteractive unlocking
docs.text:
oaiso --passphrase-fd 3 init --agent codex 3< /private/runtime/passphrase-input
  • This demonstrates FD wiring. Supply a private secret source or temporary pipe, never a passphrase file in the project or alongside ciphertext.
  • Descriptor >= 3, maximum 4096 bytes, one trailing newline removed. Separate it from API-key stdin.
  • No passphrase arguments/environment variables.
  • For passwd, provide old input using --passphrase-fd and separate new input using --new-passphrase-fd.
