docs.title: Format and limits
docs.text:
Item Specification Storage ~/.config/codex-dock/profiles/NAME/NAME.vault; 0700 directories, 0600 files Container JSON manifest containing standard age ciphertext/protected-key data; the whole .vault is not direct age CLI input Cipher age v1.3.2 X25519 recipient; HMAC-SHA256 also prevents public-key-only substitution Key protection age scrypt, logN=17 (approximately 128 MiB), only when unlocking OS keyring age private identity/authentication-key bundle in existing Secret Service Secret location Unlocked host command/proxy memory; only placeholders in work VMs Main protection Reading inactive files, disks and backups Outside protection Host root/same-UID process access, live memory, swap and outer VM snapshots
  • WSL uses private Linux storage. Reject unverified DrvFS/NFS/FUSE filesystems. Kata separately requires KVM.
  • Lost passphrases/keyring keys cannot be recovered; reauthenticate into a new profile.
  • Local-only storage cannot fully detect rollback of a VM snapshot containing both keys and ciphertext.
  • Detailed specification, verification and remaining gaps.

docs.title: From installation to the first VM
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • This page covers v0.0.4 or later. Check oaiso --version first.
  • Requires Ubuntu 26.04, x86_64, systemd, KVM and cgroup v2. Requirements.

docs.title: 1. Install the prebuilt release
docs.text:
Run as a normal user, review the plan, then apply it. First prepare curl, CA certificates and GitHub CLI. GitHub CLI verifies release signatures.

curl -fsSL https://github.com/pacificbelt30/sandbox-oasis/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/pacificbelt30/sandbox-oasis/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --apply
  • No Go, Make or source checkout is required. The script prepares uv/Python.
  • Setup also installs missing D-Bus, GNOME Keyring and secret-tool dependencies.
  • To pin the release, use the v0.0.6 installation example.
  • For main source builds, see the toolchain guide and source installation.

docs.title: 2. Log in again and check the host
docs.text:
oaiso --version
id -nG
oaiso runtime-check
  • Log out/in first; group membership must include codex-dock.
  • Continue only when runtime checks pass with exit code 0.
  • Authentication and ordinary startup run without sudo.

docs.title: 3. Unlock the keyring
docs.text:
An unlocked desktop keyring can be used directly. For SSH, WSL or a headless VM:

oaiso auth keyring session
  • Enter the private passphrase twice on first use, once subsequently.
  • Run the remaining steps inside this shell and keep it open.
oaiso auth keyring check

Keyring: ready (store/read/delete verified; no provider request).

docs.title: 4. Log in to one agent
docs.text:
Agent and method Command Codex, API key oaiso login --agent codex --method api-key --profile work Codex, subscription oaiso login --agent codex --method subscription --profile work Claude Code, API key oaiso login --agent claude --method api-key --profile work Claude Code, subscription oaiso login --agent claude --method subscription --profile work
  • API keys use hidden input and a models-list authentication check; inference is separate.
  • Subscription login runs the official CLI inside temporary Kata.
  • Successful login encrypts storage, selects the profile and prepares the admin secret.
  • Do not additionally run manual auth profile set/import or admin-secret creation for this flow.
  • Existing profiles are never overwritten; choose another name when necessary.
Profile saved: work (encrypted, 0600).
Selected profile: work
Settings: /home/user/.config/codex-dock/config.toml

docs.title: 5. Prepare the image and proxy
docs.text:
Run only the matching agent:

For Codex

oaiso init --agent codex

For Claude Code

oaiso init --agent claude
  • An uncached first run downloads/builds the default worker image and needs network access and time.
  • Ready. means images and proxy are prepared; it does not confirm a live AI response.
  • Proxy-dependent environments also need BuildKit service and build network configuration.

docs.title: 6. Run in your project
docs.text:
cd /path/to/your-project
Agent Check startup in the VM (no inference) Normal use Codex oaiso codex --version oaiso codex Claude Code oaiso claude --version oaiso claude
  • The startup check ends with codex-cli 0.163.0 or 2.1.306 (Claude Code) and exit code 0.
  • Replace the example path. The current directory is shared with the VM.
  • General Git/npm/pip traffic is denied by default; allow required destinations.
  • Daily operations.

docs.title: What each check proves
docs.text:
Check Meaning runtime-check Execution infrastructure is ready keyring check Secret storage/read-back works Successful login Credentials and initial settings were saved init prints Ready. Image and proxy preparation succeeded codex/claude --version The pinned CLI started and exited inside the VM; inference remains untested Actual agent response The account/model can perform inference

Automated verification uses invalid credentials. Real login and inference depend on the account, plan, model permissions and network. See verification and remaining checks.

docs.title: Manage credential keys with a keyring
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available in v0.0.3 or later.
  • New oaiso login profiles use Secret Service by default. Existing profiles keep their storage backend.
  • API keys and OAuth tokens remain age-encrypted in .vault. The keyring holds the age private identity and authentication key.
  • Work VMs receive no keyring, D-Bus socket or real credentials.

docs.title: Choose a session
docs.text:
Environment Action Available desktop keyring Run oaiso login normally; an unlocked keyring needs no additional input SSH, WSL or headless VM Open oaiso auth keyring session Without a keyring Choose login --encrypt for a product passphrase Explicit plaintext Choose login --plaintext; 0700 directories and 0600 files
  • No GUI, TPM or USB key is required.
  • An unavailable keyring fails closed. A disposable store/read/delete probe runs before provider login or API-key collection.

docs.title: 1. Install dependencies
docs.text:
v0.0.3+ oaiso setup installs missing D-Bus, GNOME Keyring and secret-tool dependencies. Offline setup requires these packages in advance. Manual Ubuntu installation:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends dbus-daemon gnome-keyring libsecret-tools
Component Purpose and official documentation D-Bus User-process communication; official session runner GNOME Keyring Key storage/unlocking; project, daemon manual secret-tool Secret Service store/lookup/delete; official implementation

The full GNOME desktop is unnecessary; distribution packages can still pull GUI-related libraries.

docs.title: 2. Desktop use
docs.text:
oaiso auth keyring check
oaiso login --agent codex --method subscription --profile work
oaiso init --agent codex

Keyring: ready (store/read/delete verified; no provider request).
  • check uses a random disposable item; existing secrets are never displayed.
  • Without DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, Oaiso discovers the owned bus socket in the user's private 0700 runtime directory.
  • An existing PAM configuration may unlock the keyring at OS login. Oaiso never receives the OS password.
  • Oaiso does not edit PAM. Passwordless logins, including SSH public-key authentication, may need a separate unlock. PAM documentation.

docs.title: 3. Headless use
docs.text:
oaiso auth keyring session
  1. Enter and confirm a private passphrase on first use; enter it once subsequently.
  2. Oaiso starts private D-Bus and GNOME Keyring processes and unlocks storage.
  3. Use ordinary commands inside the opened shell:
oaiso auth keyring check
oaiso login --agent claude --method api-key --profile claude-work
oaiso init --agent claude
oaiso claude
exit
  • The 12–4096-byte passphrase is independent of the OS login password.
  • Encrypted storage lives at ~/.config/codex-dock/keyring/keyrings/, separate from the desktop keyring.
  • CLI processes in the session share the unlocked service.
  • Exiting stops the private keyring and D-Bus; encrypted storage remains.
  • Concurrent private sessions using the same storage are rejected.
  • An already-running Auth Proxy retains its own in-memory key. Run oaiso auth profile lock NAME before leaving if the proxy must also lock.
  • Later unlocking of these profiles must also run inside keyring session.

To run one command:

oaiso auth keyring session -- oaiso auth keyring check

Explicit noninteractive input uses global --passphrase-fd. Never store the passphrase in argv, environment or a plaintext file.

docs.title: Existing profiles
docs.text:
• Existing plaintext/passphrase profiles remain usable.
  • To change backend, log in to a new profile name with the intended keyring available.
  • No automatic keyring copying or conversion of existing passphrase profiles.
  • age format and profile locking, verification and limitations.

docs.title: Review and apply live egress changes
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4, for egress proxies created by a build containing this feature.
  • Run on the host with existing node-management permissions.
  • Updates affect the entire selected shared proxy. All its existing HTTP/CONNECT connections close.
Scope Behavior General HTTP/CONNECT Confirm termination of old connections before allowing connections under the new rules SSE / tunneled WebSocket Closed along with their underlying HTTP/CONNECT connections Fixed AI routes Unchanged; their auth/model controls remain independent Workers, jobs, previews Continue running; applications relying on closed connections may fail Private/metadata/DNS protections Remain mandatory Host configuration file Not rewritten Persistence Proxy-private 0600 file, restored after process restart; removed with the proxy

docs.title: 1. Draft a proposal
docs.text:
Example: propose an exact-host grant for api.example.com:443.

oaiso policy propose api.example.com:443 \
  --worker dev-worker --output ./policy-proposal.json
cat ./policy-proposal.json

Alternatively, use the latest retained denial:

oaiso policy propose --worker dev-worker --output ./policy-proposal.json
cat ./policy-proposal.json
  • Choose one alternative. The output file must be new.
  • Nothing is automatically approved or applied.
  • The generated proposal adds an exact hostname. It never removes denies, broadens shared port grants or adds IP grants.
  • Review/edit the complete Rules object manually for changes outside this narrow proposal operation.
  • Denial history belongs to the shared proxy, may include other workers, and does not authenticate a requesting worker.
  • DNS/address validation still happens at connection time; a proposal does not guarantee connectivity.

docs.title: 2. Review the change and its scope
docs.text:
oaiso policy plan --worker dev-worker --file ./policy-proposal.json
Field Review before Current rules, generation and readiness proposed Complete proposed rule set workers Workers currently sharing this proxy connections_closed The scope of connection termination id Change-plan ID
  • This is not a proof of policy widening/narrowing: overlapping domains, CIDRs and denies require review.
  • Approval belongs to the caller with node permissions; the plan ID checks the proposed content, scope and generation.
  • The worker list is an observation. The update is proxy-wide, including workers joining during application.

docs.title: 3. Apply the reviewed plan
docs.text:
Enter the plan ID from the previous output:

read -r -p 'Policy plan ID: ' policy_plan_id

oaiso policy apply --worker dev-worker \
  --file ./policy-proposal.json --plan-id "$policy_plan_id"
oaiso policy show --worker dev-worker --json
  • Already-sent data and work started upstream cannot be retracted.
  • Success means exit code 0, ready: true, and an increased generation.
  • Stale plans/generations are refused. Review again before applying.
  • Persistence/termination failures never report completion. A lost response may follow an actual change: inspect before retrying.
  • update_pending: true blocks new general traffic. To finish the same intent, use the original proposal file to review a fresh plan and apply it again. Other stale proposals remain refused.
  • Corrupt saved policy prevents startup instead of restoring older permissive launch arguments.

docs.title: Existing proxies and Go API
docs.text:
Item Behavior Older proxy Live updates refused; recover worker artifacts, then stop and recreate workers and proxy to enable control New worker allocation Refuse reuse when live rules differ from original launch rules; select a proxy for the desired policy Management path Existing node Exec → private 0600 Unix socket; no management TCP listener Audit Proxy-local permission_change intent/result records, without policy values or tokens Propose client.ProposePolicy(ctx, workerID, destination) Plan client.PlanPolicyChange(ctx, workerID, cxd.EgressPolicy{...}) Apply client.ApplyPolicyChange(ctx, workerID, policy, plan.ID)
  • Editing configuration alone does not update a running proxy.
  • Creation RequestID/options remain unchanged. Replaying creation does not reset a live policy change; inspect the actual policy instead.
  • Emergency worker-wide stop remains oaiso policy quarantine --worker dev-worker; quarantine cannot be undone or restarted.

docs.title: Allow general network traffic
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Traffic Default Fixed Codex/Claude AI routes Authorized by live placeholders, provider and model rules Git, npm, pip and arbitrary websites General egress; disconnected without a domain or CIDR grant Direct VM traffic, host and other workers Blocked

docs.title: 1. Configure host destination grants
docs.text:
• File: ~/.config/codex-dock/config.toml.
  • This example grants GitHub and npm. Add actual distribution and redirect destinations as needed.
  • Merge into the existing [proxy] table; retain admin_secret_file and other keys.
[proxy]
forward_default_deny = true
forward_allow_domains = ["github.com", "registry.npmjs.org"]
forward_allow_ports = [80, 443]
Setting Meaning github.com Domain and subdomains =api.github.com Exact hostname only Ports alone Do not grant destinations Domain and CIDR allowlists together Both must match; denials always win Private, loopback and metadata IPs Cannot be unblocked with a CIDR grant
  • GitHub asset downloads may use other domains not granted by this example.
  • SSH, JVM and custom CA behavior: compatibility settings.

docs.title: 2. Check before launch
docs.text:
oaiso policy check --json
oaiso policy explain registry.npmjs.org:443 --json

Output of the second command with the grants above

{
  "destination": {"Host": "registry.npmjs.org", "Port": 443},
  "allowed": true,
  "code": "address_not_checked",
  "stage": "destination",
  "addresses_checked": 0,
  "complete": false
}
  • Formatted for readability; the CLI emits one line.
  • allowed: true, complete: false: hostname and port passed; DNS IP checks have not run. This does not prove live connectivity.
  • A valid policy check returns exit code 0 and policy JSON with source: configuration for NEW workers; not a live update.

Also check a destination without a grant

oaiso policy explain example.com:443 --json

{
  "destination": {"Host": "example.com", "Port": 443},
  "allowed": false,
  "code": "domain_not_allowed",
  "stage": "destination",
  "addresses_checked": 0,
  "complete": true
}
  • Denial is expected here. explain itself succeeds; inspect allowed and code rather than the command's exit status for the policy decision.

  • Without destination grants: code: general_egress_disabled. Fixed AI routes are separate.

  • These inspect host settings for new workers; they do not change live traffic.

  • explain opens no connection; this example checks hostname and port only.
  • Add --resolve to check DNS result IPs; this still does not test live service connectivity.
  • Interactive editing: oaiso proxy configure, also available when the node is stopped.

docs.title: 3. Apply to new workers
docs.text:
Current state Action First setup Continue to init in the quick start Existing proxies/workers Save results, stop/remove workers, stop/remove affected proxies, run init with the new settings, create new workers
  • Saving settings does not update existing proxies, CONNECT tunnels or workers.
  • Procedure and names: proxy recreation (Japanese).
  • Per-worker --egress-allow-domain and presets narrow host grants; they cannot add destinations denied by the host.

docs.title: 4. Inspect or stop a worker
docs.text:
oaiso policy show --worker WORKER --json
oaiso policy events --worker WORKER --json
  • Replace WORKER with a name from oaiso ps -a.
  • Denial history is shared by workers on the same egress proxy; it is not an independent per-run audit log.
  • Immediate cutoff: oaiso policy quarantine --worker WORKER. Stops communication and all jobs, and forbids restarting that worker.
  • Retention, artifacts and failure handling: quarantine contract.
  • Detailed rules: network policy (Japanese).

docs.title: Save and export diagnostics
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4.
  • Local JSONL, without an external monitoring service or permanent collector.
Kind Retained fields Limits status Existing readiness check names/results No additional connection, release, decryption or inference check resources Host cgroup current/optional peak memory, guest/host limits, OOM kills Not guest RSS; unavailable data is unknown denial General-egress proxy reason codes Reads up to 1000 retained console lines; a shared proxy does not prove per-worker attribution launch Total/per-phase launch durations and outcome Excludes builds, foreground waiting and subsequent inference collection Unavailable denial history Collection failure is not zero denials
  • Excludes credentials, commands, URLs, destinations, workspace paths and free-form errors. Worker IDs are SHA-256 hashes, not a promise of complete anonymity.
  • Keeps current and previous files, default 1 MiB each. --max-bytes accepts 1 KiB–8 MiB per file. Older records are discarded.
  • Directory 0700, files 0600; rejects unsafe permissions, symlinks and multiple hard links. This is diagnostic history, not a root/same-UID-resistant audit log.

docs.title: Capture and export
docs.text:
On a prepared node, as the regular operator, replace my-worker with an existing worker:

oaiso observe capture --directory "$HOME/.local/state/oaiso/observations" --worker my-worker
oaiso observe export --directory "$HOME/.local/state/oaiso/observations"

Status only:

oaiso observe capture --directory "$HOME/.local/state/oaiso/observations"

Twelve samples, five seconds apart:

oaiso observe capture --directory "$HOME/.local/state/oaiso/observations" \
  --worker my-worker --samples 12 --interval 5s
  • Success prints Diagnostics saved .... Inspect JSONL kind and status.
  • Failed/unavailable checks still save available records, then return exit 1. Use oaiso status for recovery instructions.
  • Deduplication is bounded within one capture. Repeated captures, truncated proxy history and downtime are not an exactly-once delivery contract.
  • AI auth-proxy denials and request contents are not collected.

docs.title: Launch timing
docs.text:
oaiso run --name measured-job --detach --keep \
  --observe-dir "$HOME/.local/state/oaiso/observations" --exec 'sleep 300'
oaiso observe export --directory "$HOME/.local/state/oaiso/observations"
  • Storage failure warns without changing launch results, worker ownership or cleanup.
  • Go API: pass LaunchWithTimings results to cxd.SaveLaunchObservation(directory, worker.ID, timings, err != nil); read with cxd.ReadObservations(directory).
  • Not yet in public release bundles. See verification records.

docs.title: Preview a guest web application
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4.
  • Requires a running worker with an HTTP/WebSocket app reachable at guest 127.0.0.1.
  • Listens only on host 127.0.0.1; this is not public hosting.

Example: the app is already listening on guest port 3000.

oaiso preview dev-worker 3000 --lifetime 30m

Example output; port and token vary:

http://127.0.0.1:49152/__oaiso_login?token=...
  1. Open the URL in a browser on the execution host.
  2. Login sets a cookie and redirects to the app root.
  3. Press Ctrl-C in the CLI to close the preview.
Control Behavior Authentication Random per-preview token; HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie Lifetime Default 30 minutes, maximum one hour; closes connections on expiry/CLI exit Target Exactly one worker-loopback port, through verified Exec streams Host and Origin Reject values different from the issued loopback origin Capacity Eight concurrent requests, sixteen TCP connections, 8 MiB request bodies Worker stop/quarantine Refuse new requests; close existing connections after state checks every second Secrets Strip the preview cookie before forwarding to the guest; no provider credentials are injected Management sockets Never published
  • Keep the login URL private.
  • The browser executes JavaScript returned by the guest app. VM isolation does not isolate the browser.
  • This connection is separate from general egress and AI authentication. Changing egress policy alone does not close the preview.
  • Each connection starts a guest relay process; this is a development preview, not a high-throughput serving path.
preview, err := client.Preview(ctx, workerID, 3000, 30*time.Minute)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer preview.Close()
// Present preview.URL explicitly to the user; do not automatically log it.
<-preview.Done()
  • Applications with absolute URLs or custom Origin validation may need application configuration matching the preview URL.

docs.title: Connection, bandwidth, FD and I/O limits
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4, with matching CLI, node, guard and proxy.
  • Optional. Unset settings retain existing behavior.
  • Separate from CPU, memory, PIDs, request-body size and per-execution AI usage limits.

docs.title: Scope and behavior
docs.text:
Resource Scope At the ceiling TCP connections Per proxy and socket source IP Close new connections; retain existing HTTP/SSE/WS/CONNECT Bandwidth Combined directions per proxy/source IP, bytes/second Wait before delivery; initial 32 KiB burst; no new stream lifetime timeout File descriptors (FD) Each guest process, through an operator-defined profile Equal soft/hard RLIMIT_NOFILE; additional opens fail with EMFILE. Exec and child processes use the same ceiling Block I/O Host VM cgroup, per selected block device io.max delays reads/writes at BPS/IOPS ceilings
  • A separate admin listener is outside these limits. Legacy single-listener configurations share the same budget with admin connections.
  • Connection counts include idle and TLS sockets. HTTP/2 streams within one socket are not separate connections. Use existing --max-concurrent for AI request concurrency.
  • Bandwidth counts worker-facing socket bytes, including auth TLS handshakes/records and opaque CONNECT payloads. It excludes IP/TCP headers, retransmissions and the separate upstream hop.
  • Kernel socket buffers mean this is not an exact instantaneous NIC throughput cap.
  • Auth and general-egress proxies have independent budgets; they do not provide one combined VM bandwidth ceiling.
  • Existing --max-transfer-bytes limits cumulative AI/broker body bytes, terminating an over-budget stream. Bandwidth throttling limits bytes/second without a cumulative cap.
  • Token/certificate expiry, revocation, explicit maximum lifetimes/idle reaping and clients' own timeouts remain effective.

docs.title: Configure proxy connections and bandwidth
docs.text:
As the ordinary operator after independent login and initialization. Before changing existing proxies, finish and remove their workers, then explicitly recreate the proxies (Japanese).

oaiso proxy run --max-connections 512 --max-connections-per-source 32 \
  --network-bytes-per-second 1048576
CLI (proxy run / proxy serve) Host [proxy] key Values --max-connections max_connections 0 unlimited, 1–65536 --max-connections-per-source max_connections_per_source 0 unlimited, 1–65536; cannot exceed the nonzero global limit --network-bytes-per-second network_bytes_per_second 0 unlimited, 1024–1099511627776

Alternatively, edit the host's ~/.config/codex-dock/config.toml:

[proxy]
max_connections = 512
max_connections_per_source = 32
network_bytes_per_second = 1048576
  • Explicit flags win. Host settings also apply to automatic startup and policy-specific proxies; project oaiso.toml cannot supply them.
  • A mismatch with an existing proxy fails instead of silently retaining old limits. Editing configuration does not interrupt existing connections.
  • Sources use socket IPs, never forwarding headers. Managed Kata VMs use distinct addresses on individual networks.
  • NAT clients sharing an address share a budget. This is not authenticated execution-ID accounting; tokens and certificates still provide authorization.
  • Source bookkeeping holds at most 4096 entries. Reconnects do not reset unrefilled bandwidth buckets. Recreating the proxy resets bandwidth state; this is not a durable cumulative usage ledger.
  • Refusals happen at TCP admission, so an HTTP 429 is not guaranteed. Closed connections release their slots.

docs.title: Define an FD ceiling
docs.text:
As an ordinary operator in a scratch directory. If profiles already exist, append the generated element to their JSON array, preserving existing definitions.

oaiso profile define limited --base compact --pids-limit 512 --nofile 1024 \
  > resource-profiles.json
  • --nofile: 0 retains the runtime default, otherwise 128–1048576.
  • Generating JSON does not register it. Complete the operator registration below.
  • Startup and restart compare the OCI setting and trusted guard observations before user code and authentication are activated.
  • This is per guest process, not a VM-wide aggregate FD count or a limit on the host Kata runtime/proxy.

docs.title: Alternatively, include block I/O ceilings
docs.text:
The operator must identify the host device. Replace the example 8:0 with its actual MAJOR:MINOR. The io controller must be delegated down to the node's subtree; unavailable requested limits fail closed.

oaiso profile define limited-io --base compact --pids-limit 512 --nofile 1024 \
  --io-limit '8:0 rbps=67108864 wbps=8388608 riops=4096 wiops=1024' \
  > resource-profiles.json
Dimension Meaning rbps / wbps Read/write bytes per second; positive values up to 2^40 riops / wiops Read/write operations per second; positive values up to 2^30 Omitted / max Unlimited dimension; at least one finite dimension per device Repeat --io-limit Up to 16 devices; duplicate devices/keys and unknown keys fail
  • Only block I/O attributed to the host VM cgroup on the selected device is covered. Cached reads, tmpfs, other devices and work performed by separate services are outside that scope.
  • Device mapping, writeback and shared inode attribution affect results. Check io.stat and your real workload on the correct device.
  • The kernel permits temporary bursts. This is neither an exact one-second window nor a minimum bandwidth guarantee for other VMs.
  • Specifications: Linux cgroup v2 I/O controller, OCI process rlimits.

docs.title: Register and check the profile
docs.text:
1. Drain affected VMs/reservations, preserve existing definitions and install the JSON:
sudo install -d -o root -g root -m 0755 /etc/codex-dock
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0600 resource-profiles.json \
  /etc/codex-dock/resource-profiles.json
sudo systemctl cat codex-dock-node
sudo systemctl edit codex-dock-node
  1. In the editor, preserve the original ExecStart command/arguments and append the resource-profile flag. The empty assignment clears the previous command. Replace the placeholder with the command you inspected:
[Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=<original command you inspected> --resource-profiles /etc/codex-dock/resource-profiles.json
  1. After saving, reload and restart. Recheck overridden binary/manifest references after release upgrades:
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart codex-dock-node
for attempt in $(seq 1 60); do
  if oaiso profile --node --json; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
oaiso profile --node --json

For the FD-only example, as the ordinary operator in the project directory:

oaiso run --name limited-job --profile-size limited --detach --keep --exec 'sleep 600'
oaiso exec limited-job -- sh -c 'ulimit -Sn; ulimit -Hn'
oaiso vm inspect limited-job --json

For the I/O example instead:

oaiso run --name limited-job --profile-size limited-io --detach --keep --exec 'sleep 600'
oaiso exec limited-job -- sh -c 'ulimit -Sn; ulimit -Hn'
oaiso vm inspect limited-job --json
  • Both examples print 1024 twice for FD limits. In VM inspection, io.max is configuration and io.stat is an observation, not proof that all storage is covered.
  • Remove your VM afterwards with oaiso rm -f limited-job.
  • Drain reservations before modifying/removing definitions. Retained budgets cannot be reinterpreted. See operator-defined profiles.

docs.title: Go API
docs.text:
API Setting / observation Case auth proxy CaseProxyOptions.NetworkResources = cxd.ProxyResourceLimits{MaxConnections: 512, MaxConnectionsPerSource: 32, BytesPerSecond: 1048576} Managed general egress Options.EgressNetworkResources uses the same type; provide explicit destination rules in EgressPolicy Complete profile contract client.ResourcePolicies(ctx), including FileDescriptorLimit and BlockIO Running VM contract The returned ResourceUsage.Policy; check the method's error. Existing Profile retains its comparable CPU/memory/PID contract Launch selection Existing LaunchRequest.Profile
  • Verification and remaining limits (Japanese). These controls do not defend against local root or a trusted operator changing the configuration.

docs.title: Verify distribution signatures and provenance
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4 or later.
  • The installer and upgrade reject unsigned online releases.
Evidence Policy Signature GitHub OIDC/Sigstore, using official GitHub CLI trusted roots; never trust keys supplied by the artifact Built source All three executables must identify the current clean checkout commit in Go build metadata Publisher Exact pacificbelt30/sandbox-oasis/.github/workflows/release.yml and selected refs/tags/<version> Runner GitHub-hosted; reject self-hosted provenance Subjects Archive, installer, SHA256SUMS and SBOM Portable evidence provenance.json signature/certificate/transparency verification bundle Inventory CycloneDX 1.6, actual linked Go modules, Go standard library and pinned downloaded runtime assets Inventory exclusions Guest OCI image packages and host OS packages Rollback floor Root-owned release-floor.json retains the highest installed release

Checksums detect corruption; they do not replace signatures. CI obtains short-lived signing certificates, without a persistent publisher private key. Compromise of GitHub, Sigstore, workflows or dependencies remains outside this guarantee.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Official GitHub CLI for Linux, supporting gh attestation verify --bundle --source-ref --cert-identity. Needed for signed installation/upgrade, not ordinary VM use.
  • Existing installer prerequisites: Bash, curl, CA certificates and uv-managed Python. No Go/Make required for prebuilt installation.
  • Local evidence bundles avoid a GitHub login requirement. Trusted-root refresh may use the network.
  • Missing tools/evidence, altered signatures, unexpected signer/workflow/tag fail before placement.

docs.title: Verify the installer before executing it
docs.text:
Run as a normal user. This block verifies v0.0.6 and displays the installation plan.

export RELEASE_TAG=v0.0.6
bash <<'SH'
set -euo pipefail
: "${RELEASE_TAG:?Export the signed release tag first}"
oaiso_install_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$oaiso_install_dir"' EXIT
base="https://github.com/pacificbelt30/sandbox-oasis/releases/download/$RELEASE_TAG"
curl -fLsS --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' "$base/install.sh" -o "$oaiso_install_dir/install.sh"
curl -fLsS --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' "$base/provenance.json" -o "$oaiso_install_dir/provenance.json"
gh attestation verify "$oaiso_install_dir/install.sh" \
  --bundle "$oaiso_install_dir/provenance.json" \
  --repo pacificbelt30/sandbox-oasis \
  --source-ref "refs/tags/$RELEASE_TAG" \
  --cert-identity "https://github.com/pacificbelt30/sandbox-oasis/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/$RELEASE_TAG" \
  --cert-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --deny-self-hosted-runners --hostname github.com
bash "$oaiso_install_dir/install.sh" --version "$RELEASE_TAG"
SH

Success verifies the script and displays a plan. To apply, add --apply to the final installer invocation while retaining the verified tag. A plain curl | bash trusts the HTTPS bootstrap script before running it; the block above verifies that script first. oaiso upgrade also verifies the downloaded installer before execution.

Operation or failure Behavior Older release Reject before stopping services Deliberate older signed release Explicit --allow-downgrade on upgrade/installer/setup; keep the high-water mark Failed installation Existing automatic transactional recovery setup --rollback --apply Explicit recovery; retain the high-water mark Explicit --bundle PATH Trusted local source-built/offline bundle; no online distribution signature check Offline distribution transfer Verify signatures/hashes first and retain evidence; see official offline trust-root preparation Root replaces floor/verifier/trust roots Trusted operator action; local records cannot prevent it

A valid signature does not guarantee absence of vulnerabilities, reproducible builds or guest image safety. Main CI creates real test signatures and rejects altered artifacts/wrong workflows/wrong tags; those CI signatures cannot satisfy release admission policy.

See official attestations, verification CLI and test evidence.

docs.title: Per-execution usage limits
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4; use matching CLI, node and authentication proxy.
  • Both API and subscription authentication are enforced at the credential-holding proxy. No ledger/admin authority enters VMs.
  • Defaults preserve existing behavior. Unsupported proxies reject limited executions rather than omitting enforcement.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
CLI Control Precision and conditions --max-requests Accepted upstream requests Journaled before forwarding; upstream errors do not refund admissions. Includes model discovery, token-count metadata and broker requests --max-concurrent Concurrent requests Held until HTTP/SSE completion; 0 is unlimited, except observed-token budgets default to 1 --max-transfer-bytes Combined request/response body bytes Reserved before forwarding; headers excluded. Excess streams terminate --max-observed-tokens New-request cutoff based on observed token totals Stops subsequent AI requests once reached; not a prepaid or exact monetary cap
  • Zero fields are unlimited. Limits are immutable for the same execution.
  • Applies to AI/broker traffic through the auth proxy, not general HTTP/CONNECT egress.
  • The final inference and already-started concurrent requests can exceed the observed-token threshold. Revocation/disconnect cannot undo already-billed upstream work.
  • No monetary conversion, subscription balance or provider billing amount is fetched.
  • Limited executions reject WebSocket. Codex uses the existing HTTP/SSE configuration; Claude Code uses HTTP/SSE.
  • Token budgets support fixed AI routes. Model discovery/token-count metadata consume request and body-byte budgets, not inference-token totals.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Requires independent-profile oaiso login and oaiso init on a configured execution host. Run as an ordinary user.

  • Independent login also configures admin authority automatically.
  • Legacy proxies without an admin secret keep their unlimited behavior. To use limits, select an independent profile or configure proxy.admin_secret_file, drain workers and recreate the proxy.
oaiso run --name limited-job --detach --keep \
  --max-requests 100 --max-concurrent 2 \
  --max-transfer-bytes 10485760 --max-observed-tokens 50000 \
  --exec 'sleep 3600'
oaiso usage limited-job --json

Example before any requests:

{"policy":{"max_requests":100,"max_concurrent":2,"max_bytes":10485760,"max_tokens":50000},"requests":0,"active":0,"bytes":0,"tokens":0,"unmetered_requests":0,"indeterminate":false}
Result Meaning and next step HTTP 429 / usage_limit Request, concurrency, body-byte or observed-token cap. Concurrency-only denial can be retried after active work ends HTTP 503 / usage_state_unavailable Failed persistence or uncertain usage. Never automatically resets a budget unmetered_requests Requests without complete token-usage records; distinct from zero tokens indeterminate: true Interrupted work left an unknown remainder; further AI requests for this execution are denied
  • With a token budget, absent/truncated/unsupported usage also denies further AI requests.
  • Without a token budget, missing token usage does not disable request/concurrency/body limits.
  • Normal stop/restart and token reissue/restore preserve counters.
  • Recover artifacts and start a new worker name/execution ID to continue uncertain work. Do not delete the ledger to restore an existing execution.

docs.title: Go API and configuration
docs.text:
Surface Setting Go API LaunchRequest.UsagePolicy = &identity.UsagePolicy{MaxRequests: 100, MaxConcurrent: 2, MaxBytes: 10485760, MaxTokens: 50000} Query client.Usage(ctx, workerID); returns no credentials External Store proxy CaseProxyOptions.UsageStateDir: owner-private host directory outside workspaces Host config / oaiso.toml [run] max_requests, max_concurrent, max_transfer_bytes, max_observed_tokens Standalone proxy proxy serve --usage-state-dir PATH; requires a separate admin listener and admin secret
  • CLI-managed state: ~/.local/state/codex-dock/usage/<proxy-name-hash>/; directory 0700, files 0600.
  • Stores only hashed execution IDs, policies, counters and uncertainty flags. No API keys, OAuth or request contents.
  • One proxy exclusively owns a ledger. Invalid formats/permissions and symlinks fail closed.
  • The node rejects overlaps with worker workspaces/mounts, including creating a new ledger in an existing worker share.
  • Capacity: 10,000 executions / 8 MiB. Full/failed storage rejects new limited executions. Drain all executions, archive required records and use new execution IDs when reorganizing state.
  • Does not resist host root or the same UID altering state. Existing host trust assumptions remain.

docs.title: Encrypt worker-to-auth-proxy traffic
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Available: v0.0.4.
  • Enabled for auth proxies created by standard proxy run and Go EnsureCaseProxy.
Hop or credential Behavior Codex/Claude → guest relay HTTP on guest loopback 127.0.0.1:18083; never published outside the VM Guest relay → auth proxy TLS 1.3, client certificate bound to both the worker token and its current public key Real provider API/OAuth credentials Remain in the auth proxy Guest private key Disposable execution credential; never the proxy signing key AI HTTP/SSE/WS, token retrieval, OAuth refresh, broker Same encrypted hop and binding; existing model, scope, budget and revocation checks remain General egress proxy Existing HTTP proxy/CONNECT behavior; outside this TLS feature Host admin hop Existing separate management path; no new public management TLS service

Copied tokens alone, or combined with another execution's certificate, are rejected. Full guest compromise can still use that guest's authorized token and short-lived key. Host root, node operators and the same host UID remain trusted.

The verified bootstrap starts the loopback relay after verification/token activation, before releasing user code. Agent-specific mTLS configuration is unnecessary.

docs.title: Coverage by entrypoint
docs.text:
Entrypoint Worker-facing transport Auth proxy created by oaiso proxy run Automatically enables mTLS Go EnsureCaseProxy Automatically enables mTLS Direct oaiso proxy serve Explicit --worker-mtls, separate admin listener and protected admin secret required Custom in-process proxy Explicit WorkerMTLS configuration required Go StartCredentialBroker Current helper uses HTTP; do not use for VM paths requiring TLS
  • Configure fixed-origin broker routes through --credential-routes on the standard auth proxy to receive the same mTLS protection.
  • The legacy plaintext StartCredentialBroker path is not automatically converted to TLS.
  • Custom integrations should check ProxyCapabilities().WorkerMTLS and reject unsupported proxies when TLS is required.
  • Existing deployments are not automatically changed; align component versions and recreate them as below.

docs.title: Upgrade and use
docs.text:
Save work and drain/remove old workers/proxies before upgrading matching CLI/node/guard/proxy components. Existing environments are not automatically stopped or replaced.

On a host configured for the new CLI:

oaiso proxy run
oaiso run --name tls-example --detach --keep --no-internet --exec 'sleep 300'
oaiso stop tls-example
oaiso start tls-example
  • Admin secrets must be at least 32 bytes. When unset, managed proxies create ~/.config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret with mode 0600. Implicit reads apply only to the default local admin endpoint, never external endpoints. See authentication.
  • Worker/proxy TLS mode mismatch requires worker recreation; no HTTP fallback.
  • Direct proxy serve integrations select --worker-mtls with a separate admin listener and protected secret.
  • Specify the admin secret file explicitly for non-default admin URLs (oaiso run --proxy-admin-secret-file /absolute/path).
  • Check ProxyCapabilities().WorkerMTLS in Go. Custom legacy/in-process proxies are not changed without explicit configuration.
Lifecycle Behavior Token/client certificate At most 3600 seconds; longer TTLs rejected for new TLS workers Expiry/revoke/replacement Reject new requests and close active streams Worker stop/start Issue fresh key/certificate after verification; old key rejected Proxy restart New in-memory authority; old certificates untrusted. Stop/start workers to reauthenticate CA/server private keys Proxy memory only, generated per process Guest execution key Transferred over admin/exec stdin, saved 0600 at /run/codex-dock-control/transport.json on tmpfs; absent from argv, images and shares Checkpoint /run is excluded; restored workers get fresh execution credentials Invalid certificate/time skew/relay failure Refuse connection/startup; check node and guest clocks

Credentials are not automatically renewed indefinitely. Save work and stop/start before expiry for longer sessions. See security and test evidence.
